He gave Takeshi one last look, a hint of consideration crossing his usually mocking expression.

— Take care of yourself, little human, he added. You've survived more in two days than most souls do in a century. Keep it up.

Without waiting for an answer, he traced a gesture in the air, a dark rift opening before him, and disappeared, the tear closing immediately behind him.

Meanwhile, Agent 47 had already begun preparing his equipment, taking out a series of weapons from a hidden wall compartment and inspecting them with almost surgical method, every movement calculated, precise, without the slightest hesitation.

81, for his part, had turned to Isidora, his single eye fixed on her with renewed curiosity.

— Isidora, he said, how did you find me?

— Simple, she answered with a satisfied smile, we just asked a chair.

81 stayed silent for a moment, clearly not sure he had heard right.

— A chair, he repeated.

— A super-touchy omniscient chair, she clarified. But I'll give you the details later. First, we're going to go kill the ten jerks who locked you up.

A fierce smile stretched across 81's scarred face, his hands instinctively tightening on the hilts of his two massive swords.

— That, he said, is exactly what I wanted to hear.

Grand Patron Luigi suddenly stood up out of the jacuzzi, completely dry despite the water that had surrounded him a few seconds earlier, his suit impeccable as if it had never been wet. Takeshi blinked, unable to hide his surprise at this incongruous detail, almost trivial compared to everything he had already seen, and yet just as unsettling in its own way.

— Right, come on, you've freeloaded long enough, get lost, Grand Patron Luigi called out, gesturing toward the office door. Riper, get the earpieces ready so you can guide them.

— Copy that, Boss, the mechanical voice immediately rang out from the invisible speaker.

A small drawer opened in the wall, revealing four miniature earpieces, a matte black almost invisible to the eye, which Agent 47 methodically collected before handing one to each of them — Isidora, Takeshi, and a last one he fitted behind his own ear with almost mechanical precision.

— These earpieces connect you directly to Reaper, 47 explained in his ever perfectly neutral voice. Coordinates, tactical information, real-time communications. Do not lose them.

81, for his part, refused with a curt gesture the earpiece held out to him, a disdainful sneer twisting his scarred face.

— I don't need your gadgets, he said. I've waited millennia for this revenge. I'm not going to carry it out to the sound of a little voice in my ear.

47 barely raised an eyebrow, putting the earpiece away without insisting further.

— As you wish, he said simply.

Isidora, adjusting hers with obvious pleasure, turned to Grand Patron Luigi, a crooked smile on her lips.

— Welcoming as ever, you, she said. Thanks for the hospitality, Grand Patron. We'll cross paths again.

— I don't doubt it for a second, he answered with a wink, already sitting back down behind his desk, as if the entire scene had been just one more formality in his day. Go on, beat it now, I've got an empire to run.

The little group — 81, Agent 47, Isidora and Takeshi — finally left the office, heading deeper into the corridors of the Martian base, each of them aware that the real confrontation, the one against Rex Stella and the nine others who had sealed 81 away, was only just beginning.

A faint crackle sounded in Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice rising with mechanical precision.

— Location confirmed. Rex Stella and the four other Archdragons are currently in a parallel dimension classified as "Dragon Sanctuary." Coordinates transmitted to your navigation unit, Agent 47.

— Copy that, 47 answered, adjusting his weapon without the slightest change in his expression.

81 turned to him, a fierce smile stretching across his scarred face.

— So, he said, how do we get there?

— A ship is waiting for us on the surface, 47 answered. Estimated travel time: fourteen minutes.

— Fourteen minutes, 81 repeated with a dark little laugh. I've waited millennia. Fourteen more minutes is nothing.

Isidora, walking beside Takeshi, gave him a little nudge with her elbow, a mischievous smile hovering on her lips.

— Okay, last chance to change your mind, kid, she said. We're literally about to follow a god killer into a massacre of ancient dragons. Not exactly your classic family outing.

— After everything I've already been through today, Takeshi answered with a tired smile, I think I'm past the point where I can still back out.

They soon reached the surface, where a ship larger than the previous one was already waiting for them, its dark hull faintly gleaming under the reddish Martian sky. They climbed aboard, 81 bending double to get through the hatch, his massive shoulders brushing the walls of the cabin.

The ship took off almost immediately, shooting through the Martian atmosphere before tipping into a flight that had nothing conventional about it anymore — space itself seeming to fold around them as they crossed the impossible distances separating them from the Dragon Sanctuary.

— Final approach, Reaper's voice announced through 47's earpiece. Thirty seconds to landing.

81 straightened up, his two swords sliding out of their sheaths in one fluid gesture, a deep rumble escaping his chest — a mixture of rage held back for millennia and an almost animal impatience.

— Finally, he murmured, his single eye shining with a murderous gleam. Rex Stella. I'm coming.

The ship touched down in an almost unreal silence, its engines cutting out without a sound on an expanse of white stone, smooth and perfectly flat, stretching as far as the eye could see under a sky strangely devoid of any visible celestial body — no sun, no stars, only a diffuse brightness that seemed to come from the rock itself.

The hatch opened, and 81 was the first to step out, his swords already in hand, his single eye sweeping the horizon with predatory intensity. Isidora and Takeshi followed close behind, while Agent 47 brought up the rear, his weapon perfectly steady in his gloved hands.

They didn't have to wait long.

A massive silhouette stood out in the distance, its immense wings spread against the pale sky, a reptilian creature whose scales seemed to catch and reflect every invisible air current around it. It landed with surprising grace for its size, its claws scraping against the white stone, its reptilian gaze instantly locking onto 81.

— Rex Aira, Isidora murmured, a new tension in her voice.

The dragon stood motionless for a long moment, as if struck dumb, before a low, almost panicked rumble escaped its throat.

— You, it said, its hoarse voice echoing across the stone expanse, heavy with an ancient terror. It's impossible. You're supposed to be sealed. How—

— I had help, 81 cut in icily, his grip tightening on his swords. And now, Rex Aira, I can finally finish what we should have finished millennia ago.

The dragon took a step back, its wings instinctively spreading again, a glint of panic crossing its reptilian eyes as it understood, with chilling clarity, that the vengeance it had believed contained forever had finally caught up with it.

81 didn't even bother raising his swords. He charged straight in, at a speed impossible for such an imposing mass, crossing the space between himself and the dragon in a barely perceptible fraction of a second.

Rex Aira reacted instinctively, spreading its wings in a brutal movement, generating gusts so violent that the air itself seemed to tear around them, translucent cracks streaking through reality with every beat, the white stone of the ground cracking under the pressure of the supernatural wind.

Nothing stopped 81.

He went through the gusts as if they were nothing but a light breeze, his fist crashing into the dragon's flank with a dull, staggering thud that made the whole creature reel despite its titanic mass. Rex Aira let out a roar of pain, trying to recover, to generate an even more powerful gust — but 81 was already on it, a second blow landing on its jaw, then a third against its ribs, every impact echoing like a thunderclap across the silent expanse.

The dragon tried to retreat into the air, its wings beating frantically, but 81 literally leapt after it, grabbing hold of one of its legs before slamming it back down to the ground with a deafening crash, the white stone splitting under the impact into a spiderweb of crevasses.

— You can't— Rex Aira tried, its voice trembling, broken with pain, you can't already be this strong, it's impossible, you were sealed, you—

— I had all the time in the world to train, 81 cut in, his fist coming down again, without the slightest trace of pity in his voice.

Isidora, standing back with Takeshi and Agent 47, watched the scene with a mixture of fascination and obvious caution, instinctively taking another step back with every impact.

— Okay, she said softly, almost to herself. Okay, okay, okay. I'd forgotten how freaky it is to watch him fight for real.

Takeshi stood frozen, unable to tear his eyes away from the methodical massacre unfolding before him, a chilling certainty slowly settling in him that he had literally just freed something that even the most powerful entities in the universe had deemed necessary to lock away.

Isidora, a delighted smile lighting up her face, hurriedly pulled out her phone, the screen lighting up instantly — signal, at last, was back.

— Ah, finally! she exclaimed, raising the phone to film the scene. I thought I was going to die without being able to post this.

She carefully framed 81 methodically crushing Rex Aira against the cracked white stone, quickly tapping the screen to add a caption.

— "My buddy just got out of prison and he's already wrecking an ancient dragon, just another day," she murmured as she typed, a satisfied smile on her lips. #GodKiller #Comeback #Sanctuary

Takeshi, still frozen by the horror of the fight, turned his head toward her, incredulous.

— You're filming this for Instagram? Here, right now?

— Well, yeah, she answered without taking her eyes off the screen, adjusting the angle for a better shot. It's not every day you get to see a dragon massacre live. Gotta immortalize it.

A particularly violent roar rang out, Rex Aira making one last attempt to break free, unleashing a gust powerful enough to make Isidora stagger — who, without even panicking, simply steadied her phone with one hand while backing up with the other.

— Oh, gorgeous shot, that one, on top of it, she remarked, delighted, before turning her attention back to the fight. Go on, 81, one last hit for the camera!

81, without turning around, without even seeming aware he was being filmed, closed his massive hand around the dragon's neck, lifting it partly off the ground with a gesture of inhuman strength.

— You're going to pay, he said in a low voice, for every second I spent locked up.

Agent 47, who had stayed silent and perfectly still since the fight began, exchanged a neutral look with Takeshi, as if to underline, without a word, the quiet absurdity of the scene — an ancient cosmic massacre, filmed live for social media by a witch of the Void.

81 slowly raised a single finger, his massive nail extending toward Rex Aira's gargantuan eye, held immobile by the relentless grip crushing its throat. The dragon, unable to break free, let out a strangled cry, its reptilian pupil contracting in pure terror at this tiny, almost trivial gesture compared to the power already unleashed.

— No, no, wait, please— it tried, its voice breaking.

81 didn't wait.

With a single movement, hardly more than a flick, his nail pierced the dragon's massive eye, bursting it in a geyser of dark, viscous matter that spattered several meters around. An inhuman scream tore through the air, Rex Aira writhing violently in 81's grip, its wings beating frantically, yet unable to free it from that hold.

Isidora, phone still in hand, let out a delighted little shriek, instinctively zooming in on the scene.

— OH FUCK, she exclaimed, now that's a shot! People are gonna lose their minds!

Takeshi abruptly looked away, seized by a violent wave of nausea, one hand pressed against his mouth while the echo of the dragon's scream kept ringing across the white stone expanse.

— Is that... is that really necessary? he asked, his voice strangled, not daring to look again.

— You asked for his help against a cult, Agent 47 answered soberly, unfazed despite the carnage. This is part of the price.

81, still holding the dying dragon in one hand, finally turned his single eye toward the group, an icy satisfaction crossing his scarred face.

— One down, he said, his voice filled with absolute coldness. Nine to go.

Rex Aira lay on the ground, its massive body shaken by irregular spasms, its one remaining eye fixed on the empty sky, a trickle of dark blood slowly flowing from its empty socket. Isidora walked up without the slightest embarrassment, crouching near the dying dragon's head, her phone already raised to capture the moment.

— Smile for the camera, she said with a little laugh, taking several shots from different angles, completely indifferent to the hoarse moans still escaping the dragon's throat.

81 came over in turn, his heavy steps making the white stone ground vibrate slightly. He drew one of his two swords, the blade sliding out of its sheath with a metallic hiss, and without another word, drove it sharply into Rex Aira's throat.

The dragon arched violently one last time, a final hoarse breath escaping its half-open jaws, before falling back, completely still, onto the cracked stone.

81 pulled his blade out with a sharp jerk, the dragon's dark blood dripping along the metal, and put it straight back into its sheath without bothering to wipe it, a reddish trail marking its passage.

— That's one, he said simply, his single eye already sweeping the horizon in search of the next.

Isidora stood up, putting her phone away after one last satisfied look at her photos.

— Okay, she said, we've got the first one. Nine left, like you said. Where are we going now?

Agent 47, whose earpiece crackled slightly, turned his head toward the group, his voice still perfectly neutral despite the macabre scene around him.

— Reaper has located the four other Archdragons, he said. They are gathered in the same sanctuary, about two kilometers from here.

81 gave a fierce smile, his shoulders straightening, a new impatience running through his massive body.

— Perfect, he said. We keep going.

Isidora turned her phone back on, a delighted smile on her lips, and switched the app to live mode.

— Okay, people, she said, turning the camera on herself as she walked, we're continuing today's little dragon hunt. We just did one, there are four more around here, and I guarantee you this is big stuff.

She turned the camera back toward 81, who was walking ahead, his swords still dripping, completely indifferent to the lens aimed at him.

— Here's my buddy fresh out of prison, she announced with an almost touristy enthusiasm. Say hi, 81!

81 didn't answer, didn't even slow down, his single eye fixed straight ahead as if the phone, the camera and the millions of potential viewers simply didn't exist.

— He's shy, Isidora remarked, unfazed, then turning the lens toward Lucifer, who was walking with perfect nonchalance, apparently already completely used to this kind of situation.

— Hi everyone, he said in a monotone voice, giving the camera a vague wave before turning his attention elsewhere, as if it were the most mundane formality in the world.

Agent 47 didn't flinch in the slightest when the lens briefly settled on him, simply continuing to walk, his eyes scanning the horizon with total professional concentration, as if the camera were just one more element of the scenery to ignore.

Takeshi, on the other hand, froze completely when the phone turned toward him, his eyes going wide.

— Wait, what— no, turn that off, he said, hastily raising a hand in front of his face. You can't just... we're tracking down ancient dragons and you're doing a live for your followers?!

— Well, yeah, Isidora answered with disarming naturalness, still filming despite his protests. That's exactly what we're doing. Look, there are already twelve thousand people watching.

— This is completely insane, Takeshi muttered, finally turning away from the camera, a mixture of exasperation and total disbelief painted on his face.

— Shh, said Isidora, a mischievous smile on her lips, you're going to discourage my fans with that negative attitude. Come on, smile a little, it's not every day you get to witness the death of several legendary dragons live.

A faint crackle came through Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice rising with its usual mechanical precision.

— Updated information, it announced out loud for the group. Rex Stella is currently absent from the sanctuary. The four remaining Archdragons — Rex Ingenous, Rex Aqua, Rex Terra and Rex Stella — apologies, correction — Rex Ingenous, Rex Aqua and Rex Terra are therefore vulnerable and isolated, without the support of their king.

— And their chances of survival, if all three face 81 at once? asked Agent 47, his voice still perfectly neutral.

— Calculating, Reaper answered. Combined probability of survival: 0.38752637%.

Isidora, still live, let out a delighted burst of laughter, immediately turning her phone toward herself.

— Did you hear that, people? Zero point thirty-eight percent! Even three against one, they've got practically no chance!

81, still walking ahead without turning around, let out a satisfied, almost amused rumble.

— Good, he said simply. This'll go faster than expected.

Takeshi, still uncomfortable with the lightness with which everyone seemed to approach what was about to become a genuine massacre, cast a worried glance at Isidora.

— You're really calculating survival statistics in the middle of an Instagram live, he said, more as a resigned observation than a real question.

— Well, yeah, she answered with a radiant smile, my followers love numbers. It gives it a sporty feel, you know? Like match commentary.

Agent 47, unfazed, resumed his walk toward the sanctuary, his weapon still braced against his shoulder.

— Three hundred meters to visual contact, he announced simply, completely ignoring the ambient absurdity of the situation.

81 picked up the pace, a growing impatience showing through every one of his movements, both hands tightening on the hilts of his swords.

— Three more down, he murmured, almost to himself. Only seven after that.

They walked for another ten minutes or so across the white stone expanse, Isidora continuing to narrate the trip for her followers with unshakable enthusiasm, until the horizon finally opened onto a vast rocky clearing where three massive silhouettes stood motionless, their scales gleaming in the diffuse light of the sanctuary.

Rex Ingenous, its deep red scales glowing like embers, Rex Aqua, whose body seemed to ripple like liquid water despite its apparent solidity, and Rex Terra, massive and covered in a thick rocky crust, stood grouped together, their reptilian gazes trained on the little group approaching.

A heavy silence settled, the three dragons exchanging a look, a growing tension visible in their stiffened postures.

— Where is Rex Aira? Rex Terra finally asked, its deep voice echoing like a rumble of stone.

81 didn't answer right away, a fierce smile slowly stretching across his scarred face, his two swords still dripping with the previous dragon's blood.

Rex Aqua was the first to understand, its liquid body freezing instantly, an expression of horror crossing its reptilian features.

— No, it murmured. It's not possible. He's supposed to be sealed.

— He was, said 81, his voice heavy with deadly coldness. He isn't anymore.

Rex Ingenous took a step back, its glowing scales intensifying under the visible effect of panic, a budding fire already crackling around its claws.

— Rex Aira, it said slowly, finally understanding. You killed him.

— Yup, 81 confirmed with obvious pleasure. And you're next on my list.

Isidora, still live, zoomed in with relish on the three visibly terrified dragons.

— Oh, this is getting dramatic, people, she commented cheerfully. Look at those faces, it's like they've just seen a ghost.

Rex Terra, regaining a semblance of composure, took a heavy step forward, the stone cracking under its massive claws, its gaze determined despite the obvious fear still in its posture.

— There are three of us, it said, its voice trying to regain some confidence. Even you can't beat all of us at once.

81 cracked his neck with a nonchalant gesture, his two swords slowly rising, his smile widening even further.

— We'll see about that, he said simply, before lunging forward.

Agent 47, standing back at a perfectly calculated distance, raised his voice, his tone as neutral as ever despite the gravity of the announcement.

— Reaper has just recalculated your chances of survival, he said, addressing the three dragons directly. Zero point thirty-eight percent. Combined.

Rex Terra let out a contemptuous rumble, its claws digging a little further into the rock.

— You really think we're going to swallow a number pulled out of nowhere, human? it spat.

— It is not pulled out of nowhere, 47 answered without the slightest trace of emotion. It is a calculation based on verified combat data.

Rex Aqua shook its head, its body rippling nervously, a mixture of defiance and terror showing in its posture.

— We're three ancient Archdragons, it said, trying to convince itself as much as the others. We have a chance.

81, for his part, stayed silent in the face of their protests, an absolute calm settling on his scarred face as he slowly sheathed one of his two swords, keeping only the second in his right hand. He took up a low stance, his legs slightly bent, his single eye narrowing to a focused slit, every muscle in his massive body tensing in a taut, almost feline stillness.

— Only one sword? Rex Ingenous repeated, a hint of disbelief breaking through its fear.

— You don't deserve both, 81 answered in a low voice, almost a whisper, charged with an icy confidence that had nothing boastful about it — only a cold certainty, born of a billion years of massacres.

Isidora, still live, almost whispered to her camera, as if not to break the tension of the moment.

— People, she said, I think we're getting close to the moment when everything tips over. Look at him. He's not even worried.

The three Archdragons exchanged one last look, a silent decision forming between them, before deploying simultaneously — Rex Ingenous rising into the air in a roar of flames, Rex Aqua partially liquefying into a rippling, menacing mass, and Rex Terra charging straight ahead, the stone cracking under each of its steps.

81 didn't move a centimeter, waiting, his fierce smile slowly widening as the three creatures bore down on him.

— Finally, he murmured.

The three dragons combined their attacks in a simultaneous onslaught — the roaring flames of Rex Ingenous, the corrosive liquid mass of Rex Aqua, and a telluric shockwave unleashed by Rex Terra, all converging in a destructive torrent toward 81, enough in theory to level an entire mountain.

81 simply raised his sword, a single, almost lazy movement, and the combined attack smashed against the blade in a blinding flash, the energy dispersing in a brutal blast that kicked up clouds of white dust all around him — but he himself remained perfectly still, his foot sunk barely a few centimeters into the rock by the mere pressure of the impact.

A stunned silence followed, the three dragons frozen, unable to understand how their combined assault had just been neutralized with a single gesture.

Isidora, still live, burst out laughing, her phone shaking slightly with her hilarity.

— They tried to give him a facial, she said between bursts of laughter. Guess it's a bit limp today.

81 slowly lowered his sword, the dust settling around him, revealing his scarred face, still without the slightest trace of effort.

— That's it? he asked, obvious disappointment in his voice. I've seen baby gods hit harder than that.

Rex Terra, visibly trembling, took a step back, terror definitively winning out over any attempt at bravery.

— That... that's not possible, it stammered. No one can block a combined attack of the three elements like that.

— Apparently someone can, 81 answered with an icy smile, returning to his fighting stance, his sword slowly rising. Right. My turn now.

81 moved with a speed that defied all logic for a creature his size, his sword tracing a perfect arc through the air. The blade cleanly severed Rex Terra's throat, its massive head rolling to the ground with a dull crash before its body even had time to collapse. In the same fluid movement, 81 spun around, his sword cutting Rex Aqua down mid-charge, its liquid form freezing instantly before crumbling into an inert mass, unable to re-form.

Two bodies already lay on the ground, leaving only Rex Ingenous, backing away hastily, its glowing scales trembling with undisguised terror.

— You won't force me to use black magic, 81, it spat, its voice wavering despite the defiance it tried to put into it. Never.

81 stopped, his dripping sword pointed carelessly at the ground, a nasty smile stretching across his face.

— Then die, he shot back, taking a slow, almost theatrical step forward. And we'll see if your pride saves you.

He lunged forward, his sword coming down on Rex Ingenous — but the dragon, in a desperate move, dodged by a hair, its scales flaring with a darker, almost sickly light, a black aura beginning to creep along its massive body.

— No choice, Rex Ingenous murmured, its voice distorting, deeper, hoarser, as the black energy intensified around it, gradually devouring the natural red glow of its scales.

Isidora, still live, leaned forward, her excitement palpable through the screen.

— Ooh la la, people, this smells like a plot twist, she commented. He's bringing out the big guns.

81, far from worried, let out a deep laugh, visibly savoring this sudden change in the fight.

— Finally, he said, a little resistance. Show me what you've got, Soul Dragon.

Rex Ingenous stretched a trembling claw toward 81, the black aura crackling around it in a final outburst.

— Cardiac Attack! it cried, its voice distorted by the effort and the black magic pulsing through its body.

81 suddenly staggered, a rumble of pain escaping him as he slowly sank to his knees, one hand pressed against his chest.

— This curse destroys the target's heart, Rex Ingenous explained, a triumphant smile twisting its reptilian features despite the visible exhaustion overtaking it. You never stood a chance.

A heavy silence settled, Isidora holding her breath, her camera still trained on the scene, while Takeshi, horrified, took a step forward.

But 81 got back up.

Slowly, his fierce smile returning to his face, an amused glint crossing his single eye.

— You've mastered that spell well, he said, his voice regaining all its strength. But you're forgetting one detail. The number of gods I've absorbed over time means I've been able to modify my own body. Right now, you've just destroyed one heart out of the six hundred and twenty-one I've got in my body.

Rex Ingenous stood frozen, horror slowly spreading across its face as 81 went on, his smile widening even further.

— And you're far too exhausted to cast another one, he concluded. So, conclusion: you lost.

Isidora burst out laughing, barely able to keep her phone steady.

— He got fucking owned! she yelled for her live, tears in her eyes. People, did you see that?! SIX HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE HEARTS! This guy isn't even human, like literally!

Rex Ingenous backed away, desperately trying to gather enough energy for one last attack, but its body was already shaking violently, the strain of its spell having visibly consumed what little strength it had left.

81 walked toward it at a leisurely pace, his sword slowly rising, his scarred face no longer betraying the slightest trace of the pain he had just endured.

— Right, he said, let's finish this.

Rex Ingenous, in one last desperate burst, unleashed a wave of concentrated flames, all its remaining energy channeled into this single attack — but 81 stayed perfectly still, the flames dissipating against his skin without leaving the slightest mark, as if they had never existed.

— That's it? asked 81, almost disappointed, his hand slowly closing around the hilt of his second sword and drawing it from its sheath with a metallic hiss.

Rex Ingenous backed away, its legs trembling beneath it, terror having definitively replaced every trace of defiance in its reptilian eyes.

— Wrath of Eternity, 81 murmured, his two blades slowly rising on either side of his body, a dark and ancient aura coiling around the steel.

He lunged forward, a lightning speed propelling his massive body across the space between him and the dragon, and in a crossing motion of surgical precision, his two swords sliced clean through Rex Ingenous, a perfect "X" appearing for a fraction of a second before the dragon's body literally split in two, each half collapsing on either side in an almost anticlimactic silence after the violence of the fight.

Total silence fell over the clearing again, only the wind now sweeping the white stone littered with the remains of the three Archdragons.

81 stood still for a moment, his two dripping swords hanging along his arms, his single eye fixed on the lifeless bodies around him, a cold and absolute satisfaction written on his scarred face.

— Four down, he said finally, his voice echoing in the restored silence. Only six left.

Isidora, still live, stayed speechless for a moment — a feat in itself — before going on, her voice tinged with a sincere respect mixed with her usual enthusiasm.

— People, she said, I think we just witnessed one of the freakiest things in my entire long existence. And believe me, I've seen some freaky things.

Takeshi, still in shock from the carnage that had just unfolded before his eyes, stayed silent, his gaze slowly moving from the mangled bodies to 81, who was already calmly sheathing his two swords as if nothing had happened.

— How many are left again? he finally asked, his voice flat.

— Six, Agent 47 answered without the slightest emotion. Rex Stella, and five humans involved in the original sealing.

A faint crackle ran through Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice immediately correcting the information.

— Correction, it announced. The rest of those involved in his sealing are not all human.

47 nodded slightly, adjusting his information without the slightest apparent concern.

— Clarification requested, he said simply.

— The ten entities that took part in sealing 81 were: the five Archdragons, four of whom have just been eliminated — Rex Stella remaining. Justice Man, the Incarnation of Justice. Aravos, the Star of Decline. Shadow, formerly Jesus Christ, now an entity bound to the Void. And the Incarnation of Death, vanished from every known reality since the event.

81, who was calmly wiping one of his blades against his forearm, stopped dead at the list, a bitter sneer twisting his scarred face.

— Aravos, he repeated, a dark gleam crossing his single eye. That one, I'm going to take very special pleasure in tracking down.

Isidora, lowering her phone for the first time since the fight began, frowned.

— Wait, she said, isn't Aravos the unkillable guy who appears and disappears whenever he feels like it? Like, literally nobody can find him if he doesn't want to be found?

— Exactly, 81 confirmed, finally sheathing his second sword. Which is going to make things a little more interesting.

Takeshi, trying to keep up despite the accumulated exhaustion and horror, raised a hesitant hand.

— And the Incarnation of Death, he said, is she really impossible to find? Like, completely?

— Vanished from every text and every known reality, Agent 47 answered. No data available on her current location, or even on her continued existence.

81 shrugged, an icy smile returning to his face.

— Too bad for her, he said. If she ever reappears, she'll get her punishment like the others. In the meantime, we've got Rex Stella to find. And him, unlike the others, I know exactly where to find.

A rumble suddenly tore through the sky, a resonance so deep it seemed to vibrate directly in the bones of every member of the group. In the distance, the few points of light visible through the sanctuary's atmosphere began to tremble, then to move, torn from their positions by a gravitational force of inconceivable power.

Then the sky literally opened, an explosion of blinding intensity tearing through space like a supernova being born, a torrent of white and golden light swallowing the entire horizon.

From that tear emerged a mass whose scale defied all understanding — a dragon whose head alone could have swallowed entire planets, its body stretching over a distance the human eye couldn't even properly grasp, each scale sparkling like a constellation in its own right.

Rex Stella.

Isidora, her phone still in hand, stood open-mouthed, the camera shaking violently as she tried to capture the inconceivable scale of the creature that had just appeared.

— People, she said, her voice for the first time stripped of all nonchalance, I... I think I'm out of words. Look at the size of that. It's bigger than several supermassive black holes put together.

Takeshi, his head thrown back, tried in vain to fit the whole creature into his field of vision, a dull dizziness seizing him before this scale that went beyond anything he had imagined possible.

— That's... that's not even a dragon anymore at this point, he murmured. It's a fucking cosmic phenomenon.

81, the only one among them who didn't seem impressed, slowly raised his head toward the immensity that had just materialized above them, his single eye shining with a gleam that mixed ancient hatred and cold anticipation.

— Rex Stella, he said, his voice echoing with an almost frightening calm in the face of what stood before him. The King of Dragons himself.

Agent 47, unfazed even before this cosmic manifestation, raised his head in turn, his earpiece crackling as Reaper visibly tried, without much success, to calculate probabilities against an entity of that scale.

— Reaper reports a calculation error, he announced flatly. The probability of survival cannot be established. The data exceeds known parameters.

81 let out a deep laugh, both hands tightening on the hilts of his swords, his gaze never leaving the titanic immensity now hovering above them.

— Finally, he said, an opponent worthy of me.

Reaper resumed its calculation, its synthetic voice echoing through 47's earpiece, while the titanic mass of Rex Stella slowly approached, every movement of its immense body warping the surrounding space as if reality itself were struggling to contain such a scale.

— Calculation complete, Reaper announced. Probability of victory for 81: insufficient data for a reliable result. Uncertainty factor: maximum.

Rex Stella finally came to a halt, its presence literally crushing the entire horizon, its gaze — each of its eyes vaster than an entire city — settling with almost solemn slowness on the tiny figure of 81, standing in the middle of the cracked white stone.

— I knew you would come back, said Rex Stella, its voice resonating not like an ordinary sound but like a vibration passing directly through matter itself, felt in the bones rather than heard with the ears. But I didn't think it would be so soon. Soon enough for me to see it with my own eyes, someday.

81 stayed motionless, his single eye raised toward the cosmic immensity before him, a cold smile slowly stretching across his scarred face.

— You seemed in a hurry to avoid me, though, he shot back. Gone the very moment I arrived. Not very brave, for a king.

— I was not absent out of cowardice, Rex Stella replied, a hint of amusement tinging its cosmic voice. I was watching. I wanted to see how far your vengeance would go before stepping in myself.

Isidora, her phone still raised despite the persistent trembling of her hands, almost whispered, her voice for once devoid of any sarcasm.

— People, I think we're witnessing something that's literally going to change the history of the universe. Nobody move.

Takeshi, unable to tear his eyes from the crushing immensity looming over them, felt an icy shiver run down his spine, a terrifying certainty settling in him: no matter how much power 81 had shown so far, this confrontation promised to be of a completely different nature.

Rex Stella slowly spread its immense wings, the shadow they cast swallowing the entire horizon, an aura of cosmic power radiating from every beat.

— I am the King of... it began, its voice resonating with solemn gravity.

— DUMBASSES! Isidora yelled from below, her phone still pointed at the sky.

A brief silence followed, Rex Stella seeming barely disturbed, catching its cosmic breath.

— No, I am the King of... it went on.

— SHIT FLIES! Isidora shouted again, barely able to contain her laughter.

— No, I am the King of... Rex Stella insisted, a hint of annoyance perceptible in the very vibration of the air.

— PICKLES! she bellowed one last time, doubled over.

— SHUT UP! Rex Stella finally roared, its cosmic voice exploding with such force that the white stone cracked all around them, a few distant clouds scattering instantly under the shockwave. I AM THE KING OF DRAGONS!

A stunned silence followed this explosion of anger, Isidora herself frozen for a moment, before a delighted smile spread across her face.

— Okay, she said, finally reining in her laughter for her audience, people, even the King of Dragons knows Isidora's law: nobody escapes my roasts, not even things bigger than a galaxy.

81, who had watched the whole scene with a mixture of amusement and growing impatience, let out a deep little laugh.

— Annoying as ever, you, he said to Isidora, before turning his gaze back to the immensity of Rex Stella. Right. Now that we're done with the botched introductions, can we get to the serious stuff?

Rex Stella slowly lowered its gigantic head toward 81, a cold determination replacing the annoyance still vibrating in its aura.

— Yes, it said. Let us finish this, god killer.

Isidora turned to face the camera, a smug smile glued to her lips, her tone instantly regaining all its lightness despite the cosmic scale of what was looming behind her.

— Heads up, people, she told her live, reunions hit you the same way colonoscopies do. They're a pain in the ass.

She swung the camera toward Rex Stella and 81, who were facing each other, an almost palpable tension vibrating in the air between the dragon's cosmic immensity and the god killer's stubbornly motionless figure.

— Except this time, she specified, it's a bit bigger than a hospital tube.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47, turned his head toward her, incredulous despite everything he had already seen.

— You really find a way to make jokes, here, right now? he asked.

— Always, Isidora answered without even turning around, the smile still hanging on her lips. That's my thing, dealing with stress with crappy jokes. That, or I start screaming in terror, and honestly, both options are valid given the size of that thing.

Rex Stella, royally ignoring the exchange, slowly folded its gigantic wings, its cosmic gaze never leaving 81, an ancient and implacable determination readable in every one of its movements.

— Enough talk, it said, its voice vibrating through the air itself. Show me what millennia of imprisonment have made of you, 81.

81 smiled, a fierce grin twisting his scarred face, his two swords slowly rising, ready.

— With pleasure, he answered, before lunging forward, his tiny figure charging straight at the cosmic immensity before him.

Rex Stella opened its gigantic maw, a torrent of miniature stars — each burning with the intensity of a real sun — bursting out toward 81 in a devastating rain that could have vaporized entire solar systems. 81 was engulfed in the impact, an explosion of blinding light illuminating the whole sanctuary.

When the light faded, 81 was still standing, a few superficial burn marks smoking slightly on his skin, but nothing more — no real wound, no perceptible weakness in his posture.

Isidora, still filming with growing enthusiasm, let out a mocking burst of laughter.

— Are all the dragons limp-dicked today, or what? she called up to the sky, for Rex Stella's benefit.

— SHUT UP! Rex Stella roared, its cosmic voice making the whole air vibrate. I'm trying to have a stylish fight before I croak, so shut up!

81, nonchalantly brushing the last ashes off his shoulder, looked up at the dragon's immensity with an amused smile.

— You're right, though, he said to Isidora without taking his eyes off it, a king should at least try to die with a bit of panache.

— I will die with A LOT of panache, Rex Stella retorted, a hint of wounded pride breaking through its cosmic voice, its scales beginning to light up with a more intense glow, a titanic energy visibly building up throughout its immense body.

Agent 47, standing back, watched the scene with unshakable neutrality, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Reaper detects a massive buildup of energy, he announced. Recommendation: move back several additional kilometers.

Takeshi, already backing away instinctively, nodded vigorously.

— Yes, we're moving back, we're moving back right now, he said, dragging Isidora by the arm despite her protests.

— Wait, I haven't finished filming! she protested, her phone still held up toward the sky despite Takeshi's pulling.

81, alone before the growing immensity of Rex Stella, didn't back away an inch, a fierce smile spreading across his face as the cosmic energy kept building above him.

— Go on, he said. Show me your panache.

The energy Rex Stella had built up suddenly exploded in a titanic blast, a wave of cosmic light crashing toward 81 — but at that very instant, in a movement of incomprehensible speed, he leapt right through the attack itself, his two swords slicing the air before plunging deep into the dragon's gigantic chest.

A monstrous gash opened across Rex Stella's chest, a glittering dust — a mixture of starlight and cosmic matter serving as blood — pouring out in a cascade, lighting up the entire sky with a golden rain that slowly fell around them like a swarm of shooting stars.

— Watch out, he's gonna give us a facial, Isidora had called out a few seconds earlier, a mocking look on her lips — before the opposite happened before her eyes, astonishment instantly replacing her smile.

Rex Stella roared in pain, a sound that made all of space tremble, its immense wings beating frantically, scattering even more of the star dust flowing from its wound.

Agent 47, reacting with mechanical speed, immediately took a small glass vial from inside his jacket, stepping forward to collect a sample of the glittering substance falling around them.

— Sample of cosmic matter, he said simply, sealing the vial with a precise gesture. Potential analysis for scientific purposes.

Isidora, instantly regaining her liveliness, pulled a small vial of her own from her cape — from where, no one could have said — and collected some too, a delighted smile spreading across her face.

— Mine's for my potions, she said with a wink. This kind of stuff sells for a fortune on the cosmic black market.

Takeshi, still in shock from the power of the attack he had just witnessed, stood open-mouthed, his gaze moving from the dragon's gaping wound to 81, who was already landing on the ground after his leap, his swords dripping with that same glittering dust.

— You're really going shopping in the middle of a cosmic fight, he said, incredulous.

— You've gotta know how to seize opportunities, Isidora answered without the slightest embarrassment, carefully putting her vial away.

81 looked back up at Rex Stella, a satisfied smile stretching across his scarred face despite the immensity of the wound he had just inflicted — a wound that, compared to the dragon's size, was only a scratch, but enough to prove that even the King of Dragons could bleed.

— So, he said, shall we continue?

Rex Stella roared, a torrent of cosmic energy concentrating between its gaping jaws, space itself curving under the titanic pressure of the attack being formed. Then, in a final outburst, it fired a massive black hole, almost as vast as its own gigantic body, a sphere of absolute darkness swallowing everything in its path, warping the surrounding light and space.

Isidora, her phone still raised, whistled in admiration instead of backing away, filming with redoubled enthusiasm.

— Holy cow, people, look at that thing, she said, as if it were a particularly good fireworks display. XXL black hole alert, we might be filming the end of the game, stay tuned!

81 simply raised his head toward the black hole bearing down on him, his scarred face betraying not the slightest trace of worry. He took a deep breath and blew.

The black hole instantly fell apart, the concentrated cosmic energy dispersing in a silent burst of light, like a soap bubble popping in a light breeze.

Absolute silence fell over the scene, Rex Stella itself frozen.

— That's... it began, its cosmic voice losing all its grandeur, how...

— I've digested entire stars, 81 cut in with a cold smile. Your little black hole was nothing compared to what I've already swallowed.

Isidora burst out laughing, turning her camera toward herself with undisguised pleasure.

— PEOPLE, HE BLEW ON A BLACK HOLE! she yelled, delighted, as if she had just witnessed the best moment of her evening rather than a near-cosmic annihilation. I swear, if I had to write a manual for the perfect cosmic troll, that would be the title of chapter one.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed, sat down heavily on the cold stone.

— How can you stay so... cheerful, right now? he asked, incredulous.

— Because if I freak out, I stop having fun, Isidora answered with a wink, and that, big guy, is out of the question.

Rex Stella, its wings trembling slightly, backed away for the first time since the fight began, a chilling reality finally sinking in.

Isidora's phone slipped from her hand in the haste of a movement that was too sudden, smashing right into a puddle of stellar blood spread across the white stone. The screen crackled, a bluish glow briefly running through the device before it went dead for good, melted by the cosmic acidity of the liquid.

A deathly silence followed — then something changed radically in Isidora's attitude.

— YOU SON-OF-A-BITCH PIECE-OF-SHIT DRAGON, MY LIVE! she screamed, her voice vibrating with such sudden rage that even Takeshi took an instinctive step back. I'M GONNA MAKE YOU EAT YOUR DEAD, YOU SUB-SHIT, GET OVER HERE, I'M GONNA WRECK YOU!

She threw herself forward, her hands stretched toward the sky, thousands of spells bursting simultaneously from her palms — dark lightning bolts, lances of absolute void, spirals of corrosive energy, an onslaught so dense that the very air seemed to scream under the pressure. Rex Stella, already weakened by its fight with 81, had absolutely no way to defend itself against this uninterrupted barrage, every spell sinking into its massive body, piercing its scales, sending geysers of star dust spurting out with each impact.

In barely a few seconds, the dragon's gigantic head fell heavily, dying, a dull death rattle escaping its throat as the spells kept raining down relentlessly.

81, standing back, watched the scene with a satisfied smile, his arms crossed, visibly delighted by the show.

— Well then, he said to Rex Stella, almost mocking, you wanted a stylish fight. Look at that, it's way more stylish than what I would've done.

Takeshi, completely frozen, watched Isidora continue her rampage, unable to recognize the offhand, joking woman who, just seconds earlier, had been cracking jokes about colonoscopies.

— So that was her real limit, he murmured to Agent 47, who remained unfazed beside him. Not death. Not danger. Her phone.

— Data confirmed, 47 answered without the slightest trace of irony.

Lucifer, who had stayed back since the fight began, watched the scene with an almost jaded calm, arms crossed, a crooked smile hovering on his lips.

— Strangely enough, I kind of saw that coming, he said.

Takeshi turned his head toward him, still shaken by the explosion of rage he had just witnessed.

— You knew she'd react like that? he asked, incredulous.

— Let's just say I've known her for a long time, Lucifer answered with a shrug. I've seen Isidora completely ignore a god threatening her with death. But the day someone accidentally deleted her stories because of a technical error... let's just say I still have nightmares about that week.

Rex Stella, barely conscious, its massive head resting against the shattered stone, let out one last faint rumble, an almost inaudible plea mixing with its dying breath.

— Mercy... stop her...

81 walked up calmly, visibly savoring every second of the scene, his sword still drawn.

— Sorry, buddy, he said with a fierce smile, but apparently you touched something more sacred than your own life.

Isidora, still unleashed, sent one last particularly devastating spell, a lance of pure void piercing straight through one of the dragon's cosmic eyes, before finally stopping her assault, panting, her hands still smoking with residual energy.

— There, she said, her ragged breathing gradually calming down. That'll teach you.

She turned around, finding all eyes fixed on her — Takeshi still shocked, Lucifer amused, Agent 47 unfazed, and 81 clearly impressed — before shrugging with disconcerting naturalness, as if nothing had happened.

— What? she said. I had like forty thousand people watching. I had to get at least a little revenge.

Isidora rummaged in a fold of her cape, a radiant smile instantly reappearing on her face.

— Oh, actually I had another one, she said with total ease, pulling out a second phone, as if the whole scene of rage that had just unfolded had been nothing more than a slight setback.

She immediately reopened the app, relaunching the live with a quick gesture — and the viewer counter exploded almost instantly, skyrocketing.

— Sixty-nine million viewers, my favorite number, she read aloud, a delighted smile spreading across her face. People, sorry for the interruption, little technical issue, but we're back!

Meanwhile, 81 had approached Rex Stella, the dragon's gigantic mass still shaken by sporadic tremors, its eye fixed on the figure approaching it with a terror that had nothing to do with their earlier fight anymore.

— Keep her away, Rex Stella murmured, its cosmic voice reduced to a broken whisper. Please. Do whatever you want with me, but keep that madwoman away.

81 let out a deep laugh, crouching slightly to get closer to the dying dragon's gaze.

— You survived a massacre of millennia, my return, a fight against me, he said, almost admiring despite himself. And she's the one who ended up breaking you.

— She is terrifying, Rex Stella answered, a shudder running through its whole massive body. Truly terrifying.

— Yeah, 81 confirmed with a satisfied smile, slowly raising his sword. That's exactly why she's my friend.

He brought his blade down with a sharp stroke, cleanly slicing through the dragon's immense throat, putting a definitive end to the reign of the King of Dragons with one last cosmic sigh that slowly faded into the restored silence of the sanctuary.

81 went methodically to each of the dragons' remains, laying his hand on each lifeless body — Rex Aira, Rex Terra, Rex Aqua, Rex Ingenous — a dark glow escaping with each contact, absorbed straight into his chest, his massive body shuddering slightly with each new wave of power taken in.

He finished with Rex Stella, his hand resting on the immensity of the King of Dragons' skull, an aura of cosmic energy — the vastest of all — slowly flowing out of the remains to join 81, a shiver of power running through his whole body as he absorbed it completely.

— And there we go, he said, savoring the sensation, ten fewer on my list. Well, six, counting the dragons as one.

Isidora, still live, filmed the scene with undisguised enthusiasm.

— People, you are witnessing a cosmic absorption LIVE, she exclaimed. Like, literally nobody else in the known universe can say they've seen this!

Lucifer, standing back, watched the scene with placid calm, not the least bit surprised by the scale of the massacre.

— That's about what I expected, he remarked simply, as if he were watching a soccer match whose score he already knew.

Agent 47, for his part, stayed focused on his earpiece, listening to the latest data transmitted by Reaper.

— Analysis complete, he finally announced. Having analyzed the entire fight, I can confirm that even without Isidora's intervention, Rex Stella's chances of survival were zero. Even lower than statistical nothingness.

Takeshi, still sitting on the cold stone, looked up at 81, whose body seemed almost to radiate a new power, denser, even more crushing than the one he was already displaying.

— So basically, he said, you were just playing with him the whole time.

81 turned his head toward him, a fierce smile stretching across his scarred face, his six hundred and twenty-one hearts now beating with renewed power.

— A little, yeah, he admitted. But hey, I had to warm up at least a bit after millennia of sitting still.

A faint crackle sounded in Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice speaking up again with its usual precision.

— Analysis complete, it announced. Justice Man is currently located on Earth, within KJ's sphere of influence. Current activity: arresting small-time criminals.

Isidora, still live, burst out laughing, turning her camera toward 47 to capture his reaction.

— Wait, seriously? she said. The guy has a power that can lock anyone up in an infinite dimensional prison, and he spends his time nabbing petty street-corner dealers?

— Data confirmed, 47 answered without the slightest trace of irony.

81, who was calmly sheathing his swords, let out an amused rumble.

— That's just like him, he remarked. Always wanting to save the world, one jerk at a time. Even when he could take on bigger things.

— It's not even ironic, Lucifer added with a crooked smile. That's literally his philosophy. Justice, even on a small scale, matters to him as much as on a big one.

Takeshi, finally getting to his feet, brushed off the white dust clinging to his clothes, a mixture of fatigue and apprehension crossing his face.

— So where do we go now? he asked. Back to Earth to take him on directly?

81 turned to him, a calculating smile gradually replacing his satisfied look.

— Yeah, he said. But this time, we'll have to do it more discreetly. Justice Man, unlike the dragons, isn't the type to get distracted by roasts or Instagram lives.

— A real killjoy, then, Isidora remarked, reluctantly putting her phone away at last. Okay, come on, off to Earth then.

Agent 47 adjusted his weapon, his gaze already turning toward the horizon, ready to lead the way.

— Coordinates transmitted, he said. Ship approaching in three minutes.
codex-t1-c10.text: They retraced their steps across the liquid expanse, Takeshi clutching the crystal sphere against him with an almost pathological caution, every step echoing softly in the heavy silence of the Dimension of Shadows. The portal reappeared on the horizon, exactly where they had left it, a dark tear hanging in the void. They went through it one by one, the same sensation of total compression passing through them before they reappeared, in a flash of white light, at the center of the metal ring of the Martian base. Agent 47 was already waiting for them, motionless, as if he hadn't moved a centimeter since they left. — Two minutes in the real world, he said, his voice as neutral as ever. Interesting. I will pass the information on to the scientists. But first, follow me. Grand Patron Luigi is waiting for you in his office. He turned on his heel without waiting for an answer, resuming his mechanical walk through the corridors. Takeshi, still a little dazed by the sudden return to reality, exchanged a look with Isidora. — Two minutes? he repeated. We spent like... an hour in there, didn't we? — Time doesn't work the same in that kind of place, Isidora answered with a shrug, as if the remark were completely obvious. Don't worry, you'll get used to it. Lucifer, walking behind them, glanced at the sphere still clutched in Takeshi's hands. — Be careful with that, he said. I really don't want us to accidentally release the worst god killer of all time in a corridor of Grand Patron Luigi's Martian base. — Believe me, Takeshi answered, his voice tense, I'm not taking my eyes off it for a second. They followed Agent 47 through several more corridors, gradually climbing back up to the upper levels of the base, until they reached a door more imposing than the others, guarded by two soldiers who stepped aside instantly as 47 approached. — The Boss is inside, he said simply, stopping in front of the door. Go in. Isidora pushed the door open without the slightest hesitation, walking in as if the office already belonged to her. Grand Patron Luigi, for his part, was lounging in a jacuzzi installed right in the room, the bubbling water swirling gently around him — still wearing a full suit, his red tie floating slightly on the surface. — Bathing suit, you like it? he said with a satisfied smirk, spreading his arms as if to present his outfit. — You're the one who lives like that, huh, not us, Isidora answered, settling right down on the edge of the jacuzzi without caring in the slightest about how incongruous the scene was. Takeshi, hanging back with the sphere still clutched in his hands, watched the scene with growing disbelief. After everything he had just been through — Hell, the Dimension of Shadows, an omniscient entity stuck in a chair — seeing the most dangerous man in the known universe splashing around in a jacuzzi in a three-piece suit seemed almost trivial in comparison. — So, said Grand Patron Luigi, his eyes settling on the crystal sphere, you found your thing? — Yeah, Lucifer answered, stepping closer in turn, we even got a bonus. The kid's father is alive. Locked up by the Cult of KJ. Grand Patron Luigi's smile wavered slightly at the mention of KJ, a more calculating gleam crossing his eyes, before he immediately went back to his casual air. — The Cult, huh, he said. Interesting. Well, anyway, congratulations, kids. You survived a round trip into a dimension that even I considered a gamble. He sat up slightly in the water, his eyes settling directly on Takeshi, a salesman's smile returning to his face. — And you, kid, he said, looks like you've got a tough decision to make now. Free a god killer, or go save your father stashed away with KJ's lunatics. Honestly, I wouldn't want to be in your shoes. Takeshi tightened his grip on the sphere, a semblance of determination finally breaking through the exhaustion and confusion piled up since the start of this impossible day. — I'm going to free 81 first, he said. And since I'm the one who freed him, maybe he'll help me free my father. Grand Patron Luigi stayed silent for a moment, his fingers lightly tapping the surface of the water, before an approving smile formed on his face. — Smart choice, he said. It's true that, from what I know, 81 only hates gods. You're not one. And on top of that, you helped free him. That should be enough for him to owe you at least that much. Isidora, sitting on the edge of the jacuzzi, raised an eyebrow, a crooked smile stretching across her lips. — "Should" being the key word in that sentence, huh, she said. We're still talking about a guy who devoured a billion years of deities. Gratitude might not be his strong suit. — It's a risk worth taking, Takeshi answered, his voice firmer than he would have thought possible a few moments earlier. But between waiting indefinitely to find a way into the Cult of KJ and potentially having the help of the most powerful being in the universe... I'd rather take my chances with him. Lucifer crossed his arms, watching Takeshi with a new, almost surprised respect. — Well, well, he said. You might not have much in the way of powers, kid, but you've got balls. Gotta give you that much. Alastor, who had stayed silent until then, let out a satisfied little laugh. — Right, he said, so how do we wake him up without him killing all of us the very next second? Lucifer shrugged, a half-reassuring, half-amused smile hovering on his lips. — Sure, 81 is a powerful being, he said, but he puts up with Isidora, he's buddies with me, and on top of that we've got the equivalent of KJ in power right here, in a jacuzzi. Should be fine. Grand Patron Luigi let out a short laugh from his bath, waving a hand through the water with almost royal nonchalance. — It's sweet of you to count on me as a safety net, he said, but I'm warning you right now: if 81 loses it, I'm not stepping in for free either. — Of course, Isidora muttered, rolling her eyes. Everything has a price with you. — Always, Grand Patron Luigi confirmed with a wink. Takeshi, still a little tense at the idea of releasing an entity capable, in Alastor's own words, of surpassing the Incarnation of Death herself, tightened his grip on the sphere. — So, he said, if I sum up: we're assuming that if things go wrong, you'll all be there to stop me from getting killed in the next second. — That's more or less the idea, yes, Lucifer confirmed with a smile. — Reassuring, Takeshi muttered. — It's already more than you had when you summoned Alastor all alone in a forest, Alastor pointed out with a wink. At least here, you've got company. Isidora got up from the edge of the jacuzzi, stretching, her gaze passing over each member of the group with a new energy. — Okay, she said, so where do we do this? Because I don't really feel like accidentally breaking this sphere in the middle of Grand Patron Luigi's office. — That's indeed a good question, said Lucifer, and one I'd also rather we answered before doing anything. Grand Patron Luigi waved a hand through the water, brushing the question aside with a casual gesture. — Nah, I don't care, he said. You can do it in my office. A stunned silence greeted this statement, every eye turning to him. — Wait, said Lucifer, we're talking about freeing 81 here. THE 81. Here, in your office, while you're splashing around in a jacuzzi? — Yeah, Grand Patron Luigi confirmed with a shrug, as if the remark made absolutely no sense. This room is armored against pretty much everything that exists. If it goes wrong, the damage won't leave this room. And if not, well, too bad for the furniture. Isidora gave a delighted smile, settling comfortably against the edge of the desk, as if the prospect particularly amused her. — I like this plan, she said. Honestly, seeing 81 wake up next to a jacuzzi and a guy in a soaking-wet suit has pretty high comedic potential. Alastor raised an eyebrow, a crooked smile appearing on his face. — True, it wouldn't be the worst entrance for an entity that's supposed to be terrifying, he said. Takeshi, for his part, felt his heart beat harder and harder, the sphere still clutched in his hands, the reality of what he was about to do gradually sinking in with a gravity that no offhand remark really managed to lighten. — Okay, he said finally, his voice trembling slightly. So I... I just throw it on the floor, is that it? — That's it, Grand Patron Luigi confirmed, sitting up slightly in the jacuzzi, a glint of genuine interest crossing his eyes for the first time. Go ahead, kid. Smash it. Takeshi took a deep breath, his fingers tightening one last time around the sphere before he raised it above his head and hurled it against the floor with all his strength. The glass shattered with a sharp crack, almost disappointing in its simplicity, a dust of crystal scattering in a fine cloud that slowly settled onto the office floor. Then the air tore apart. A gigantic mass emerged from nothingness in a fraction of a second, a colossus nearly three meters tall, every muscle in his body taut like living stone, two massive swords crossed on his back, their blades seeming to absorb the surrounding light rather than reflect it. His face bore the scars of a billion years of combat — one eye missing, replaced by a deep scar running across his whole face, and countless other marks weathered into his skin, each one telling a story of violence no one in the room could have imagined. A deathly silence fell over the office, only the faint lapping of the jacuzzi absurdly continuing to disturb the surrounding calm. 81 stood motionless for a moment, his single eye slowly sweeping the room — the jacuzzi, Grand Patron Luigi still soaking in his suit, Lucifer, Alastor, Isidora, and finally Takeshi, still frozen in front of him, his hands empty now that the sphere was nothing but a pile of debris at his feet. Then, in a deep, hoarse voice, as if rusted by an eternity of forced silence, he finally spoke his first words since being sealed. — Who... freed me? Isidora, still leaning nonchalantly against the wall, crossed her arms with a mocking smile. — Welcome back to the land of the living, she said. Did you miss me? — I've just come out of a prison where I was locked up for thousands of years, and you ask me that, you big fat bitch! 81 roared, his voice echoing against the office walls with a power that made the windows rattle. — Calm down, said Lucifer, raising his hands in a soothing gesture. She was useful, after all. Apart from shattering my self-confidence. 81 slowly turned his single eye toward Lucifer, a glint of recognition briefly crossing his scarred face. — Lucifer, he said, less hostile but still wary. Still alive too, I see. — We do what we can, Lucifer answered with a cautious smile. The colossus swept the room with his gaze again, this time stopping on Grand Patron Luigi, still submerged in his jacuzzi, completely unfazed by the situation. — And who's this, the jackass in the soaking-wet suit? asked 81, one eyebrow — well, the brow ridge above his remaining eye — rising with a mixture of confusion and contempt. — Grand Patron Luigi, the man himself answered with a salesman's smile, waving a dripping hand in greeting. Pleased to meet you. This is my place, by the way. 81 stared at him for a moment, as if assessing the potential threat, before shrugging slightly, apparently unimpressed. — Never heard of you, he said. — You will, Grand Patron Luigi answered without losing his smile. 81's gaze finally settled on Takeshi, who had stayed silent since the colossus woke up, his single eye studying him with an intensity that made the young man take an instinctive step back. — You, said 81 in a lower, almost calculating voice. You're the one who broke the sphere. Takeshi straightened up slightly, gathering what little courage he had left. — Yes, he answered, it was me. 81 stared at him a moment longer, something almost like consideration crossing his weathered face. — Well, I thank you, demon — even if you've still got more of a human side, he said. You freed me, and that, I won't forget. But first, I have to go kill Rex Stella and all the other bastards who locked me up. A tense silence settled, Isidora suddenly sitting up straight, her offhand air giving way to sincere worry. — Wait, wait, she said. We knew you'd want revenge, but right now, straight away? We've barely gotten you out of there. — I've waited thousands of years, 81 answered, his voice hardening. I'm not waiting one more second. Takeshi, sensing that this moment might be his only chance, stepped forward, his voice hesitant but determined. — Wait, he said. Before you go off to kill anyone, I need your help. Well, so to speak. I just freed you, so I was hoping that... maybe... you could help me in return. 81 slowly turned his single eye toward him, a heavy silence settling as he assessed him again, this time with more calculating attention. — Help you with what, exactly? he asked, a hint of suspicion in his hoarse voice. — My father, said Takeshi. He's being held by the Cult of KJ. For years now. And I... I can't go there alone. A silence settled, 81 remaining motionless, his eyes still fixed on Takeshi, as if literally weighing the value of this request against his thirst for immediate revenge. 81 slowly crossed his massive arms, his single eye not leaving Takeshi, a decision visibly forming behind his hard expression. — Since you freed me, I accept, he said at last. But first, I want my revenge. I promise I'll go take on this unknown cult you're talking about. After. Takeshi hesitated, a hint of frustration showing through his relief. — How long will that take? he asked. My revenge, it... well, my father, he's been waiting for years. I wouldn't want it to drag on even longer. — Depends how long they take to die, 81 answered with chilling calm. Rex Stella and the others locked me up for millennia. I don't intend to do things halfway. Isidora let out a low whistle, exchanging a look with Lucifer. — This should be fun, she said. Grand Patron Luigi, still in his jacuzzi, raised a hand, an amused smile on his lips. — Mind you, he said, if you want a hand speeding things up, I've got resources. Lots of resources. It could considerably shorten the revenge schedule. 81 turned his gaze toward him, a glint of new interest crossing his scarred face. — You said you'd never heard of me, he said. So why would you help me? — Because I like watching chaos get organized efficiently, Grand Patron Luigi answered with a wink. And incidentally, because having a god killer who owes me a favor could come in handy later. 81 let out a deep laugh, almost a rumble, slowly shaking his head. — You, he said, I'm starting to like you. Grand Patron Luigi tapped the edge of his jacuzzi, addressing an invisible point on the ceiling. — Riper, call 47 and tell him to come now. He's going to go with our newly released friend. A cold, mechanical voice immediately rang out from a speaker hidden somewhere in the room. — Copy that, Boss. Agent 47 on his way. Isidora raised an eyebrow, turning to Grand Patron Luigi with amused curiosity. — Riper? she repeated. What's that, your invisible butler? — Reaper, Grand Patron Luigi corrected with a patient smile. My AI. Unhackable, always listening, always efficient. Unlike some, he added with a pointed look at Lucifer, who still has breakable wooden doors in his palace. — Okay, we get it, Lucifer muttered. A few moments later, the office door opened without the slightest sound, revealing Agent 47, impeccable as ever in his black suit, his eyes sweeping the room with absolute calm — even in the face of the massive and clearly hostile presence of 81, who was already sizing him up with a mixture of curiosity and contempt. — You called me, Boss, said 47, his voice as neutral as always. — Yeah, Grand Patron Luigi confirmed. You're going with our friend here, the big one-eyed bruiser, on his little personal revenge trip. Consider it a paid vacation. 47 turned his head toward 81, assessing him in silence for a long moment, not a trace of worry breaking through his usual mask of indifference. — Understood, he said simply. 81, for his part, let out a deep little laugh, almost amused by the perfect calm of the man facing him. — You're not scared of me, he said, one eyebrow raised. — Fear is not one of my parameters, 47 answered without the slightest hesitation. A silence followed, 81 seeming to weigh that answer with a new interest, almost respect. — I like this guy, he said finally, turning to Grand Patron Luigi. He's coming with me. Lucifer turned to Alastor, his tone taking on an unusual seriousness. — I'm going to follow 81, he said. You, go back to Hell, guard the kingdom for me. Alastor nodded, a crooked smile reappearing despite the gravity of the moment. — Count on me, Lulu, he said. I'll try not to break too much while you're away. Well, okay, a little. He gave Takeshi one last look, a hint of consideration crossing his usually mocking expression. — Take care of yourself, little human, he added. You've survived more in two days than most souls do in a century. Keep it up. Without waiting for an answer, he traced a gesture in the air, a dark rift opening before him, and disappeared, the tear closing immediately behind him. Meanwhile, Agent 47 had already begun preparing his equipment, taking out a series of weapons from a hidden wall compartment and inspecting them with almost surgical method, every movement calculated, precise, without the slightest hesitation. 81, for his part, had turned to Isidora, his single eye fixed on her with renewed curiosity. — Isidora, he said, how did you find me? — Simple, she answered with a satisfied smile, we just asked a chair. 81 stayed silent for a moment, clearly not sure he had heard right. — A chair, he repeated. — A super-touchy omniscient chair, she clarified. But I'll give you the details later. First, we're going to go kill the ten jerks who locked you up. A fierce smile stretched across 81's scarred face, his hands instinctively tightening on the hilts of his two massive swords. — That, he said, is exactly what I wanted to hear. Grand Patron Luigi suddenly stood up out of the jacuzzi, completely dry despite the water that had surrounded him a few seconds earlier, his suit impeccable as if it had never been wet. Takeshi blinked, unable to hide his surprise at this incongruous detail, almost trivial compared to everything he had already seen, and yet just as unsettling in its own way. — Right, come on, you've freeloaded long enough, get lost, Grand Patron Luigi called out, gesturing toward the office door. Riper, get the earpieces ready so you can guide them. — Copy that, Boss, the mechanical voice immediately rang out from the invisible speaker. A small drawer opened in the wall, revealing four miniature earpieces, a matte black almost invisible to the eye, which Agent 47 methodically collected before handing one to each of them — Isidora, Takeshi, and a last one he fitted behind his own ear with almost mechanical precision. — These earpieces connect you directly to Reaper, 47 explained in his ever perfectly neutral voice. Coordinates, tactical information, real-time communications. Do not lose them. 81, for his part, refused with a curt gesture the earpiece held out to him, a disdainful sneer twisting his scarred face. — I don't need your gadgets, he said. I've waited millennia for this revenge. I'm not going to carry it out to the sound of a little voice in my ear. 47 barely raised an eyebrow, putting the earpiece away without insisting further. — As you wish, he said simply. Isidora, adjusting hers with obvious pleasure, turned to Grand Patron Luigi, a crooked smile on her lips. — Welcoming as ever, you, she said. Thanks for the hospitality, Grand Patron. We'll cross paths again. — I don't doubt it for a second, he answered with a wink, already sitting back down behind his desk, as if the entire scene had been just one more formality in his day. Go on, beat it now, I've got an empire to run. The little group — 81, Agent 47, Isidora and Takeshi — finally left the office, heading deeper into the corridors of the Martian base, each of them aware that the real confrontation, the one against Rex Stella and the nine others who had sealed 81 away, was only just beginning. A faint crackle sounded in Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's synthetic voice rising with mechanical precision. — Location confirmed. Rex Stella and the four other Archdragons are currently in a parallel dimension classified as "Dragon Sanctuary." Coordinates transmitted to your navigation unit, Agent 47. — Copy that, 47 answered, adjusting his weapon without the slightest change in his expression. 81 turned to him, a fierce smile stretching across his scarred face. — So, he said, how do we get there? — A ship is waiting for us on the surface, 47 answered. Estimated travel time: fourteen minutes. — Fourteen minutes, 81 repeated with a dark little laugh. I've waited millennia. Fourteen more minutes is nothing. Isidora, walking beside Takeshi, gave him a little nudge with her elbow, a mischievous smile hovering on her lips. — Okay, last chance to change your mind, kid, she said. We're literally about to follow a god killer into a massacre of ancient dragons. Not exactly your classic family outing. — After everything I've already been through today, Takeshi answered with a tired smile, I think I'm past the point where I can still back out. They soon reached the surface, where a ship larger than the previous one was already waiting for them, its dark hull faintly gleaming under the reddish Martian sky. They climbed aboard, 81 bending double to get through the hatch, his massive shoulders brushing the walls of the cabin. The ship took off almost immediately, shooting through the Martian atmosphere before tipping into a flight that had nothing conventional about it anymore — space itself seeming to fold around them as they crossed the impossible distances separating them from the Dragon Sanctuary. — Final approach, Reaper's voice announced through 47's earpiece. Thirty seconds to landing. 81 straightened up, his two swords sliding out of their sheaths in one fluid gesture, a deep rumble escaping his chest — a mixture of rage held back for millennia and an almost animal impatience. — Finally, he murmured, his single eye shining with a murderous gleam. Rex Stella. I'm coming. The ship touched down in an almost unreal silence, its engines cutting out without a sound on an expanse of white stone, smooth and perfectly flat, stretching as far as the eye could see under a sky strangely devoid of any visible celestial body — no sun, no stars, only a diffuse brightness that seemed to come from the rock itself. The hatch opened, and 81 was the first to step out, his swords already in hand, his single eye sweeping the horizon with predatory intensity. Isidora and Takeshi followed close behind, while Agent 47 brought up the rear, his weapon perfectly steady in his gloved hands. They didn't have to wait long. A massive silhouette stood out in the distance, its immense wings spread against the pale sky, a reptilian creature whose scales seemed to catch and reflect every invisible air current around it. It landed with surprising grace for its size, its claws scraping against the white stone, its reptilian gaze instantly locking onto 81. — Rex Aira, Isidora murmured, a new tension in her voice. The dragon stood motionless for a long moment, as if struck dumb, before a low, almost panicked rumble escaped its throat. — You, it said, its hoarse voice echoing across the stone expanse, heavy with an ancient terror. It's impossible. You're supposed to be sealed. How— — I had help, 81 cut in icily, his grip tightening on his swords. And now, Rex Aira, I can finally finish what we should have finished millennia ago. The dragon took a step back, its wings instinctively spreading again, a glint of panic crossing its reptilian eyes as it understood, with chilling clarity, that the vengeance it had believed contained forever had finally caught up with it. 81 didn't even bother raising his swords.
