codex-t1-c5.title: Chapter 5 — Damn It, Lulu's Not Here
codex-t1-c5.html:
The same demon reappeared in the doorway, even more hunched than the first time, as if merely coming back to announce another disappointment was a danger in itself.

— Excuse me, Lord Alastor, he said in a strangled, almost pleading voice, but Lucifer has had something come up and won't be back for a little while. He didn't say how long. I'm truly sorry.

Alastor stayed silent a moment, staring at the demon with an intensity that visibly made the little creature lose what little composure he had left. Then, without a word, he let out a long, theatrical sigh, slowly shaking his head.

— Of course, he muttered, more to himself than to anyone else. Always "something came up" with him. One day he'll have to actually run an empire properly, we'll see what he says then.

He waved a hand at the demon, who didn't need to be told twice and immediately bolted out of the hall, his footsteps echoing hurriedly down the corridor until they vanished completely.

Alastor then turned to Takeshi, his usual smile gradually returning to his face, as if this annoyance no longer mattered in the slightest.

— Well, he said, stretching, looks like your meeting with the king will have to wait a bit, little human. Lucky or unlucky, I couldn't tell you.

Alastor turned on his heel, motioning for Takeshi to follow.

— Right, we're not gonna stand around here waiting for Lulu to deign to show up, he said. Come on, I'll show you something else.

— Where are we going? Takeshi asked, falling into step.

— You'll see. You've still got a lot of stuff to discover before you start to understand where you've landed.

They left the throne room, going down by a different corridor from the one they had come up. Takeshi glanced at the demons they passed — always that same silence, those same averted eyes.

— They're really never going to get used to you walking by? he asked.

— No, Alastor answered with a satisfied smile. And that's just fine.

They soon came out of the palace onto a square larger than the one they had arrived by. In the distance, a structure caught Takeshi's eye — a circular arena from which screams poured out, the roar of a crowd, a din that contrasted with the almost religious calm of the palace.

— What's that? he asked, nodding toward the arena.

— Ah, that, said Alastor, a smile spreading across his face. That, little human, is my favorite place around here. Want to see?

— Do I really have a choice?

— No, Alastor answered, laughing, already walking toward the arena. But you'd have said yes anyway, I already know you a little.

They stopped in front of the arena entrance, the roar of the crowd growing louder as they approached.

— The Arena of Despair, Alastor announced with a theatrical gesture. One of the best-known tourist attractions in Hell. Inside, any demon can fight anyone else.

— Sounds like a lovely concept, said Takeshi, a hint of sarcasm piercing through the caution in his voice.

— The nice thing, Alastor went on without picking up on it, is that the weakest demons who fight in there can't kill each other. But the most powerful ones — like me, for example — those can.

Takeshi frowned.

— Wait, but... they're already dead, aren't they? How can you die a second time?

— Good question, said Alastor, a smile spreading across his face as if he had been waiting for exactly that one. If a soul dies after its first death, here, in Hell, it's destroyed. For good. Nothing after. No Heaven, no Purgatory, no second chance. Just... nothing.

He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his words on Takeshi.

— So yeah, he added, when I step into the arena, the betting usually stops pretty fast.

They left the arena, the crowd's screams gradually fading behind them, replaced little by little by a denser, almost liquid silence. Alastor led Takeshi through a maze of narrow alleys until they came out onto a dark bank, where a thick river flowed, an almost black red, its surface barely seeming to move despite the current.

— The Styx, Alastor announced, stopping at the edge. The most dangerous river in Hell.

Takeshi stayed carefully back, watching the water — if you could still call it water — with instinctive mistrust.

— It looks... calm, he said.

— That's what makes it dangerous, Alastor answered. It was created with Lucifer's own blood.

Takeshi turned to him, frowning.

— Lucifer's blood? How do you fill a whole river with someone's blood?

— You ask way too many logical questions for a place that isn't, Alastor answered with a short laugh. But fine, to keep it simple: Lucifer is the king of Hell. His blood isn't really like yours. There's as much of it as needed.

He gestured at the river, his smile fading slightly, giving way to something more serious.

— And believe me, little human, if you ever touch this water — even just with the tip of your finger — you'll very quickly regret being curious.

Takeshi took a step back, almost instinctively, his eyes no longer leaving the motionless surface of the river.

— This water, said Alastor, staring at the Styx with unusual gravity, is so full of rage and anger that touching it could drive anyone mad. Even a demon. Even me, if I were dumb enough to dip my hand in it for more than two seconds.

— But what would it do to you, exactly? Takeshi pressed.

Alastor shrugged, a smile slowly returning to his lips, as if the question amused him more than it worried him.

— No idea, and I don't particularly feel like finding out. Let's just say all that anger built up since Lucifer fell from Heaven is always looking for somewhere to get out. So don't give it the chance.

He turned away from the river and set off again along the bank, glancing back one last time at Takeshi to make sure he was following.

— Come on. There's still one or two things I want to show you before I take you somewhere you can't do anything stupid.

Alastor stopped dead when he spotted the scene farther down the street — two demons in the middle of a brawl, one of them already on the ground, taking blow after blow without really defending himself anymore.

— Keep a low profile for two minutes, he murmured to Takeshi.

A shiver passed over his face, his features blurring for an instant before settling into a completely different appearance — more ordinary, more nondescript, almost invisible against the background.

— Don't say anything, he added in a low voice. Let me handle it.

They walked down the alley. The demon doing the hitting stopped, turning his head toward them, a nasty sneer twisting his face when he saw Takeshi.

— Hey, you, with the ass-face, he called out, come fight me.

He charged at Takeshi, fist raised, ready to strike — but Alastor stepped in with one fluid motion, his hand catching the demon's fist in midair. A sharp, wet crack echoed through the alley as Alastor closed his grip, a delighted smile spreading across his borrowed face.

— Unfortunately, he said in an almost singsong voice, you can't kill him while he's under my protection.

He let go of the crushed wrist, revealing his true appearance at the same time, his familiar face sliding back into place. The demon's eyes went wide, recognition hitting his face with immediate terror — and without another word, he bolted at full speed in the opposite direction, his shattered wrist clutched to his chest.

Alastor burst out laughing, a dry, satisfied sound, before motioning Takeshi to keep walking down the alley with him.

— Right, come on, he said. We've still got a ways to go.

The demon messenger caught up with them, out of breath, hastily bowing before Alastor.

— Lord Alastor, Lucifer is back in the throne room.

Alastor gave a broad smile, rubbing his hands together with obvious satisfaction.

— Finally, he said. Come on, little human, this time we're really going to meet him.

They headed back up to the throne room, Alastor quickening his pace with an enthusiasm that promised nothing calm. When he reached the great doors, he didn't even bother pushing them — one sharp kick sent them flying off their hinges, the wood smashing against the inside wall with a deafening crash.

— Hi Lulu, Alastor called out as he walked in, sorry, but doors are less theatrical.

Lucifer, sitting on his throne, didn't even look up at the remains of the door, as if the spectacle had long since stopped deserving the slightest attention.

— That's still the 47th this week, he said in a flat, almost weary tone. It's not that I'm short on staff, but the drafts are annoying. So try not to always smash all my fucking doors.

Lucifer turned his eyes back to Alastor, his head still slumped against his arm, his elbow propped on the armrest of the throne in a posture that betrayed an almost physical boredom.

— Anyway, apart from breaking doors, he drawled, may I ask why you wanted to see me?

— It's very simple, Alastor answered, a smile spreading across his face. Right here, Lulu, you have in front of you a very special being. One of the last Mystics.

Lucifer raised his head slightly, one eyebrow lifting with budding interest, his eyes really settling on Takeshi for the first time since they had walked in.

— A Mystic, he repeated, his voice losing a little of its weariness. It's been a while since I've seen one of those come through here.

— And I'll even confess something, Alastor added, this time turning directly to Takeshi, his smile widening even further.

Takeshi felt his heart tighten, a new apprehension replacing the simple nervousness he had felt since arriving before the throne.

— Isidora, said Alastor, is one of your distant aunts. Very distant, even. Banished from your family.

— What? Takeshi blurted, shock cutting his voice short, his eyes widening as he thought, despite himself, of that offhand woman sitting on the throne a few moments earlier, busy on her phone.

— Oh yes, Alastor went on, visibly delighted with his little effect, I asked Poppy about it while you were sleeping on my pile of bones.

Lucifer let out a dry little laugh, finally sitting up completely on his throne, his fingers drumming against the armrest with renewed interest.

— Well, well, he said, you don't bring me ordinary tourists, do you? A Mystic AND family of Isidora, in the same evening. Does she know you're family?

Takeshi, still in shock, took a moment before managing to get anything out.

— I... I don't even know how to react to that, he said finally, his voice shaking. My family... well, the one I know, never talked about her. Never.

— Doesn't surprise me, said Alastor with a short laugh. Knowing her, I imagine she pretty much earned her banishment.

Lucifer rummaged in the folds of his cape before pulling out a small crumpled scrap of paper, which he unfolded with almost theatrical slowness.

— Very well, Al, he said, but one question. Why did I find a note from Isidora on my throne that says, word for word...

He cleared his throat, putting on a mocking voice to read aloud.

— "Lulu, heads up, Al and his weird demon are gonna come by, have fun with them in a threesome, nah just kidding, but more seriously I might have found where 81 is hidden, so when you get back send me an Insta DM and I'll come. PS: I left you a boomer phone."

He looked up from the paper, a sarcastic smile hovering on his lips, his eyes settling directly on Alastor.

— "His weird demon," he repeated with relish. That's you, human.

— Charming, Alastor muttered, visibly unbothered by the description.

Takeshi, for his part, stood frozen, the name he had just heard echoing over and over in his mind with chilling weight.

— Wait, he said hesitantly, she said she'd found where 81 was hidden? The... the God Killer?

Lucifer turned his gaze to him, a smile slowly stretching across his face, something darker briefly crossing his eyes.

— Yep, he said simply, folding the paper between his fingers. That very one.

He glanced at Alastor, his smile gradually fading into a more serious, almost tense expression.

— You know what that means, if she's really found something, huh, Al?

— Yeah, Alastor answered, his own voice losing every trace of its usual lightness. It means we're all going to need our best excuses for not being around when she actually frees him.

Lucifer held out the phone to Alastor, an almost embarrassed gesture.

— Here, you do it, he said. You know technology isn't my thing.

— True, Alastor agreed, taking the phone, Isidora made a point of that in her note.

He turned the screen on, revealing the wallpaper — Isidora, frozen in a photo, flipping the bird straight at the camera.

— Charming, as always, Alastor remarked with a short laugh, before looking for the app and clumsily typing out the message.

He pressed the screen one last time, sending the DM, then set the phone back down on the armrest of the throne.

— There, done. Now we wait.

Silence fell over the hall again, broken only by the distant crackle of the hanging flames. Takeshi, still shaken by everything he had just learned, glanced nervously at the walls, as if he were already expecting what was about to happen.

He didn't have to wait long.

A deafening crash suddenly rang out, an entire wall of the hall exploding into a cloud of rubble and black dust. Isidora stood in the middle of the debris, her phone still in hand, the screen lit, without even bothering to look toward the gaping hole she had just blown in the wall.

— The repair budget's going to be tight this year, Lucifer commented, with the same couldn't-care-less intonation as always, as if the explosion were just a minor administrative inconvenience.

Isidora tucked her phone into a fold of her cape, an annoyed look crossing her face.

— Fuck's sake, Lulu, you ruined my story, she snapped. You can shut up too, you know.

— You're the one who blew up my wall, Lucifer retorted without much conviction.

— Anyway, she went on, completely ignoring the remark, I still need you to study 81, so I'll avoid killing you. So, I studied several billion trillion billion, et cetera, and I found where 81 is locked up.

She paused, a satisfied smile stretching across her lips, visibly proud of her announcement.

— It's a weird dimension, it's called the Dimension of Shadows. Basically, everything that doesn't exist, will exist, has existed or has been forgotten — like Lulu's charisma — ends up there. And in there, it's likely our little dragons and the other assholes locked him up.

Lucifer raised an eyebrow, deliberately ignoring the jab at his charisma, his attention entirely focused on the information she had just delivered.

— The Dimension of Shadows, he repeated slowly, as if trying to gauge the real weight of the discovery. Are you sure?

— Ninety-nine percent sure, Isidora answered with a casual shrug. The only annoying thing is that even I don't know how to get in. No ritual, no artifact, no known coordinates. It's the kind of place that exists just... so that nobody ever gets in.

She glanced at Alastor, then at Takeshi, a calculating smile settling on her face.

— But hey, she added, I might have a little idea for getting around that. An idea that involves your new little buddy right there.
codex-t1-c5.text: The same demon reappeared in the doorway, even more hunched than the first time, as if merely coming back to announce another disappointment was a danger in itself. — Excuse me, Lord Alastor, he said in a strangled, almost pleading voice, but Lucifer has had something come up and won't be back for a little while. He didn't say how long. I'm truly sorry. Alastor stayed silent a moment, staring at the demon with an intensity that visibly made the little creature lose what little composure he had left. Then, without a word, he let out a long, theatrical sigh, slowly shaking his head. — Of course, he muttered, more to himself than to anyone else. Always "something came up" with him. One day he'll have to actually run an empire properly, we'll see what he says then. He waved a hand at the demon, who didn't need to be told twice and immediately bolted out of the hall, his footsteps echoing hurriedly down the corridor until they vanished completely. Alastor then turned to Takeshi, his usual smile gradually returning to his face, as if this annoyance no longer mattered in the slightest. — Well, he said, stretching, looks like your meeting with the king will have to wait a bit, little human. Lucky or unlucky, I couldn't tell you. Alastor turned on his heel, motioning for Takeshi to follow. — Right, we're not gonna stand around here waiting for Lulu to deign to show up, he said. Come on, I'll show you something else. — Where are we going? Takeshi asked, falling into step. — You'll see. You've still got a lot of stuff to discover before you start to understand where you've landed. They left the throne room, going down by a different corridor from the one they had come up. Takeshi glanced at the demons they passed — always that same silence, those same averted eyes. — They're really never going to get used to you walking by? he asked. — No, Alastor answered with a satisfied smile. And that's just fine. They soon came out of the palace onto a square larger than the one they had arrived by. In the distance, a structure caught Takeshi's eye — a circular arena from which screams poured out, the roar of a crowd, a din that contrasted with the almost religious calm of the palace. — What's that? he asked, nodding toward the arena. — Ah, that, said Alastor, a smile spreading across his face. That, little human, is my favorite place around here. Want to see? — Do I really have a choice? — No, Alastor answered, laughing, already walking toward the arena. But you'd have said yes anyway, I already know you a little. They stopped in front of the arena entrance, the roar of the crowd growing louder as they approached. — The Arena of Despair, Alastor announced with a theatrical gesture. One of the best-known tourist attractions in Hell. Inside, any demon can fight anyone else. — Sounds like a lovely concept, said Takeshi, a hint of sarcasm piercing through the caution in his voice. — The nice thing, Alastor went on without picking up on it, is that the weakest demons who fight in there can't kill each other. But the most powerful ones — like me, for example — those can. Takeshi frowned. — Wait, but... they're already dead, aren't they? How can you die a second time? — Good question, said Alastor, a smile spreading across his face as if he had been waiting for exactly that one. If a soul dies after its first death, here, in Hell, it's destroyed. For good. Nothing after. No Heaven, no Purgatory, no second chance. Just... nothing. He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his words on Takeshi. — So yeah, he added, when I step into the arena, the betting usually stops pretty fast. They left the arena, the crowd's screams gradually fading behind them, replaced little by little by a denser, almost liquid silence. Alastor led Takeshi through a maze of narrow alleys until they came out onto a dark bank, where a thick river flowed, an almost black red, its surface barely seeming to move despite the current. — The Styx, Alastor announced, stopping at the edge. The most dangerous river in Hell. Takeshi stayed carefully back, watching the water — if you could still call it water — with instinctive mistrust. — It looks... calm, he said. — That's what makes it dangerous, Alastor answered. It was created with Lucifer's own blood. Takeshi turned to him, frowning. — Lucifer's blood? How do you fill a whole river with someone's blood? — You ask way too many logical questions for a place that isn't, Alastor answered with a short laugh. But fine, to keep it simple: Lucifer is the king of Hell. His blood isn't really like yours. There's as much of it as needed. He gestured at the river, his smile fading slightly, giving way to something more serious. — And believe me, little human, if you ever touch this water — even just with the tip of your finger — you'll very quickly regret being curious. Takeshi took a step back, almost instinctively, his eyes no longer leaving the motionless surface of the river. — This water, said Alastor, staring at the Styx with unusual gravity, is so full of rage and anger that touching it could drive anyone mad. Even a demon. Even me, if I were dumb enough to dip my hand in it for more than two seconds. — But what would it do to you, exactly? Takeshi pressed. Alastor shrugged, a smile slowly returning to his lips, as if the question amused him more than it worried him. — No idea, and I don't particularly feel like finding out. Let's just say all that anger built up since Lucifer fell from Heaven is always looking for somewhere to get out. So don't give it the chance. He turned away from the river and set off again along the bank, glancing back one last time at Takeshi to make sure he was following. — Come on. There's still one or two things I want to show you before I take you somewhere you can't do anything stupid. Alastor stopped dead when he spotted the scene farther down the street — two demons in the middle of a brawl, one of them already on the ground, taking blow after blow without really defending himself anymore. — Keep a low profile for two minutes, he murmured to Takeshi. A shiver passed over his face, his features blurring for an instant before settling into a completely different appearance — more ordinary, more nondescript, almost invisible against the background. — Don't say anything, he added in a low voice. Let me handle it. They walked down the alley. The demon doing the hitting stopped, turning his head toward them, a nasty sneer twisting his face when he saw Takeshi. — Hey, you, with the ass-face, he called out, come fight me. He charged at Takeshi, fist raised, ready to strike — but Alastor stepped in with one fluid motion, his hand catching the demon's fist in midair. A sharp, wet crack echoed through the alley as Alastor closed his grip, a delighted smile spreading across his borrowed face. — Unfortunately, he said in an almost singsong voice, you can't kill him while he's under my protection. He let go of the crushed wrist, revealing his true appearance at the same time, his familiar face sliding back into place. The demon's eyes went wide, recognition hitting his face with immediate terror — and without another word, he bolted at full speed in the opposite direction, his shattered wrist clutched to his chest. Alastor burst out laughing, a dry, satisfied sound, before motioning Takeshi to keep walking down the alley with him. — Right, come on, he said. We've still got a ways to go. The demon messenger caught up with them, out of breath, hastily bowing before Alastor. — Lord Alastor, Lucifer is back in the throne room. Alastor gave a broad smile, rubbing his hands together with obvious satisfaction. — Finally, he said. Come on, little human, this time we're really going to meet him. They headed back up to the throne room, Alastor quickening his pace with an enthusiasm that promised nothing calm. When he reached the great doors, he didn't even bother pushing them — one sharp kick sent them flying off their hinges, the wood smashing against the inside wall with a deafening crash. — Hi Lulu, Alastor called out as he walked in, sorry, but doors are less theatrical. Lucifer, sitting on his throne, didn't even look up at the remains of the door, as if the spectacle had long since stopped deserving the slightest attention. — That's still the 47th this week, he said in a flat, almost weary tone. It's not that I'm short on staff, but the drafts are annoying. So try not to always smash all my fucking doors. Lucifer turned his eyes back to Alastor, his head still slumped against his arm, his elbow propped on the armrest of the throne in a posture that betrayed an almost physical boredom. — Anyway, apart from breaking doors, he drawled, may I ask why you wanted to see me? — It's very simple, Alastor answered, a smile spreading across his face. Right here, Lulu, you have in front of you a very special being. One of the last Mystics. Lucifer raised his head slightly, one eyebrow lifting with budding interest, his eyes really settling on Takeshi for the first time since they had walked in. — A Mystic, he repeated, his voice losing a little of its weariness. It's been a while since I've seen one of those come through here. — And I'll even confess something, Alastor added, this time turning directly to Takeshi, his smile widening even further. Takeshi felt his heart tighten, a new apprehension replacing the simple nervousness he had felt since arriving before the throne. — Isidora, said Alastor, is one of your distant aunts. Very distant, even. Banished from your family. — What? Takeshi blurted, shock cutting his voice short, his eyes widening as he thought, despite himself, of that offhand woman sitting on the throne a few moments earlier, busy on her phone. — Oh yes, Alastor went on, visibly delighted with his little effect, I asked Poppy about it while you were sleeping on my pile of bones. Lucifer let out a dry little laugh, finally sitting up completely on his throne, his fingers drumming against the armrest with renewed interest. — Well, well, he said, you don't bring me ordinary tourists, do you? A Mystic AND family of Isidora, in the same evening. Does she know you're family? Takeshi, still in shock, took a moment before managing to get anything out. — I... I don't even know how to react to that, he said finally, his voice shaking. My family... well, the one I know, never talked about her. Never. — Doesn't surprise me, said Alastor with a short laugh. Knowing her, I imagine she pretty much earned her banishment. Lucifer rummaged in the folds of his cape before pulling out a small crumpled scrap of paper, which he unfolded with almost theatrical slowness. — Very well, Al, he said, but one question. Why did I find a note from Isidora on my throne that says, word for word... He cleared his throat, putting on a mocking voice to read aloud. — "Lulu, heads up, Al and his weird demon are gonna come by, have fun with them in a threesome, nah just kidding, but more seriously I might have found where 81 is hidden, so when you get back send me an Insta DM and I'll come. PS: I left you a boomer phone." He looked up from the paper, a sarcastic smile hovering on his lips, his eyes settling directly on Alastor. — "His weird demon," he repeated with relish. That's you, human. — Charming, Alastor muttered, visibly unbothered by the description. Takeshi, for his part, stood frozen, the name he had just heard echoing over and over in his mind with chilling weight. — Wait, he said hesitantly, she said she'd found where 81 was hidden? The... the God Killer? Lucifer turned his gaze to him, a smile slowly stretching across his face, something darker briefly crossing his eyes. — Yep, he said simply, folding the paper between his fingers. That very one. He glanced at Alastor, his smile gradually fading into a more serious, almost tense expression. — You know what that means, if she's really found something, huh, Al? — Yeah, Alastor answered, his own voice losing every trace of its usual lightness. It means we're all going to need our best excuses for not being around when she actually frees him. Lucifer held out the phone to Alastor, an almost embarrassed gesture. — Here, you do it, he said. You know technology isn't my thing. — True, Alastor agreed, taking the phone, Isidora made a point of that in her note. He turned the screen on, revealing the wallpaper — Isidora, frozen in a photo, flipping the bird straight at the camera. — Charming, as always, Alastor remarked with a short laugh, before looking for the app and clumsily typing out the message. He pressed the screen one last time, sending the DM, then set the phone back down on the armrest of the throne. — There, done. Now we wait. Silence fell over the hall again, broken only by the distant crackle of the hanging flames. Takeshi, still shaken by everything he had just learned, glanced nervously at the walls, as if he were already expecting what was about to happen. He didn't have to wait long. A deafening crash suddenly rang out, an entire wall of the hall exploding into a cloud of rubble and black dust. Isidora stood in the middle of the debris, her phone still in hand, the screen lit, without even bothering to look toward the gaping hole she had just blown in the wall. — The repair budget's going to be tight this year, Lucifer commented, with the same couldn't-care-less intonation as always, as if the explosion were just a minor administrative inconvenience. Isidora tucked her phone into a fold of her cape, an annoyed look crossing her face. — Fuck's sake, Lulu, you ruined my story, she snapped. You can shut up too, you know. — You're the one who blew up my wall, Lucifer retorted without much conviction. — Anyway, she went on, completely ignoring the remark, I still need you to study 81, so I'll avoid killing you. So, I studied several billion trillion billion, et cetera, and I found where 81 is locked up. She paused, a satisfied smile stretching across her lips, visibly proud of her announcement. — It's a weird dimension, it's called the Dimension of Shadows. Basically, everything that doesn't exist, will exist, has existed or has been forgotten — like Lulu's charisma — ends up there. And in there, it's likely our little dragons and the other assholes locked him up. Lucifer raised an eyebrow, deliberately ignoring the jab at his charisma, his attention entirely focused on the information she had just delivered. — The Dimension of Shadows, he repeated slowly, as if trying to gauge the real weight of the discovery. Are you sure? — Ninety-nine percent sure, Isidora answered with a casual shrug. The only annoying thing is that even I don't know how to get in. No ritual, no artifact, no known coordinates. It's the kind of place that exists just... so that nobody ever gets in. She glanced at Alastor, then at Takeshi, a calculating smile settling on her face. — But hey, she added, I might have a little idea for getting around that. An idea that involves your new little buddy right there.

codex-t1-c6.title: Chapter 6 — Next Stop: Another Dimension Lost Up My Asshole.
codex-t1-c6.html:
Isidora pointed at Takeshi with a jerk of her head, a crooked smile still hanging on her lips.

— Okay, either we try sending him in as a scout, she said, but then again, he might disappear like Lulu's hair.

— I still have all my hair, Lucifer muttered, one hand instinctively running through it.

— Or, Isidora went on without even acknowledging him, we can make a pact with a powerful enough entity. Okay, I don't know who yet, but it's still a solution. So shut your mouths.

Takeshi, who hadn't said a word since the wall exploded, felt an icy shiver run down his spine at the idea of even being mentioned as a potential "scout" for a dimension whose entrance even Isidora didn't know.

— Wait, he said finally, his voice hesitant but determined to be heard. Where exactly are you talking about sending me? Into the Dimension of Shadows? Straight in?

Isidora turned her head toward him, as if she had almost forgotten he could talk.

— Yeah, she said with disconcerting nonchalance. Well, if we figure out how. It's just one option among others, calm down.

— It's an option that means I might disappear forever, Takeshi answered, his voice rising slightly in pitch.

— Well, yeah, she confirmed without the slightest ounce of compassion. That's the risk of the job.

Alastor let out a short laugh, visibly amused by Takeshi's growing panic, while Lucifer merely watched the scene with distant interest, his chin still resting on his fist.

— Don't worry, little human, said Alastor. Nobody's decided anything yet. We're thinking, that's all. That's already not bad, for us.

Lucifer straightened up slightly on his throne, his gaze sliding toward Isidora with a hint of irony.

— Not that I'm a fan of humans turned demons, he said, but if he croaks for nothing, it's pointless. And besides, Isidora, you're his distant aunt.

Isidora froze for a moment, her gaze slowly turning to Takeshi, as if she were seeing him for the first time in a completely different light. She narrowed her eyes, looking him up and down with a new, almost clinical attention.

— Wait, what? she said finally, her voice losing all its usual nonchalance. Seriously?

— Seriously, Alastor confirmed, a satisfied smile spreading across his face. I asked Poppy. One of the last Mystics, and incidentally family of yours. Small world, huh?

Isidora stayed silent for a long moment, her eyes still fixed on Takeshi, something unreadable crossing her features — a mixture of surprise, calculation, and a hint of interest that had nothing to do with the Dimension of Shadows anymore.

— Well, shit, she said at last, a dry little laugh escaping her. That changes things quite a bit.

She stepped closer to Takeshi, still studying him, a new smile forming on her lips — more calculating than warm.

— Okay, in that case, she went on, turning to Lucifer, maybe we'll avoid sending him off to get erased in some godforsaken dimension. We'll need another plan.

Lucifer shrugged, an amused smile hovering on his face.

— Finally, an intelligent decision, he remarked.

Isidora came even closer, her piercing gaze scrutinizing Takeshi as if he were a particularly disappointing collector's item.

— Holy shit, so this is the son of the family furniture, she blurted. You don't look like him. For starters, you keep your mouth shut, and you haven't tried to take on a cult whose leader has a soul fragment from one of the most powerful creatures in the universe. And more, but I can't be bothered to list it all.

Takeshi frowned, confusion mixing with growing worry.

— What are you talking about? he asked. What do you mean, a cult?

— Well, it's easy, answered his rather disreputable aunt, a nasty smile stretching across her lips. Your father, the biggest idiot in the family, because the moment he became leader, he went off on his shitty crusade.

Takeshi stood frozen, the word "father" echoing in him with a weight he hadn't anticipated.

— My father? he repeated, his voice trembling slightly. Leader of what? He... he's alive? You know where he is?

Isidora gave a short, dry, almost cruel laugh, slowly shaking her head.

— Now that, big guy, is the best question of the evening. And I don't have the answer.

Isidora crossed her arms, her gaze wandering for a moment to some undefined point, as if she were mentally going back through decades, or even more.

— Listen, kid, she said, I've been alive for a long time. Like, a really long time. I've known the whole line of Mystics, generation after generation. Your family, I watched it be born, grow up, reproduce, die, start all over again.

She paused, a bitter smile hovering on her lips.

— And one day, your father found out about my little activities. Let's just say I wasn't exactly the type to follow the Mystics' very strict rules about magic and the Void. He didn't like it. So he banished me. Just like that. No trial, no discussion.

— Banished how? Takeshi asked, his voice hesitant.

— How do you think? she answered with a disillusioned shrug. Cut off from the bloodline, erased from the registers, no longer allowed to set foot in any sacred place of the Mystics. As if I'd never existed.

She came a little closer still, her gaze locking straight onto Takeshi's, something harder, colder, piercing through her usually offhand tone.

— So yeah, your father and I weren't exactly on good terms. But that doesn't stop me from finding it ironic that his own son ends up here, in Hell, chatting with the aunt he banished. The world has a shitty sense of humor sometimes.

Isidora straightened up, her tone gradually returning to its usual casualness, even if something more thoughtful lingered in her eyes.

— Mind you, she said, crossing her arms, there's even a chance your father's in the Dimension of Shadows too. With his shitty crusade and his disappearance, it'd fit pretty well.

Takeshi felt his heart tighten, a fragile and painful hope springing up despite himself.

— You think he could be alive? There?

— I said a chance, Isidora clarified, raising a finger in warning. Not a certainty. It's one of the mysteries nobody has the answer to yet. So don't get carried away too fast, big guy.

She glanced at Alastor and Lucifer, a crooked smile reappearing on her face.

— Which means, she added, we now have two good reasons to figure out how to get into that fucking dimension. 81, and maybe the kid's old man.

Lucifer let out a theatrical sigh, slumping back against his throne.

— Great, he said glumly. Even more reasons for things to go wrong.

Isidora whipped out her phone, throwing an arm around Takeshi's shoulders without giving him time to protest, and snapped the photo in one quick movement, her smile wide and perfectly calculated for the camera.

— Wait, what— Takeshi began, still frozen by the surprise of the gesture.

But she was already tapping on the screen, completely ignoring his reaction, typing out the caption with sudden concentration.

— There, she said, pressing "post," a satisfied smile on her lips. "A member of my family still alive, isn't that weird?"

She put the phone away as if the matter were closed, while Takeshi stood there open-mouthed.

— You... you really just posted a picture of me, he said, his voice betraying a mixture of disbelief and exasperation. On Instagram. In Hell.

— Well, yeah, Isidora answered with a shrug, as if the remark made no sense at all. You got a problem with that?

— I've got plenty of problems with that! Takeshi exclaimed. Like, can people on Earth see this account? Can my family come across it? Can—

— Relax, Isidora cut in, raising a hand. My followers are just demons, gods, and two or three bored cosmic entities. Your mom will never see it, don't worry.

Alastor, standing back, let out a short laugh, visibly delighted by the show.

— Welcome to the family, little human, he said. It's never calm with these people.

Takeshi stayed silent for a moment, his mind putting the pieces together with painful slowness, before looking back up at Isidora.

— But then, he said, if my mother is alive... does that mean she's one of the Mystics?

Isidora shook her head, an almost sympathetic sigh escaping her, as if she already regretted what she was going to have to say.

— No, let me crush your dreams right away, she said. Your mother lost her memories. Because of the cult. And you, they figured a kid would never remember, so they just... let you go.

Takeshi felt an icy cold settle in his chest, the words echoing over and over in his mind.

— Wait, he said, his voice shaking. My mother... the one I've always talked to on the phone, the one who raised me... she's not really...

— Oh no, she's very real, Isidora cut in quickly, a hint of irritation in her voice. She really is your biological mother. She just doesn't remember anything from before. For her, you've always been a normal kid, born into a normal family. The cult erased everything about the Mystics, your father, the whole damn mess.

She paused, watching Takeshi with an attention almost unusual for her, something resembling compassion briefly showing through her usually offhand tone.

— It must have been easier for her that way, she added more softly. No memories, no grieving to do. Just a normal life with a son she loves, without knowing what she really lost.

Takeshi stayed silent, the weight of this revelation crashing down on him with a force he hadn't anticipated — this new certainty that his whole childhood, his whole life with his mother, rested on an induced amnesia, a lie she didn't even know about herself.

Lucifer straightened up on his throne, drawing everyone's attention back to him, a mocking smile already hovering on his lips.

— Right, so, Isidora, a plan for this dimension pulled out of my ass, he said.

— For once you're telling the truth, Isidora shot back without a second's hesitation. True, seeing what a dimension-fucker you are, we could fit at least eighteen in there. And that's only if you're constipated.

Lucifer rolled his eyes without even bothering to reply, while Alastor let out a short laugh behind them.

— So, Isidora went on, getting serious again — or at least as serious as she could get — to get in, we have to ask an entity. After looking into it, because I don't work like a king sitting on his throne all the time, we have two options. Either we ask a Higher Incarnation, or Grand Patron Luigi.

Takeshi, who was following the conversation with growing confusion, raised a hesitant hand.

— Wait, you've lost me there, he said. What's a Higher Incarnation? And who's Grand Patron Luigi?

Isidora turned her head toward him, one eyebrow raised, as if she had almost forgotten he knew nothing about any of this.

— Oh right, that's true, you're brand new, she said. Okay, express summary: there's a guy, well, an entity, called KJ, older than absolutely everything, creation and destruction in person. He's got some super-powerful buddies called the Higher Incarnations, like his own sub-gods.

— And Grand Patron Luigi, said Lucifer, taking over, in an almost more cautious tone than usual, is the other cosmic lunatic. A human, originally, but he became an anomaly on the same level as KJ. He runs an interdimensional mafia. Like, really interdimensional. Missiles, spaceships, the whole shebang.

— And let's just say, Isidora added, that asking either of them for a favor is never free. Never.

Isidora tucked a strand of hair behind her ear, an almost irritated look crossing her face at the idea of having to explain any further.

— Okay, talking to an Incarnation isn't going to be easy, she said. Like, really not easy. First we have to find one willing to see us without reducing us to ashes before we finish a sentence.

— And the other option? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised.

— To talk to Grand Patron Luigi, Isidora continued, we'll have to go to Earth. The right side of it. If we don't get spotted by his little dog with the mass-produced product name, anyway.

— His little dog? Takeshi repeated, confusion clearly showing in his voice.

— Agent 47, Lucifer clarified, with a mix of respect and wariness in his tone. Don't make that face, kid, he's more dangerous than the nickname makes him sound.

Isidora brushed the remark aside with a wave of her hand, turning her attention back to the other three, a crooked smile reappearing on her lips.

— Anyway, choose, she said, hands on her hips, her gaze moving from Lucifer to Takeshi and then to Alastor. Higher Incarnation, survival odds debatable. Or Grand Patron Luigi, on Earth, with a risk of getting spotted by the best assassin in the entire known universe. What do you think?

Alastor raised a hand, as if struck by a brilliant idea.

— We could also go to one of the bases, he said. They're on Mars and the Sun, I think?

Lucifer slowly turned his head toward him, a half-dismayed, half-appalled expression settling on his face.

— I knew drugs had negative effects, but to this point, fuck's sake, Al, he said. Think for two seconds. Getting near one of those bases is literally signing your own death warrant. On Earth, our chances are already slim. But on an actual base...

— True, Isidora confirmed, a mocking smile stretching across her lips. For once his shit's coming out the bottom and not out of his mouth.

Alastor shrugged, visibly not very offended by the collective verdict, while Isidora turned to Takeshi, an almost solemn look briefly replacing her usual nonchalance.

— We can't go there, so Earth it is, dear distant nephew, she said. You're going back to your planet.

Takeshi felt a shiver run through him, a confused mixture of hope and apprehension at the idea of seeing Earth again — his mother, his girlfriend, his apartment, his life from before — but tinged with a new worry about what awaited him there now.

— Wait, he said, his voice hesitant. If I go back to Earth... Poppy won't be able to find me, right? Since I'm... dead?

An awkward silence settled, Isidora and Alastor exchanging a look that was anything but reassuring.

— Now that, Isidora said finally, is an excellent question I really don't feel like answering honestly.

— Poppy must have left Earth a long time ago, said Alastor. The whole universe is a playground for her. And if a universe isn't entertaining enough, she just switches. So she's probably very far away by now.

Takeshi felt some of the tension in his chest loosen, without disappearing entirely.

— Probably, he repeated. That's not exactly what you'd call a guarantee.

— Nothing's ever a guarantee with her, little human, Alastor answered with a crooked smile. But you've got a better chance of getting hit by a bus on Earth than of running into her again. Well, a cosmic bus, but you get the idea.

Isidora nodded, picking her phone back up absentmindedly, as if the matter were already settled in her mind.

— Well, there you go, she said. Plan B approved. We head to Earth, we find Grand Patron Luigi, we negotiate to get into the Dimension of Shadows, and with a bit of luck, we get 81 back and maybe the kid's old man along the way.

— Simple, then, Lucifer remarked dryly, clearly not convinced.

— I never said it was simple, Isidora answered with a predatory smile. I said it was the plan.

And besides, Isidora, you're his distant aunt. Isidora froze for a moment, her gaze slowly turning to Takeshi, as if she were seeing him for the first time in a completely different light. She narrowed her eyes, looking him up and down with a new, almost clinical attention. — Wait, what? she said finally, her voice losing all its usual nonchalance. Seriously? — Seriously, Alastor confirmed, a satisfied smile spreading across his face. I asked Poppy. One of the last Mystics, and incidentally family of yours. Small world, huh? Isidora stayed silent for a long moment, her eyes still fixed on Takeshi, something unreadable crossing her features — a mixture of surprise, calculation, and a hint of interest that had nothing to do with the Dimension of Shadows anymore. — Well, shit, she said at last, a dry little laugh escaping her. That changes things quite a bit. She stepped closer to Takeshi, still studying him, a new smile forming on her lips — more calculating than warm. — Okay, in that case, she went on, turning to Lucifer, maybe we'll avoid sending him off to get erased in some godforsaken dimension. We'll need another plan. Lucifer shrugged, an amused smile hovering on his face. — Finally, an intelligent decision, he remarked. Isidora came even closer, her piercing gaze scrutinizing Takeshi as if he were a particularly disappointing collector's item. — Holy shit, so this is the son of the family furniture, she blurted. You don't look like him. For starters, you keep your mouth shut, and you haven't tried to take on a cult whose leader has a soul fragment from one of the most powerful creatures in the universe. And more, but I can't be bothered to list it all. Takeshi frowned, confusion mixing with growing worry. — What are you talking about? he asked. What do you mean, a cult? — Well, it's easy, answered his rather disreputable aunt, a nasty smile stretching across her lips. Your father, the biggest idiot in the family, because the moment he became leader, he went off on his shitty crusade. Takeshi stood frozen, the word "father" echoing in him with a weight he hadn't anticipated. — My father? he repeated, his voice trembling slightly. Leader of what? He... he's alive? You know where he is? Isidora gave a short, dry, almost cruel laugh, slowly shaking her head. — Now that, big guy, is the best question of the evening. And I don't have the answer. Isidora crossed her arms, her gaze wandering for a moment to some undefined point, as if she were mentally going back through decades, or even more. — Listen, kid, she said, I've been alive for a long time. Like, a really long time. I've known the whole line of Mystics, generation after generation. Your family, I watched it be born, grow up, reproduce, die, start all over again. She paused, a bitter smile hovering on her lips. — And one day, your father found out about my little activities. Let's just say I wasn't exactly the type to follow the Mystics' very strict rules about magic and the Void. He didn't like it. So he banished me. Just like that. No trial, no discussion. — Banished how? Takeshi asked, his voice hesitant. — How do you think? she answered with a disillusioned shrug. Cut off from the bloodline, erased from the registers, no longer allowed to set foot in any sacred place of the Mystics. As if I'd never existed. She came a little closer still, her gaze locking straight onto Takeshi's, something harder, colder, piercing through her usually offhand tone. — So yeah, your father and I weren't exactly on good terms. But that doesn't stop me from finding it ironic that his own son ends up here, in Hell, chatting with the aunt he banished. The world has a shitty sense of humor sometimes. Isidora straightened up, her tone gradually returning to its usual casualness, even if something more thoughtful lingered in her eyes. — Mind you, she said, crossing her arms, there's even a chance your father's in the Dimension of Shadows too. With his shitty crusade and his disappearance, it'd fit pretty well. Takeshi felt his heart tighten, a fragile and painful hope springing up despite himself. — You think he could be alive? There? — I said a chance, Isidora clarified, raising a finger in warning. Not a certainty. It's one of the mysteries nobody has the answer to yet. So don't get carried away too fast, big guy. She glanced at Alastor and Lucifer, a crooked smile reappearing on her face. — Which means, she added, we now have two good reasons to figure out how to get into that fucking dimension. 81, and maybe the kid's old man. Lucifer let out a theatrical sigh, slumping back against his throne. — Great, he said glumly. Even more reasons for things to go wrong. Isidora whipped out her phone, throwing an arm around Takeshi's shoulders without giving him time to protest, and snapped the photo in one quick movement, her smile wide and perfectly calculated for the camera. — Wait, what— Takeshi began, still frozen by the surprise of the gesture. But she was already tapping on the screen, completely ignoring his reaction, typing out the caption with sudden concentration. — There, she said, pressing "post," a satisfied smile on her lips. "A member of my family still alive, isn't that weird?" She put the phone away as if the matter were closed, while Takeshi stood there open-mouthed. — You... you really just posted a picture of me, he said, his voice betraying a mixture of disbelief and exasperation. On Instagram. In Hell. — Well, yeah, Isidora answered with a shrug, as if the remark made no sense at all. You got a problem with that? — I've got plenty of problems with that! Takeshi exclaimed. Like, can people on Earth see this account? Can my family come across it? Can— — Relax, Isidora cut in, raising a hand. My followers are just demons, gods, and two or three bored cosmic entities. Your mom will never see it, don't worry. Alastor, standing back, let out a short laugh, visibly delighted by the show. — Welcome to the family, little human, he said. It's never calm with these people. Takeshi stayed silent for a moment, his mind putting the pieces together with painful slowness, before looking back up at Isidora. — But then, he said, if my mother is alive... does that mean she's one of the Mystics? Isidora shook her head, an almost sympathetic sigh escaping her, as if she already regretted what she was going to have to say. — No, let me crush your dreams right away, she said. Your mother lost her memories. Because of the cult. And you, they figured a kid would never remember, so they just... let you go. Takeshi felt an icy cold settle in his chest, the words echoing over and over in his mind. — Wait, he said, his voice shaking. My mother... the one I've always talked to on the phone, the one who raised me... she's not really... — Oh no, she's very real, Isidora cut in quickly, a hint of irritation in her voice. She really is your biological mother. She just doesn't remember anything from before. For her, you've always been a normal kid, born into a normal family. The cult erased everything about the Mystics, your father, the whole damn mess. She paused, watching Takeshi with an attention almost unusual for her, something resembling compassion briefly showing through her usually offhand tone. — It must have been easier for her that way, she added more softly. No memories, no grieving to do. Just a normal life with a son she loves, without knowing what she really lost. Takeshi stayed silent, the weight of this revelation crashing down on him with a force he hadn't anticipated — this new certainty that his whole childhood, his whole life with his mother, rested on an induced amnesia, a lie she didn't even know about herself. Lucifer straightened up on his throne, drawing everyone's attention back to him, a mocking smile already hovering on his lips. — Right, so, Isidora, a plan for this dimension pulled out of my ass, he said. — For once you're telling the truth, Isidora shot back without a second's hesitation. True, seeing what a dimension-fucker you are, we could fit at least eighteen in there. And that's only if you're constipated. Lucifer rolled his eyes without even bothering to reply, while Alastor let out a short laugh behind them. — So, Isidora went on, getting serious again — or at least as serious as she could get — to get in, we have to ask an entity. After looking into it, because I don't work like a king sitting on his throne all the time, we have two options. Either we ask a Higher Incarnation, or Grand Patron Luigi. Takeshi, who was following the conversation with growing confusion, raised a hesitant hand. — Wait, you've lost me there, he said. What's a Higher Incarnation? And who's Grand Patron Luigi? Isidora turned her head toward him, one eyebrow raised, as if she had almost forgotten he knew nothing about any of this. — Oh right, that's true, you're brand new, she said. Okay, express summary: there's a guy, well, an entity, called KJ, older than absolutely everything, creation and destruction in person. He's got some super-powerful buddies called the Higher Incarnations, like his own sub-gods. — And Grand Patron Luigi, said Lucifer, taking over, in an almost more cautious tone than usual, is the other cosmic lunatic. A human, originally, but he became an anomaly on the same level as KJ. He runs an interdimensional mafia. Like, really interdimensional. Missiles, spaceships, the whole shebang. — And let's just say, Isidora added, that asking either of them for a favor is never free. Never. Isidora tucked a strand of hair behind her ear, an almost irritated look crossing her face at the idea of having to explain any further. — Okay, talking to an Incarnation isn't going to be easy, she said. Like, really not easy. First we have to find one willing to see us without reducing us to ashes before we finish a sentence. — And the other option? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised. — To talk to Grand Patron Luigi, Isidora continued, we'll have to go to Earth. The right side of it. If we don't get spotted by his little dog with the mass-produced product name, anyway. — His little dog? Takeshi repeated, confusion clearly showing in his voice. — Agent 47, Lucifer clarified, with a mix of respect and wariness in his tone. Don't make that face, kid, he's more dangerous than the nickname makes him sound. Isidora brushed the remark aside with a wave of her hand, turning her attention back to the other three, a crooked smile reappearing on her lips. — Anyway, choose, she said, hands on her hips, her gaze moving from Lucifer to Takeshi and then to Alastor. Higher Incarnation, survival odds debatable. Or Grand Patron Luigi, on Earth, with a risk of getting spotted by the best assassin in the entire known universe. What do you think? Alastor raised a hand, as if struck by a brilliant idea. — We could also go to one of the bases, he said. They're on Mars and the Sun, I think? Lucifer slowly turned his head toward him, a half-dismayed, half-appalled expression settling on his face. — I knew drugs had negative effects, but to this point, fuck's sake, Al, he said. Think for two seconds. Getting near one of those bases is literally signing your own death warrant. On Earth, our chances are already slim. But on an actual base... — True, Isidora confirmed, a mocking smile stretching across her lips. For once his shit's coming out the bottom and not out of his mouth. Alastor shrugged, visibly not very offended by the collective verdict, while Isidora turned to Takeshi, an almost solemn look briefly replacing her usual nonchalance. — We can't go there, so Earth it is, dear distant nephew, she said. You're going back to your planet. Takeshi felt a shiver run through him, a confused mixture of hope and apprehension at the idea of seeing Earth again — his mother, his girlfriend, his apartment, his life from before — but tinged with a new worry about what awaited him there now. — Wait, he said, his voice hesitant. If I go back to Earth... Poppy won't be able to find me, right? Since I'm... dead? An awkward silence settled, Isidora and Alastor exchanging a look that was anything but reassuring. — Now that, Isidora said finally, is an excellent question I really don't feel like answering honestly. — Poppy must have left Earth a long time ago, said Alastor. The whole universe is a playground for her. And if a universe isn't entertaining enough, she just switches. So she's probably very far away by now. Takeshi felt some of the tension in his chest loosen, without disappearing entirely. — Probably, he repeated. That's not exactly what you'd call a guarantee. — Nothing's ever a guarantee with her, little human, Alastor answered with a crooked smile. But you've got a better chance of getting hit by a bus on Earth than of running into her again. Well, a cosmic bus, but you get the idea. Isidora nodded, picking her phone back up absentmindedly, as if the matter were already settled in her mind. — Well, there you go, she said. Plan B approved. We head to Earth, we find Grand Patron Luigi, we negotiate to get into the Dimension of Shadows, and with a bit of luck, we get 81 back and maybe the kid's old man along the way. — Simple, then, Lucifer remarked dryly, clearly not convinced. — I never said it was simple, Isidora answered with a predatory smile. I said it was the plan.

codex-t1-c7.title: Chapter 7 — Not Even a 1% Chance, Right?
codex-t1-c7.html:
Isidora raised her hand, slicing the air with a sharp gesture. Reality tore open before them, a dark rift opening in the void and revealing, for an instant, Earth hanging in the darkness of space, surrounded by other distant planets faintly twinkling.

— Come on, let's go, she called, jumping into the rift first without the slightest hesitation.

Lucifer followed with a resigned sigh, then Alastor, dragging Takeshi along with a firm hand on his shoulder. The passage was brief, a sensation of total compression followed by immediate vertigo — and the next instant, all four of them were standing right in the middle of the Place de l'Étoile, the Arc de Triomphe towering above them, cars honking frantically around the roundabout without a single driver seeming to notice their sudden appearance.

— My favorites, said Isidora with a wide smile, sweeping her gaze over the hurried passersby around them. Parisian assholes. Do you know them, Takeshi?

— No, he answered, still a little dazed by the crossing. I lived in New York.

Isidora turned to him, a predatory smile stretching across her lips.

— If you think Paris is like the clichés, she answered, you're going to see your dreams shatter like Lulu's confidence in himself.

Lucifer, who was discreetly adjusting a lock of hair, shot her a black look without bothering to reply, while Alastor watched the city around them with an almost nostalgic interest, a smile hovering on his lips.

A driver, visibly at the end of his rope, stuck his head out of his car window, yelling over the concert of horns.

— Hey! You morons, get out of the way, goddamn it, my wife's going into labor!

Isidora turned her head toward him, a radiant smile spreading across her face, before answering as she strolled on, not quickening her pace in the slightest.

— Calm down, dumbass, we've all got our priorities in life, jerk.

The man stayed open-mouthed for a moment, visibly unprepared for that level of nonchalance, before starting to honk again with even more rage. Takeshi, walking behind, cast an embarrassed glance at the car, then at Isidora.

— Maybe you could hurry up a little, couldn't you? Like, his wife is giving birth right now.

— So what? Isidora answered without even turning around. I'm not the one who knocked her up. He can deal with it himself.

Lucifer, walking beside them with royal nonchalance, as if the entire Parisian traffic simply didn't exist for him, let out a short laugh.

— Welcome to Earth, kid, he told Takeshi. You'll quickly figure out that nobody in this group really has a sense of priorities.

They eventually reached the sidewalk, leaving behind them a concert of horns and insults that didn't seem to bother anyone in the group at all, except Takeshi, who turned back toward the road one last time, a mixture of embarrassment and disbelief painted on his face.

The same man suddenly reappeared, disheveled, out of his car, screaming across the street and pointing at them.

— MY WIFE DIED BECAUSE OF YOU, YOU FILTHY BITCH!

Isidora stopped dead in the middle of the crosswalk, turning toward him with a delighted smile, as if that accusation had just made her entire day.

— If you'd kept your libido in check and put away your tiny sausage, she'd still be alive, she answered with a smirk, before resuming her walk across the street with a deliberately provocative slowness, taking all the time in the world despite the cars already starting to honk around her again.

The man stood frozen on the sidewalk, mouth open, unable to come up with a comeback to such a level of audacity, while Lucifer burst out laughing behind them, one hand pressed against his stomach.

— Now that, he said between bursts of laughter, is high art, Isidora. High art.

Takeshi hurried to catch up with the group, casting a nervous glance back at the man still planted in the middle of the street.

— Isn't what we're doing supposed to be discreet? he asked, a hint of exasperation in his voice. We're supposed to not get spotted, right?

— Little human, Alastor answered with an amused smile, we're in the middle of Paris with the king of Hell, a witch of the Void, and a demon older than most known civilizations. It's a little late to think about discretion.

The group finally stopped in front of the gates of the Élysée, the imposing facade of the palace rising before them, guards standing frozen on either side of the main entrance.

— Here we are at the Paradise of getting screwed, Isidora announced with a theatrical gesture toward the building. Where all the decisions got made, especially about the fucking taxes. Now Macron scrubs the floor for Grand Patron Luigi's general, who took command of the Élysée exactly seven years, four months, five weeks, five days, seventeen hours, thirty-seven minutes and forty-seven seconds ago. Forty-nine now.

Takeshi blinked, trying his best to keep up.

— How do you know that? he asked.

— Dunno, I made it up, Isidora answered with a perfectly relaxed shrug. But Macron really does clean the floor with his tongue.

Takeshi turned his head toward the palace entrance, and indeed, through the gates, you could make out a figure kneeling on the marble floor, methodically licking it under the indifferent gaze of two soldiers in dark armor posted nearby.

— Is that... is that really him? Takeshi asked, his voice strangled by a mixture of disgust and disbelief.

— Yup, Lucifer confirmed, watching the scene with almost jaded detachment. It's been like that for years. Grand Patron Luigi likes to humiliate the people who had power before him. A matter of principle, I suppose.

Alastor, for his part, stayed silent, his eyes scanning the surroundings with a new attention, more serious than usual.

— Right, he said finally, we're here. Now we need to figure out how to get in without getting torn to shreds by security.

Isidora walked up to one of the guards posted in front of the gates, a predatory smile already stretching across her lips.

— Hey you, ugly mug, come here for two seconds, please.

The guard stiffened, turning his head toward her with a suspicious expression.

— Ma'am, this is the private property of General Duchon, he said in a curt, almost mechanical tone.

Isidora burst out laughing, a loud sound that echoed all the way back into the street behind them.

— Holy shit, Lulu, we found someone who's almost as much of a moron as you, she called over her shoulder.

— Always a pleasure, Lucifer answered flatly, clearly not offended in the slightest.

Isidora turned her attention back to the guard, her smile gradually fading into something sharper, almost threatening.

— Anyway, she said, we need to talk to General My-Ass in there. So open the door, or I'll open your skull, and the door too while I'm at it.

The guard hesitated, his hand instinctively sliding toward the weapon at his belt, his eyes seeking support from his colleague a few meters away — but the latter stayed frozen, visibly just as uneasy facing the little group standing before the gates.

— I... I have to check with my superiors, he finally stammered, his voice losing its initial confidence.

Takeshi, hanging back, watched the scene with growing tension, casting a nervous glance at Alastor.

— This is really going to end badly, isn't it? he murmured.

— Oh, very likely, Alastor answered with a delighted smile, making not the slightest effort to reassure him.

A dark flash burst from Isidora's hand, an invisible force brutally slamming the guard's head against the metal gate, his helmet banging against the bars with a dull thud. The man let out a strangled cry, his hands thrashing against a grip he couldn't even see.

— Listen to me carefully, you dried-up ballsack, said Isidora, her voice suddenly deeper, stripped of all the lightness she had shown until then. Either you open the door, or we're going to have a problem. And believe me — ask that shithead who passes for the king of Hell — to keep going, I won't hesitate to burn off your ball hair and make you eat it, and then make you eat your own shit. So you have exactly five seconds.

— That's true, Lucifer confirmed with a nonchalant shrug, as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world. She's done worse to gods, so imagine what she can do to you.

The guard, his face crushed against the gate, let out a panicked whimper, his eyes rolling frantically toward his colleague, who took a step back, visibly unwilling to intervene.

— Five, Isidora began, a nasty smile stretching across her lips.

— Okay, okay! the guard cried, his voice choked with panic. I'll open it, I'll open it, let me go!

Isidora released her grip with a careless gesture, the guard nearly collapsing to the ground, gasping, before rushing to the control panel to open the gates, his hands shaking so hard he missed the button twice before finally hitting it.

Takeshi watched the scene, a mixture of horror and morbid fascination painted on his face, as the massive gates slowly began to open before them with a metallic creak.

— You're really terrifying, he murmured, more to himself than to anyone else.

— Thank you, Isidora answered with a radiant smile, as if it were the nicest compliment she'd received all day.

Once the gates were open, the guard tried a desperate move — his hand lunging for his weapon, a cry of rage escaping him as he threw himself at Isidora. But she caught him by the neck before he could even finish the motion, a sharp crack ringing through the air as she tore his head off with an almost casual gesture, letting it drop to the ground without a glance.

— No more people, no more problem, isn't that the saying? she said, wiping her hand on her cape as if nothing had happened.

— That's not a saying, Lucifer answered, one eyebrow raised.

— So what? Isidora shot back with a shrug. It should've been one.

Takeshi stood frozen, staring at the guard's body slumped on the ground, his head still rolling slightly against the gravel of the drive. He brought a hand to his mouth, briefly seized by a wave of nausea.

— You... you just killed him, he said, his voice strangled. Just like that. Straight up.

— Well, yeah, Isidora answered, as if the remark made no sense. He tried to attack me. It was him or his rolling head. I chose.

Alastor stepped over the body without even giving it a glance, already walking toward the open gates.

— Right, he said, are we going in, or are we going to stand around debating moral philosophy in front of a corpse?

Isidora rang at the palace's main door, and a few moments later another guard came to open it — better equipped, stiffer, a stern expression frozen on his face.

— What is the reason for your visit? he asked in a strict, almost mechanical tone.

— Well, your colleague kindly let me in at the entrance, Isidora answered with an innocent smile, and I need to see the dumbass, uh... Sorry, I meant THE GREAT AND ALMIGHTY GENERAL DUCHON, she added with heavy irony, her voice rising theatrically on the last words.

The guard blinked, visibly not used to that kind of tone, but stepped aside without further discussion, opening the door wide and motioning them to follow.

— Follow me, he said simply, turning on his heel.

They followed him into the corridors of the palace, the gilding of the old days still visible on some walls, strangely at odds with dark banners bearing an unknown symbol that had since replaced the republican emblems. Takeshi looked all around him, a mixture of fascination and growing unease as they went along.

— What was this place before? he asked in a low voice, speaking more to Lucifer than to anyone else.

— The office of the President of the Republic, Lucifer answered with a crooked smile. Now it's General Duchon's. A matter of circumstances.

The guard led them to a massive double door, knocking twice sharply before opening it, revealing a vast office dominated by an immense dark wooden desk, behind which sat a man in uniform, his face weathered, a cold, calculating expression forming on his features as they entered.

General Duchon slowly rose from his armchair, his hands resting flat on the desk, his gaze sliding over each of the visitors in turn with calculated suspicion.

— You're very bold to walk into my office after killing one of our Boss's subordinates, he said in a calm, almost too calm voice. May I ask why?

Isidora stepped forward without the slightest hesitation, settling herself right on the edge of the desk, completely ignoring the chair provided across from him.

— Because he tried to play the hero, she answered with a casual smile. Honestly, it's his own fault, he shouldn't have been an idiot.

Duchon didn't flinch, his gaze then settling on Lucifer, a glint of recognition briefly crossing his eyes.

— The king of Hell himself, he said, a cautious respect showing in his voice. It's been a while.

— Indeed, Lucifer answered with a polite smile, but no warmth. As welcoming as ever, I see.

Duchon finally turned his attention to Takeshi, watching him with a more pronounced curiosity, as if trying to understand what a mere human was doing in such company.

— And him? he asked. What's he, the dish of the day?

— None of your business, Isidora cut in sharply, her smile vanishing instantly. What we're interested in is talking to Grand Patron Luigi. Directly.

A heavy silence settled over the room, Duchon straightening slightly, a new tension running through his shoulders.

— No one speaks directly to the Boss without a valid reason, he said cautiously. What do you want from him?

Isidora gave an innocent smile, nonchalantly swinging one leg against the edge of the desk.

— Let's say we have a tiny little request, she said. Just to go to a weird dimension with talking chairs.

Duchon stared at her for a moment, visibly unconvinced by the lightness of the phrasing, before slowly shaking his head.

— I'm going to send a message to General Captain 47 before answering you. Please wait, he said, pressing a radio unit on his desk.

A faint crackle preceded his voice, more formal, almost tense.

— Excuse me, General 47, but a group of individuals wishes to speak with Grand Patron Luigi.

Silence followed, broken only by the faint crackling of the radio. Takeshi felt his heart speed up at the name he had just heard — the very one Alastor had mentioned earlier, that "little dog with the mass-produced product name" who was anything but harmless.

— It's him, he murmured to Alastor, a hint of apprehension in his voice. Agent 47.

— Yup, Alastor confirmed, his usual smile suddenly gone more discreet, almost cautious.

Duchon raised a hand to call for silence, his eyes riveted on the radio, visibly waiting for an answer that, judging by the new tension in his shoulders, was never guaranteed to come quickly — or to be good.

A short beep sounded from the phone lying on Duchon's desk. He picked it up, his eyes quickly scanning the screen, an unreadable expression crossing his face.

— "The Boss is posted at red point, available for a meeting," he read aloud, before putting the phone down, his gaze rising back to the group with renewed caution.

— Red point? Isidora repeated, one eyebrow raised. What's that, a code name for the toilet?

— It's a code name for Mars, Duchon answered, his voice losing any possible amusement. The base there.

An icy silence settled over the room. Alastor and Lucifer exchanged a look, the same thought visibly crossing both their minds at once.

— Now that, Lucifer said slowly, is exactly the kind of complication I didn't need today.

Takeshi, feeling the tension go up a notch, looked from one face to another around him.

— Wait, he said. That means we have to go to Mars? Like, the base you were both saying it was suicide to go near?

Duchon gave a thin smile, almost amused by the situation.

— If the Boss wants to see you there, he said, either he's in a generous mood, or he really wants to see how you'll die trying to get in. Either way — good luck.

They followed Duchon through the corridors to an inner courtyard of the Élysée, where a small ship — barely bigger than a car, its dark, smooth hull reflecting no light — had just landed without the slightest sound.

— There's your taxi, Duchon announced with a thin smile, stepping aside to let them board. Have a nice trip.

They crammed inside, the cabin roomier than it looked from the outside, and the ship took off almost immediately, a brutal acceleration pinning Takeshi to his seat as Earth shrank behind the porthole at a speed that had nothing natural about it.

Isidora, for her part, didn't seem the least bit bothered by the trip, her phone already in hand, posting story after story with a string of hashtags scrolling under her nimble thumbs.

— #RoadTripMars #WereAllGonnaDie #Family, she muttered, filming the inside of the ship, briefly turning the camera toward Takeshi, who raised a hand to hide his face.
