Lucifer, walking beside them with royal nonchalance, as if the entire Parisian traffic simply didn't exist for him, let out a short laugh. — Welcome to Earth, kid, he told Takeshi. You'll quickly figure out that nobody in this group really has a sense of priorities. They eventually reached the sidewalk, leaving behind them a concert of horns and insults that didn't seem to bother anyone in the group at all, except Takeshi, who turned back toward the road one last time, a mixture of embarrassment and disbelief painted on his face. The same man suddenly reappeared, disheveled, out of his car, screaming across the street and pointing at them. — MY WIFE DIED BECAUSE OF YOU, YOU FILTHY BITCH! Isidora stopped dead in the middle of the crosswalk, turning toward him with a delighted smile, as if that accusation had just made her entire day. — If you'd kept your libido in check and put away your tiny sausage, she'd still be alive, she answered with a smirk, before resuming her walk across the street with a deliberately provocative slowness, taking all the time in the world despite the cars already starting to honk around her again. The man stood frozen on the sidewalk, mouth open, unable to come up with a comeback to such a level of audacity, while Lucifer burst out laughing behind them, one hand pressed against his stomach. — Now that, he said between bursts of laughter, is high art, Isidora. High art. Takeshi hurried to catch up with the group, casting a nervous glance back at the man still planted in the middle of the street. — Isn't what we're doing supposed to be discreet? he asked, a hint of exasperation in his voice. We're supposed to not get spotted, right? — Little human, Alastor answered with an amused smile, we're in the middle of Paris with the king of Hell, a witch of the Void, and a demon older than most known civilizations. It's a little late to think about discretion. The group finally stopped in front of the gates of the Élysée, the imposing facade of the palace rising before them, guards standing frozen on either side of the main entrance. — Here we are at the Paradise of getting screwed, Isidora announced with a theatrical gesture toward the building. Where all the decisions got made, especially about the fucking taxes. Now Macron scrubs the floor for Grand Patron Luigi's general, who took command of the Élysée exactly seven years, four months, five weeks, five days, seventeen hours, thirty-seven minutes and forty-seven seconds ago. Forty-nine now. Takeshi blinked, trying his best to keep up. — How do you know that? he asked. — Dunno, I made it up, Isidora answered with a perfectly relaxed shrug. But Macron really does clean the floor with his tongue. Takeshi turned his head toward the palace entrance, and indeed, through the gates, you could make out a figure kneeling on the marble floor, methodically licking it under the indifferent gaze of two soldiers in dark armor posted nearby. — Is that... is that really him? Takeshi asked, his voice strangled by a mixture of disgust and disbelief. — Yup, Lucifer confirmed, watching the scene with almost jaded detachment. It's been like that for years. Grand Patron Luigi likes to humiliate the people who had power before him. A matter of principle, I suppose. Alastor, for his part, stayed silent, his eyes scanning the surroundings with a new attention, more serious than usual. — Right, he said finally, we're here. Now we need to figure out how to get in without getting torn to shreds by security. Isidora walked up to one of the guards posted in front of the gates, a predatory smile already stretching across her lips. — Hey you, ugly mug, come here for two seconds, please. The guard stiffened, turning his head toward her with a suspicious expression. — Ma'am, this is the private property of General Duchon, he said in a curt, almost mechanical tone. Isidora burst out laughing, a loud sound that echoed all the way back into the street behind them. — Holy shit, Lulu, we found someone who's almost as much of a moron as you, she called over her shoulder. — Always a pleasure, Lucifer answered flatly, clearly not offended in the slightest. Isidora turned her attention back to the guard, her smile gradually fading into something sharper, almost threatening. — Anyway, she said, we need to talk to General My-Ass in there. So open the door, or I'll open your skull, and the door too while I'm at it. The guard hesitated, his hand instinctively sliding toward the weapon at his belt, his eyes seeking support from his colleague a few meters away — but the latter stayed frozen, visibly just as uneasy facing the little group standing before the gates. — I... I have to check with my superiors, he finally stammered, his voice losing its initial confidence. Takeshi, hanging back, watched the scene with growing tension, casting a nervous glance at Alastor. — This is really going to end badly, isn't it? he murmured. — Oh, very likely, Alastor answered with a delighted smile, making not the slightest effort to reassure him. A dark flash burst from Isidora's hand, an invisible force brutally slamming the guard's head against the metal gate, his helmet banging against the bars with a dull thud. The man let out a strangled cry, his hands thrashing against a grip he couldn't even see. — Listen to me carefully, you dried-up ballsack, said Isidora, her voice suddenly deeper, stripped of all the lightness she had shown until then. Either you open the door, or we're going to have a problem. And believe me — ask that shithead who passes for the king of Hell — to keep going, I won't hesitate to burn off your ball hair and make you eat it, and then make you eat your own shit. So you have exactly five seconds. — That's true, Lucifer confirmed with a nonchalant shrug, as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world. She's done worse to gods, so imagine what she can do to you. The guard, his face crushed against the gate, let out a panicked whimper, his eyes rolling frantically toward his colleague, who took a step back, visibly unwilling to intervene. — Five, Isidora began, a nasty smile stretching across her lips. — Okay, okay! the guard cried, his voice choked with panic. I'll open it, I'll open it, let me go! Isidora released her grip with a careless gesture, the guard nearly collapsing to the ground, gasping, before rushing to the control panel to open the gates, his hands shaking so hard he missed the button twice before finally hitting it. Takeshi watched the scene, a mixture of horror and morbid fascination painted on his face, as the massive gates slowly began to open before them with a metallic creak. — You're really terrifying, he murmured, more to himself than to anyone else. — Thank you, Isidora answered with a radiant smile, as if it were the nicest compliment she'd received all day. Once the gates were open, the guard tried a desperate move — his hand lunging for his weapon, a cry of rage escaping him as he threw himself at Isidora. But she caught him by the neck before he could even finish the motion, a sharp crack ringing through the air as she tore his head off with an almost casual gesture, letting it drop to the ground without a glance. — No more people, no more problem, isn't that the saying? she said, wiping her hand on her cape as if nothing had happened. — That's not a saying, Lucifer answered, one eyebrow raised. — So what? Isidora shot back with a shrug. It should've been one. Takeshi stood frozen, staring at the guard's body slumped on the ground, his head still rolling slightly against the gravel of the drive. He brought a hand to his mouth, briefly seized by a wave of nausea. — You... you just killed him, he said, his voice strangled. Just like that. Straight up. — Well, yeah, Isidora answered, as if the remark made no sense. He tried to attack me. It was him or his rolling head. I chose. Alastor stepped over the body without even giving it a glance, already walking toward the open gates. — Right, he said, are we going in, or are we going to stand around debating moral philosophy in front of a corpse? Isidora rang at the palace's main door, and a few moments later another guard came to open it — better equipped, stiffer, a stern expression frozen on his face. — What is the reason for your visit? he asked in a strict, almost mechanical tone. — Well, your colleague kindly let me in at the entrance, Isidora answered with an innocent smile, and I need to see the dumbass, uh... Sorry, I meant THE GREAT AND ALMIGHTY GENERAL DUCHON, she added with heavy irony, her voice rising theatrically on the last words. The guard blinked, visibly not used to that kind of tone, but stepped aside without further discussion, opening the door wide and motioning them to follow. — Follow me, he said simply, turning on his heel. They followed him into the corridors of the palace, the gilding of the old days still visible on some walls, strangely at odds with dark banners bearing an unknown symbol that had since replaced the republican emblems. Takeshi looked all around him, a mixture of fascination and growing unease as they went along. — What was this place before? he asked in a low voice, speaking more to Lucifer than to anyone else. — The office of the President of the Republic, Lucifer answered with a crooked smile. Now it's General Duchon's. A matter of circumstances. The guard led them to a massive double door, knocking twice sharply before opening it, revealing a vast office dominated by an immense dark wooden desk, behind which sat a man in uniform, his face weathered, a cold, calculating expression forming on his features as they entered. General Duchon slowly rose from his armchair, his hands resting flat on the desk, his gaze sliding over each of the visitors in turn with calculated suspicion. — You're very bold to walk into my office after killing one of our Boss's subordinates, he said in a calm, almost too calm voice. May I ask why? Isidora stepped forward without the slightest hesitation, settling herself right on the edge of the desk, completely ignoring the chair provided across from him. — Because he tried to play the hero, she answered with a casual smile. Honestly, it's his own fault, he shouldn't have been an idiot. Duchon didn't flinch, his gaze then settling on Lucifer, a glint of recognition briefly crossing his eyes. — The king of Hell himself, he said, a cautious respect showing in his voice. It's been a while. — Indeed, Lucifer answered with a polite smile, but no warmth. As welcoming as ever, I see. Duchon finally turned his attention to Takeshi, watching him with a more pronounced curiosity, as if trying to understand what a mere human was doing in such company. — And him? he asked. What's he, the dish of the day? — None of your business, Isidora cut in sharply, her smile vanishing instantly. What we're interested in is talking to Grand Patron Luigi. Directly. A heavy silence settled over the room, Duchon straightening slightly, a new tension running through his shoulders. — No one speaks directly to the Boss without a valid reason, he said cautiously. What do you want from him? Isidora gave an innocent smile, nonchalantly swinging one leg against the edge of the desk. — Let's say we have a tiny little request, she said. Just to go to a weird dimension with talking chairs. Duchon stared at her for a moment, visibly unconvinced by the lightness of the phrasing, before slowly shaking his head. — I'm going to send a message to General Captain 47 before answering you. Please wait, he said, pressing a radio unit on his desk. A faint crackle preceded his voice, more formal, almost tense. — Excuse me, General 47, but a group of individuals wishes to speak with Grand Patron Luigi. Silence followed, broken only by the faint crackling of the radio. Takeshi felt his heart speed up at the name he had just heard — the very one Alastor had mentioned earlier, that "little dog with the mass-produced product name" who was anything but harmless. — It's him, he murmured to Alastor, a hint of apprehension in his voice. Agent 47. — Yup, Alastor confirmed, his usual smile suddenly gone more discreet, almost cautious. Duchon raised a hand to call for silence, his eyes riveted on the radio, visibly waiting for an answer that, judging by the new tension in his shoulders, was never guaranteed to come quickly — or to be good. A short beep sounded from the phone lying on Duchon's desk. He picked it up, his eyes quickly scanning the screen, an unreadable expression crossing his face. — "The Boss is posted at red point, available for a meeting," he read aloud, before putting the phone down, his gaze rising back to the group with renewed caution. — Red point? Isidora repeated, one eyebrow raised. What's that, a code name for the toilet? — It's a code name for Mars, Duchon answered, his voice losing any possible amusement. The base there. An icy silence settled over the room. Alastor and Lucifer exchanged a look, the same thought visibly crossing both their minds at once. — Now that, Lucifer said slowly, is exactly the kind of complication I didn't need today. Takeshi, feeling the tension go up a notch, looked from one face to another around him. — Wait, he said. That means we have to go to Mars? Like, the base you were both saying it was suicide to go near? Duchon gave a thin smile, almost amused by the situation. — If the Boss wants to see you there, he said, either he's in a generous mood, or he really wants to see how you'll die trying to get in. Either way — good luck. They followed Duchon through the corridors to an inner courtyard of the Élysée, where a small ship — barely bigger than a car, its dark, smooth hull reflecting no light — had just landed without the slightest sound. — There's your taxi, Duchon announced with a thin smile, stepping aside to let them board. Have a nice trip. They crammed inside, the cabin roomier than it looked from the outside, and the ship took off almost immediately, a brutal acceleration pinning Takeshi to his seat as Earth shrank behind the porthole at a speed that had nothing natural about it. Isidora, for her part, didn't seem the least bit bothered by the trip, her phone already in hand, posting story after story with a string of hashtags scrolling under her nimble thumbs. — #RoadTripMars #WereAllGonnaDie #Family, she muttered, filming the inside of the ship, briefly turning the camera toward Takeshi, who raised a hand to hide his face.

codex-t1-c8.title: Chapter 8 — Nothing More Ordinary Than a Planetary Road Trip
codex-t1-c8.html:
The trip lasted barely a few minutes — just long enough to cross distances that, in any human ship, would have taken months. The ship touched down with a slight jolt in front of a massive door carved right into the red rock, and they had barely stepped off before it took off again instantly, vanishing into the dusty sky without a word of goodbye.

Fifteen guards sprang up immediately, surrounding the little group, their rifles — of a strange shape, their barrels gleaming with an unsettling bluish light — trained on them with flawless military precision.

— State the reason for your visit! one of them barked, his finger on the trigger. Immediately!

Takeshi instinctively raised his hands, his heart pounding wildly, while Isidora simply put her phone away calmly, a smile still hanging on her lips in the face of the barrels aimed at her.

— We have an appointment with your boss, she said with perfect nonchalance. Red point, ring a bell?

The guards stepped aside, lowering their weapons in an almost mechanical, synchronized movement, and the massive door opened onto an interior that contrasted violently with the reddish aridity of the Martian surface. Metal corridors stretched as far as the eye could see, lit by a cold white light. Dozens of soldiers stood at attention along the walls, some visibly human, others clearly modified — overdeveloped muscles, skin almost translucent in places. Robots patrolled among them, silent, their joints making barely a mechanical hiss. Farther off, stooped, gaunt figures pushed carts or dragged crates without ever raising their eyes — slaves, Takeshi understood with a shiver.

At the center of this organized ballet, a figure was already waiting for them, motionless, as if time itself had stopped around him.

Agent 47.

A perfectly tailored black suit, a blood-red tie, immaculate white gloves in stark contrast with the silenced pistol he held casually in one hand, barrel pointed at the floor. His face betrayed absolutely nothing — no surprise, no suspicion, not the slightest trace of emotion at the arrival of a king of Hell, a witch of the Void, an ancient demon, and a visibly terrified human.

— Follow me, he said in a perfectly neutral, almost monotone voice. The Boss is in the laboratory.

He turned on his heel without waiting for an answer, his footsteps echoing with almost hypnotic regularity on the metal floor. Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, unable to tear his eyes from this figure who, he now knew, had once survived a shot from the White Death himself.

— That's... that's him, he murmured to Alastor. The God of Death.

— Yup, Alastor confirmed in a low voice, his usual smile completely gone for the first time since they had met. And believe me, little human, now's the time to shut your mouth and walk.

Isidora put her phone away for good, her offhand air fading in turn, an unusual seriousness settling on her features as she fell into step behind Agent 47, followed closely by Lucifer, whose usual smile had also disappeared.

The group went deeper into the corridors of the base in silence, every guard, every robot, every slave they passed instinctively stepping aside as they went by — not out of respect, Takeshi understood, but out of a learned caution, the kind you reserve for what was walking in front: a man who had never missed a target.

The corridors stretched on, deeper and deeper, the air gradually filling with an acrid smell — chemical, almost burned. Screams rang out intermittently behind some closed doors, muffled, long, sometimes punctuated by an even more unsettling silence. Takeshi kept his eyes fixed straight ahead, no longer even daring to glance at the doors those sounds came from, his throat too tight to ask a single question.

Agent 47 guided them without a word, his stride always perfectly even, until they finally came out into a vast room lit by a harsh white light, packed with machines, holographic screens and tanks filled with liquids of improbable colors.

Grand Patron Luigi stood in the middle of the room, a phone in his hand, taking photos of various installations with almost childish enthusiasm, while two men in white coats — the famous German scientists — directed a dozen technicians busily working at several stations at once, trading technical terms at a speed and in a jargon Takeshi didn't understand at all.

— No, no, put the stabilizer on the left, one of the scientists was saying urgently, otherwise the resonance frequency will throw the whole quantum field out of sync again.

— We said seventeen point three, not eighteen, the other barked at a technician who was hastily adjusting a dial.

Agent 47 stopped a few meters from Grand Patron Luigi, standing back, silent, visibly waiting for his boss to notice their presence on his own rather than interrupting him.

Takeshi watched the scene, completely overwhelmed by the scale of what he was seeing — technology beyond anything he could have imagined possible, machines softly humming around them, and at the center of it all, this seemingly ordinary man who, with a single word, could wipe entire realities out of existence.

Grand Patron Luigi raised a finger without even turning around, his eyes still riveted on his screen.

— Hold on, 47, I'm posting on Insta, then we can get started, he said, his thumb rapidly scrolling through a series of hashtags.

He tapped the screen one last time, a faint beep confirming the post, before finally putting the phone in his pocket with visible satisfaction.

Isidora, for her part, had already moved closer, a sudden interest replacing her outward seriousness.

— Wait, what's your account? she asked, pulling her own phone out again. I've gotta follow, no question.

Grand Patron Luigi finally turned toward them, a perfectly rehearsed salesman's smile spreading across his face, as if he had been waiting for that question from the start.

— @GrandPatronLuigiOfficiel, he said proudly. Six billion followers on every platform, you can't miss it.

— Oh yeah, I didn't recognize you without the filter, Isidora answered, already typing the name, a little laugh escaping her.

He burst out laughing in turn, a loud and strangely warm laugh for someone whose cosmic reputation came down to an incalculable body count, before finally turning his attention to the whole group, his gaze lingering a moment longer on Takeshi, a glint of curiosity passing through his eyes.

— Well, he said, spreading his arms, satisfied, so we've got some fine company coming all the way to my place. What can I do for you, my little ones?

Isidora stepped forward, regaining her usual composure despite the heavy aura reigning in the room.

— Actually, she said, we need your help to go to a weird dimension where everything that doesn't exist exists. Like Lucifer's fashion sense. But even there, that's probably nonexistent.

— Hey, Lucifer protested without much conviction, clearly used to that kind of jab.

Grand Patron Luigi let out a little smirk, his arms slowly crossing, a calculating interest gradually replacing his salesman's smile.

— I suppose you want to find something, he said, besides the king of Hell's charisma, which is indeed nonexistent. What do you want?

Isidora exchanged a brief look with Lucifer, then with Alastor, before answering, her tone becoming a little more serious.

— The Dimension of Shadows, she said. We know 81 is locked up there. And maybe also my nephew's father, here, she added, nodding toward Takeshi.

Grand Patron Luigi's smile vanished instantly at the mention of the name, a heavy silence settling over the laboratory, the scientists themselves pausing their work, as if the air had suddenly become charged with a palpable tension.

— 81, he repeated slowly, his gaze hardening. Do you even know what you're asking?

Agent 47, who had stayed silent in the background until then, turned his head slightly toward his boss, the only perceptible reaction from him since their arrival.

Grand Patron Luigi's smirk reappeared at once, as quickly as it had vanished, an amused glint crossing his eyes.

— Nah, just kidding, relax, he said, waving a casual hand. I can give you something to get there if you want. Well, give you a solution. So I'll keep it short: basically, I own a star that I created. Actually it's a black star, and it's a portal to that very dimension. So you just have to go inside it.

A stunned silence greeted this announcement, Isidora herself left speechless for a moment before regaining her composure.

— Wait, seriously? she said. I spent months looking for a way into that dimension, and you're just telling me "yeah, I've got a star for that, no biggie"?

— Well, yeah, Grand Patron Luigi answered with a shrug, as if the remark made no sense. I've got stuff everywhere. Keep up.

Lucifer, who had stayed silent until then, frowned, suspicion clearly showing in his voice.

— And why would you help us, just like that, for free? he asked. That's not exactly your style.

Grand Patron Luigi's smile grew even wider, almost delighted to finally be asked the question he had been waiting for.

— Ah, he said, pointing at Lucifer. Now that's a good question. Because no, obviously, it's not free.

He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his announcement, before going on, his gaze sliding toward Takeshi with renewed interest.

— I have a little favor to ask of you in return. Nothing too nasty. Well, depends who you ask.

Grand Patron Luigi spread his arms, a radiant smile spreading across his face, as if he were about to announce the most important revelation of the day.

— All I want, he said, is for each of you to follow my accounts. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X. All four. That's not much to ask, is it?

A stunned silence once again greeted this statement, Takeshi blinking, unable to tell whether the man was serious.

— That's... that's your condition? he asked finally. To access a cosmic dimension that erases everything forgotten? An Instagram follow?

— And TikTok, Grand Patron Luigi specified, raising a finger. And YouTube. And X. All four, I said.

Isidora already had her phone in hand, typing frantically.

— Oh, that's been done for like ten minutes, she said with a satisfied smile, turning the screen toward him to prove it.

Lucifer sighed long and hard, pulling out his own phone with a clearly reluctant slowness.

— I have never hated my life as much as I do right now, he muttered, looking for the app.

Alastor, for his part, burst out laughing, a sincere sound that contrasted with the tension built up since their arrival on Mars.

— Honestly, he said, complying in turn, it's the simplest deal we've ever gotten from a cosmic lunatic. I'm not gonna complain.

Grand Patron Luigi watched the scene with obvious satisfaction, almost counting out loud the new follower notifications popping up on his own phone.

— And there we go, he said at last, putting the phone away. Follow 47, he'll show you the star. And be careful going in there, okay — I've never tested it on living beings, so you're the guinea pigs.

Agent 47 started moving again without a word, turning on his heel with that same mechanical regularity that never seemed to leave him. The group followed him through a new series of corridors, deeper still, the white lighting gradually giving way to a dimmer, almost bluish light, while the hum of the machines grew louder the farther they went.

Takeshi, walking at the back, glanced at Alastor.

— "I've never tested it on living beings," he repeated in a low voice, a hint of panic in his voice. He really said that, right? I didn't dream it?

— No, you didn't dream it, Alastor confirmed with a smile that was anything but reassuring.

— And nobody finds that worrying? Takeshi pressed, glancing at Isidora and Lucifer walking ahead, apparently not the least bit bothered.

— Little human, Alastor answered, you've already died once today. At this point, a second time wouldn't change much about your day.

They finally came out into an immense circular hall, its center occupied by a massive structure, a metal ring surrounding a control point where several technicians were already at work, alerted by their arrival. Agent 47 stopped dead in front of the ring, finally turning toward them, his face still devoid of the slightest expression.

— The black star is stored inside this ring, in compressed form, he said, his voice as neutral as if he were reciting a technical manual. Once activated, it will generate a direct access. You will have thirty seconds to enter before the contact point closes.

Isidora walked up to the ring, whistling softly in admiration as she looked over the structure.

— Thirty seconds, she repeated. Nice margin for error.

— It's already more than the Boss originally planned, 47 answered without the slightest perceptible trace of irony.

Lucifer stepped forward in turn, his eyes scanning the ring with obvious suspicion.

— And once we're on the other side, he said, do we have any idea what's waiting for us?

— No, 47 answered simply. No data exists on the interior of the Dimension of Shadows.

The silence that followed this answer weighed heavily on the little group, everyone exchanging a look that betrayed, for the first time since their arrival on Mars, a shared worry.

What can I do for you, my little ones? Isidora stepped forward, regaining her usual composure despite the heavy aura reigning in the room. — Actually, she said, we need your help to go to a weird dimension where everything that doesn't exist exists. Like Lucifer's fashion sense. But even there, that's probably nonexistent. — Hey, Lucifer protested without much conviction, clearly used to that kind of jab. Grand Patron Luigi let out a little smirk, his arms slowly crossing, a calculating interest gradually replacing his salesman's smile. — I suppose you want to find something, he said, besides the king of Hell's charisma, which is indeed nonexistent. What do you want? Isidora exchanged a brief look with Lucifer, then with Alastor, before answering, her tone becoming a little more serious. — The Dimension of Shadows, she said. We know 81 is locked up there. And maybe also my nephew's father, here, she added, nodding toward Takeshi. Grand Patron Luigi's smile vanished instantly at the mention of the name, a heavy silence settling over the laboratory, the scientists themselves pausing their work, as if the air had suddenly become charged with a palpable tension. — 81, he repeated slowly, his gaze hardening. Do you even know what you're asking? Agent 47, who had stayed silent in the background until then, turned his head slightly toward his boss, the only perceptible reaction from him since their arrival. Grand Patron Luigi's smirk reappeared at once, as quickly as it had vanished, an amused glint crossing his eyes. — Nah, just kidding, relax, he said, waving a casual hand. I can give you something to get there if you want. Well, give you a solution. So I'll keep it short: basically, I own a star that I created. Actually it's a black star, and it's a portal to that very dimension. So you just have to go inside it. A stunned silence greeted this announcement, Isidora herself left speechless for a moment before regaining her composure. — Wait, seriously? she said. I spent months looking for a way into that dimension, and you're just telling me "yeah, I've got a star for that, no biggie"? — Well, yeah, Grand Patron Luigi answered with a shrug, as if the remark made no sense. I've got stuff everywhere. Keep up. Lucifer, who had stayed silent until then, frowned, suspicion clearly showing in his voice. — And why would you help us, just like that, for free? he asked. That's not exactly your style. Grand Patron Luigi's smile grew even wider, almost delighted to finally be asked the question he had been waiting for. — Ah, he said, pointing at Lucifer. Now that's a good question. Because no, obviously, it's not free. He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his announcement, before going on, his gaze sliding toward Takeshi with renewed interest. — I have a little favor to ask of you in return. Nothing too nasty. Well, depends who you ask. Grand Patron Luigi spread his arms, a radiant smile spreading across his face, as if he were about to announce the most important revelation of the day. — All I want, he said, is for each of you to follow my accounts. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X. All four. That's not much to ask, is it? A stunned silence once again greeted this statement, Takeshi blinking, unable to tell whether the man was serious. — That's... that's your condition? he asked finally. To access a cosmic dimension that erases everything forgotten? An Instagram follow? — And TikTok, Grand Patron Luigi specified, raising a finger. And YouTube. And X. All four, I said. Isidora already had her phone in hand, typing frantically. — Oh, that's been done for like ten minutes, she said with a satisfied smile, turning the screen toward him to prove it. Lucifer sighed long and hard, pulling out his own phone with a clearly reluctant slowness. — I have never hated my life as much as I do right now, he muttered, looking for the app. Alastor, for his part, burst out laughing, a sincere sound that contrasted with the tension built up since their arrival on Mars. — Honestly, he said, complying in turn, it's the simplest deal we've ever gotten from a cosmic lunatic. I'm not gonna complain. Grand Patron Luigi watched the scene with obvious satisfaction, almost counting out loud the new follower notifications popping up on his own phone. — And there we go, he said at last, putting the phone away. Follow 47, he'll show you the star. And be careful going in there, okay — I've never tested it on living beings, so you're the guinea pigs. Agent 47 started moving again without a word, turning on his heel with that same mechanical regularity that never seemed to leave him. The group followed him through a new series of corridors, deeper still, the white lighting gradually giving way to a dimmer, almost bluish light, while the hum of the machines grew louder the farther they went. Takeshi, walking at the back, glanced at Alastor. — "I've never tested it on living beings," he repeated in a low voice, a hint of panic in his voice. He really said that, right? I didn't dream it? — No, you didn't dream it, Alastor confirmed with a smile that was anything but reassuring. — And nobody finds that worrying? Takeshi pressed, glancing at Isidora and Lucifer walking ahead, apparently not the least bit bothered. — Little human, Alastor answered, you've already died once today. At this point, a second time wouldn't change much about your day. They finally came out into an immense circular hall, its center occupied by a massive structure, a metal ring surrounding a control point where several technicians were already at work, alerted by their arrival. Agent 47 stopped dead in front of the ring, finally turning toward them, his face still devoid of the slightest expression. — The black star is stored inside this ring, in compressed form, he said, his voice as neutral as if he were reciting a technical manual. Once activated, it will generate a direct access. You will have thirty seconds to enter before the contact point closes. Isidora walked up to the ring, whistling softly in admiration as she looked over the structure. — Thirty seconds, she repeated. Nice margin for error. — It's already more than the Boss originally planned, 47 answered without the slightest perceptible trace of irony. Lucifer stepped forward in turn, his eyes scanning the ring with obvious suspicion. — And once we're on the other side, he said, do we have any idea what's waiting for us? — No, 47 answered simply. No data exists on the interior of the Dimension of Shadows. The silence that followed this answer weighed heavily on the little group, everyone exchanging a look that betrayed, for the first time since their arrival on Mars, a shared worry.

codex-t1-c9.title: Chapter 9 — Full of Bullshit!
codex-t1-c9.html:
Agent 47 activated a mechanism on the control panel, and the metal ring began to vibrate, a deep hum rapidly intensifying until it became almost unbearable. At its center, the air tore open, revealing a sphere so deeply black that it seemed to suck in the light of the entire room.

— Thirty seconds, 47 repeated. Now.

Without another word, Isidora was the first to leap in, followed closely by Lucifer, then Alastor, dragging Takeshi along with a firm grip. The sensation of crossing over was different from all the previous ones — an absolute void, with no direction, no up or down, as if their very existence had been momentarily suspended between two realities.

Then, as abruptly as the passage had begun, they emerged on the other side.

Takeshi immediately felt his feet sink into something cold and liquid — a thin film of water, barely a few centimeters deep, covering a ground he couldn't clearly identify, neither stone nor earth, something in between, that almost rippled under his steps as if it weren't entirely solid.

Above them, the sky — if you could still call it a sky — was nothing but a black gloom, without stars, without clouds, without the slightest identifiable source of light, and yet they could see everything clearly, as if light itself no longer really made sense here. Shapes crossed that darkness intermittently — blurry, indescribable silhouettes, some vaguely resembling objects, others creatures, still others nothing recognizable at all, gliding silently through the void without ever seeming to have any particular direction.

Takeshi turned in place, desperately searching for a horizon, a boundary, anything that would show where this place ended — but there was nothing. No beginning, no end. Just that expanse of shallow water stretching as far as the eye could see in every direction, under that sky of darkness peopled with forgotten things.

— What... what is all this? he murmured, his voice echoing strangely, as if absorbed by the surrounding void before it even fully reached his own ears.

Isidora, for her part, stood motionless, watching the shapes float above them with an expression he had never seen on her before — something that looked, for the first time, like sincere worry.

— The Dimension of Shadows, she said softly. We're here.

Isidora took out her phone, the screen lighting up in the surrounding darkness — then her face fell slightly.

— Wait, there's no signal here?! she exclaimed, waving the phone around as if that would magically make a signal bar appear. Like, I got signal IN HELL, but not here?!

She tapped frantically at the screen, turning in circles in search of a phantom signal, her look of utter disaster contrasting violently with the gravity of the place.

— This is a joke, she said. How am I supposed to post a story if there's no signal? That's the worst part of this dimension. NO SIGNAL!

Lucifer, standing back, rolled his eyes up to the sky — well, to what passed for one.

— We've just entered a dimension where everything the entire universe has forgotten ends up disappearing, he said, and your one concern is your Instagram account.

— My priorities are clear, yes, Isidora answered without the slightest embarrassment, finally tucking the phone into a fold of her cape with a disappointed sigh. Fine. Whatever. I'll catch up later. "Sorry guys, I was stuck in the absolute void, milk milk lemonade."

Alastor let out a dry little laugh, while Takeshi stayed frozen, his eyes relentlessly sweeping the infinite expanse around them, a chilling certainty gradually settling in him that here, in this place with no beginning and no end, finding anything at all — 81, his father, or even simply the way back — was going to prove much harder than expected.

Isidora slowly turned in place, scanning the shifting darkness around them, her tone gradually becoming serious again.

— Okay, now we need to figure out where you find a god killer in an infinite dimension, she said. Because right now, look as I might, I don't really see any signposts.

— Didn't you have a little idea before coming? Lucifer asked, one eyebrow raised. Like, a plan that went further than "we go in and improvise"?

— I found the dimension, Isidora answered curtly. That was already something. What else did you want, a GPS?

Alastor, who had stayed silent until then, was carefully watching the shapes drifting above them, his eyes narrowed in concentration.

— Maybe we shouldn't try to see, he said slowly. Maybe we should try to feel. Something like 81, with all the power he's absorbed, can't just be floating in the void like everything else. It must... weigh on this place, one way or another.

Takeshi, still unsettled by the vastness of the place, ventured to speak up.

— Weigh how? he asked. Like, physically?

— Like gravity, Alastor answered. If this place keeps everything that's been forgotten, then a being as enormous as him must create some kind of point of attraction. We just need to find the direction where everything seems to... converge.

Isidora froze for a moment, a slow smile stretching across her lips.

— That, she said, is the first intelligent idea you've had since we left, Al. I'm almost proud of you.

— Almost, Alastor repeated with an ironic smile.

Lucifer closed his eyes for a moment, a focused expression crossing his face, before opening them again and slowly pointing in a direction in the darkness — a point that, at first glance, was in no way different from the rest of the surrounding void.

— There, he said. I feel something, that way. A heaviness. Like a debt that hasn't been fully paid.

The group turned toward the indicated direction, the water lapping gently around their feet as a heavy silence settled, each of them aware that the next step they took would bring them, one way or another, closer to the most dangerous being ever recorded in the two Codices.

Isidora suddenly froze, a smile lighting up her face as if a light bulb had just switched on above her head.

— Oh fuck, I know! she exclaimed. We just have to ask the magic chair!

A confused silence greeted this declaration, every eye turning to her.

— The what? asked Lucifer, one eyebrow raised so high it threatened to disappear into his hair.

— The Answer, Isidora clarified, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. That omniscient entity stashed somewhere in this dimension, that answers every question except two. It's supposed to be here, right? That's exactly what we need!

Alastor frowned, a new caution crossing his eyes.

— You sure that's a good idea? he said. Every soul only gets three questions in its entire existence. And if you ask a forbidden question — like how to defeat KJ or Grand Patron Luigi — it self-destructs on the spot.

— Well, that's exactly why we'll be careful, Isidora answered with a shrug. We just ask where 81 is. It's not exactly a trick question.

Takeshi, who had followed the exchange with growing apprehension, raised a hesitant hand.

— Wait, he said, but how do we find her? Nobody's ever managed to reach her, have they?

— No known method, Isidora confirmed, a predatory smile reappearing on her lips. But hey, we're already in a dimension that's supposed to be impossible to enter. So we might as well give it a shot.

Lucifer sighed long and hard, running a hand over his face.

— Great, he said. Yet another plan that relies entirely on total improvisation.

— Got a better idea? Isidora shot back.

The silence that followed was her only answer.

They walked in silence across the liquid expanse, the water lapping faintly around their steps, while above them shapes kept drifting through the darkness — some resembling broken objects, others fragments of words, sometimes entire sentences, vanishing as soon as they seemed to take shape.

— Look, Lulu, it's full of bullshit, kind of like your big dickhead skull, Isidora called out, pointing at a shapeless mass floating lazily above them.

— Your humor is always a pleasure, Lucifer answered without even looking up.

They kept going, the atmosphere gradually growing denser, heavier, as if the air itself — if it could still be called that here — were slowly tightening around them. Then, in the distance, a strange silhouette began to take shape: a heap of furniture, dozens, maybe hundreds of pieces, piled on top of each other, floating a few meters above the liquid ground — chairs, tables, wardrobes, some familiar, others in a style Takeshi had never seen.

— What's all this crap? asked Lucifer, slowing down.

Isidora had stopped dead, her eyes fixed on the pile of furniture with a new, almost religious intensity.

— It's here, she said simply.

— How can you be so sure? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised. It's literally a pile of forgotten furniture. It could be anything.

Isidora didn't answer right away, her eyes still riveted on the floating heap, something in her attitude having completely changed — no more sarcasm, no more nonchalance, just a quiet, inexplicable certainty.

— I don't know how to explain it to you, Al, she said finally, her voice lower than usual. But I feel it. Like something pulling at the back of my skull. It's here. The chair is here.

Takeshi, uncomfortable with this sudden change of tone in her, moved a little closer to the group.

— And how do we find it in there? he asked, gesturing at the chaotic pile of suspended furniture.

Isidora took a deep breath and stepped toward the floating heap, the water lapping gently around her feet.

— We search, she answered simply. And we pray it isn't the wrong chair.

They spread out among the heap, methodically searching through dozens of suspended pieces of furniture, pushing aside ordinary chairs, busted armchairs, wobbly tables — until Alastor, pulling on a half-collapsed chest of drawers, uncovered, nestled behind a stack of wardrobes, a chair decidedly different from all the others.

Its wood seemed both ancient and intact, without a trace of wear or dust, and on top of its backrest sat a small crystal sphere, translucent, inside which a faint, almost hypnotic glow was dancing.

— That's her, Isidora breathed, rushing forward.

She took hold of it with a care unusual for her, carrying it at arm's length to a clearer patch of the liquid ground, where she set it down delicately, then stepped back a few paces, as if the object might shatter at the slightest sudden movement.

A tense silence settled, every eye fixed on the empty chair, no one daring to make the first move.

— Well, Lucifer said finally, who asks the first question?

— Not me, Isidora answered immediately, stepping back even further. I already used my three questions centuries ago. I'm not allowed anymore.

Every eye then turned to Alastor, who immediately raised his hands in refusal.

— Oh no, count me out, he said. If I ask a lousy question and this thing blows up before we get the answer we want, I don't want it to be my fault.

Lucifer sighed, glancing resignedly at the sphere.

— And if I'm the one asking, and I make a mistake, he said, it's the king of Hell himself who burns a question. A bit more symbolic weight, isn't it?

Every eye inevitably ended up converging on Takeshi, who felt his stomach knot all at once.

— Wait, no, he said, backing away instinctively. Why me?

— You've never asked anybody a question, Isidora answered with a shrug. You've still got your three chances intact. And incidentally, it's kind of your father and your Poppy problem that got us all the way here, so...

— So what? Takeshi insisted, panic clearly showing in his voice.

— So it's kind of logical that you're the one who asks, Alastor concluded with a smile that was anything but reassuring.

Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, his eyes moving from the empty chair to the faces around him, all silent, all waiting. Then, with an almost painful slowness, he stepped toward the crystal sphere, his voice hesitant when he finally broke the silence.

— And... and what do I ask first? Where 81 is, or where my father is?

A voice suddenly rang out, calm, composed, coming from no visible mouth — seeming to emanate directly from the crystal sphere resting on the chair's backrest, vibrating in the air with a clarity strangely at odds with the heavy silence of the surrounding dimension.

— Hello, visitors, said the voice. So, you managed to come here. Not everyone can. But I believe I recognize Isidora, who came here several centuries ago.

Isidora stiffened slightly, a tense smile replacing her usual confidence.

— Yeah, it's been a while, she answered, her voice losing a little of its customary composure.

— But for the others, the voice went on, let me introduce myself. I am The Answer.

A silence settled, everyone holding their breath before this invisible entity that nevertheless seemed to be watching them all, with a precision that gave them goosebumps.

Takeshi, still motionless in front of the chair, felt his throat tighten even more.

— Do you... do you know why we're here? he asked, his voice trembling.

— I know everything there is to know, The Answer replied, in a perfectly neutral tone, neither warm nor cold. But I only answer questions asked directly. So, young Mystic — for that is indeed what you are, isn't it — ask your question. Just remember: three questions per soul, not one more. And two questions in particular will cause my immediate destruction if you ask them. Think carefully.

Takeshi took a deep breath, his hands trembling slightly as he stared at the crystal sphere.

— How do we free 81, oh great omniscient chair?

— Could you please stop sucking up to it, Isidora called from the back, a sardonic smile on her lips despite the tension in the air.

A silence followed, longer than the previous one, as if The Answer were taking the time to weigh each word before replying.

— This crystal sphere resting on me is not something that belongs to me, it said finally, its voice as neutral as ever. It was placed there. And I do believe that a soul has been training for a long time, here, in this dimension.

The group exchanged confused looks, Lucifer frowning first.

— Wait, he said, are you telling us someone else is already here? For how long?

— I do not have the answer to that precise question, The Answer replied. But the energy of this sphere does not come from me. It was placed deliberately, by a consciousness present in this dimension, capable of interacting with my structure without directly summoning me.

Takeshi felt his heart race, a lightning-fast thought crossing his mind.

— My father, he murmured. Could it be my father?

— I can neither confirm nor deny that hypothesis unless you ask the question formally, The Answer replied. Remember: your first question — how to free 81 — remains pending. Do you wish me to answer it, or would you rather rephrase it to ask instead about the identity of this presence?

Isidora stepped forward, a new urgency in her voice.

— Wait, kid, think carefully, she said. You've only got three questions. If you change your mind now, it doesn't count as used, but if you phrase it badly, you might lose your chance for good.

Takeshi clenched his fists, his decision made.

— Yes, I want to know where 81 is, he said, his voice firm despite the trembling still in his hands.

A silence settled, heavier than the previous ones, before The Answer spoke again, its voice as neutral as ever but charged with a new weight.

— This crystal sphere, it said, is the God Killer's prison.

A stunned silence fell over the entire group. Takeshi took a step back, his gaze settling with growing horror on the small translucent sphere that had been resting just above his head from the start, that faint glow dancing peacefully inside it.

— Wait, said Lucifer, his voice strangled. Are you telling us that 81 — THE 81, the one who destroyed Heaven, who devoured a billion years of gods — is stashed away in this little thing the size of a golf ball?

— The physical size of a container has no bearing on the power or the entity it holds, The Answer replied. A consciousness as vast as 81's was compressed, fragment by fragment, into this enclosed space, by the ten beings responsible for his sealing. It is not an ordinary prison. It is a prison on the scale of his soul.

Isidora had frozen, her eyes riveted on the sphere with a new intensity, a mixture of fascination and pure terror crossing her usually so offhand features.

— And that famous consciousness that's been "training" here for a while, she said slowly, you're telling me it might be the one that put this chair here. On purpose. Right next to 81's prison.

— That is a possibility I can neither confirm nor deny without a direct question, The Answer repeated.

Takeshi, still in shock, looked up at the sphere he had almost literally been holding in his hands a few moments earlier without knowing it, a chilling thought gradually forcing itself on him.

— He said it had to be put somewhere else, he murmured, turning to Isidora. You moved that chair yourself, with that thing on it. We... we literally carried his prison without knowing it.

Takeshi hesitated a split second before asking his second question, his voice more confident than before.

— How can we free him?

— To free 81, The Answer replied without the slightest delay, you just need to take this crystal sphere and break it, by throwing it on the ground, for example. But I advise you to do so on physical ground.

A stunned silence greeted this answer of almost comical simplicity, in total contrast with the cosmic scale of the entity in question.

— This is a joke, said Lucifer, his voice incredulous. Like, we've got ten super-powerful beings — including an Incarnation of Death and five Archdragons — who joined forces to seal away the most dangerous threat ever known... and all it takes is dropping it on the floor to screw everything up?

— The complexity of a seal does not necessarily lie in the fragility of its breaking point, The Answer replied, but in the difficulty of reaching it. No one before you had located this dimension, let alone this specific sphere. The simplicity of the final act in no way diminishes the difficulty of the road traveled to get there.

Isidora was already backing away instinctively, her hands raised as if to push Takeshi away from the sphere he was still holding between his fingers.

— Wait, wait, wait, she said hastily. Put that fucking ball down right now, kid. Like, right now, right now.

Takeshi looked down at the sphere he hadn't even noticed he had picked up again, a cold sweat instantly running down his spine.

— Wait, he said, his voice going up a notch, you were telling me that while I was holding it in my hands?!

— Technically, The Answer specified, as long as it is not broken on a surface dense enough to release the pressure contained inside, it remains stable. You were safe. Probably.

— "Probably"?! Takeshi repeated, panic completely overwhelming him as he knelt with exaggerated slowness to set the sphere back down on the liquid ground with the delicacy of a bomb technician defusing a bomb.

Takeshi, still shaken, slowly straightened up, taking a trembling breath before asking his last question.

— Where is my father?

— Your father is... IN THAILAND! Isidora yelled, cutting off the voice that was starting to answer.

— I will start again, The Answer said in a perfectly even tone, as if the interruption had never even happened.

— So your father is... AN ASSHOLE! Isidora shouted again, grinning from ear to ear.

— I will start again, The Answer repeated, unruffled.

— Your father... ABANDONED YOU! Isidora bellowed once more, punctuating every word with a theatrical sweep of her arm.

— SHUT UP! I WANT TO TALK! The Answer finally shouted, its voice losing every trace of neutrality for the first time since their arrival.

— SO I'M STARTING AGAAAAAIN! The Answer yelled over Isidora, visibly delighted by the chaos it was causing. YOUR FATHER IS LOCKED UP IN THE CULT OF... XAVIER DUPONT DE LIGONNÈS!

— WILL YOU SHUT YOUR MOUTH!!! The Answer retorted, the crystal sphere vibrating violently under the sudden intensity of its voice, an irritated light pulsing inside it.

A shocked silence abruptly fell again, Lucifer and Alastor doubled over, unable to hold back their laughter, while Takeshi stood open-mouthed, torn between hilarity and total dismay.

— Your father, The Answer finally went on, its voice gradually regaining its usual calm, though still tinged with perceptible annoyance, is being held by the Cult of KJ. He is still alive.

Takeshi froze, the words taking several seconds to truly sink into his mind, every trace of amusement evaporating instantly.

— He... he's alive, he murmured, his voice trembling. Are you sure?

— I am never wrong, The Answer replied. Your father is being held somewhere within the Cult of KJ, since the War of the Estrangement. That was your last question. You have now used your three questions. I can no longer answer any other, for this life.

Isidora, a smile still hanging on her lips, crossed her arms with perfect nonchalance.

— Then again, it's true he could've been in Thailand, getting his ass kneaded by some Thai girl, huh. We don't know. We don't judge.

A brief silence preceded The Answer's reply, its voice returning to an icy calm, almost threatening in its recovered neutrality.

— Isidora, it said, if I had arms, legs, charisma, strength, solidity — and not just someone else's prison to show off with — I would come and knead that bitch skull of yours.

A stunned silence greeted this retort, before Lucifer burst out laughing once again, even louder than before, almost doubling over.

— Now that, he said between hiccups, is the best thing I've heard in centuries. An ancient omniscient entity threatening to knead Isidora's skull.

Isidora, for her part, stayed open-mouthed for a moment, before a delighted smile spread across her face, visibly more impressed than insulted.

— Okay, she said, respect. I didn't think you had that in you, chair.

— I am not a chair, The Answer replied curtly. I am an omniscient consciousness forced to reside in a piece of furniture for lack of options. There is a difference.

— Yeah, yeah, said Isidora, waving a casual hand, the chair. Well, thanks for the info, anyway. Even if you nearly fried twice because of me.

Takeshi, still shaken by the revelation about his father, stayed silent, his gaze lost in the dark immensity of the dimension, a new and fragile determination slowly beginning to form behind the persistent worry that filled him.
