Alastor, who had stayed silent until then, was carefully watching the shapes drifting above them, his eyes narrowed in concentration. — Maybe we shouldn't try to see, he said slowly. Maybe we should try to feel. Something like 81, with all the power he's absorbed, can't just be floating in the void like everything else. It must... weigh on this place, one way or another. Takeshi, still unsettled by the vastness of the place, ventured to speak up. — Weigh how? he asked. Like, physically? — Like gravity, Alastor answered. If this place keeps everything that's been forgotten, then a being as enormous as him must create some kind of point of attraction. We just need to find the direction where everything seems to... converge. Isidora froze for a moment, a slow smile stretching across her lips. — That, she said, is the first intelligent idea you've had since we left, Al. I'm almost proud of you. — Almost, Alastor repeated with an ironic smile. Lucifer closed his eyes for a moment, a focused expression crossing his face, before opening them again and slowly pointing in a direction in the darkness — a point that, at first glance, was in no way different from the rest of the surrounding void. — There, he said. I feel something, that way. A heaviness. Like a debt that hasn't been fully paid. The group turned toward the indicated direction, the water lapping gently around their feet as a heavy silence settled, each of them aware that the next step they took would bring them, one way or another, closer to the most dangerous being ever recorded in the two Codices. Isidora suddenly froze, a smile lighting up her face as if a light bulb had just switched on above her head. — Oh fuck, I know! she exclaimed. We just have to ask the magic chair! A confused silence greeted this declaration, every eye turning to her. — The what? asked Lucifer, one eyebrow raised so high it threatened to disappear into his hair. — The Answer, Isidora clarified, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. That omniscient entity stashed somewhere in this dimension, that answers every question except two. It's supposed to be here, right? That's exactly what we need! Alastor frowned, a new caution crossing his eyes. — You sure that's a good idea? he said. Every soul only gets three questions in its entire existence. And if you ask a forbidden question — like how to defeat KJ or Grand Patron Luigi — it self-destructs on the spot. — Well, that's exactly why we'll be careful, Isidora answered with a shrug. We just ask where 81 is. It's not exactly a trick question. Takeshi, who had followed the exchange with growing apprehension, raised a hesitant hand. — Wait, he said, but how do we find her? Nobody's ever managed to reach her, have they? — No known method, Isidora confirmed, a predatory smile reappearing on her lips. But hey, we're already in a dimension that's supposed to be impossible to enter. So we might as well give it a shot. Lucifer sighed long and hard, running a hand over his face. — Great, he said. Yet another plan that relies entirely on total improvisation. — Got a better idea? Isidora shot back. The silence that followed was her only answer. They walked in silence across the liquid expanse, the water lapping faintly around their steps, while above them shapes kept drifting through the darkness — some resembling broken objects, others fragments of words, sometimes entire sentences, vanishing as soon as they seemed to take shape. — Look, Lulu, it's full of bullshit, kind of like your big dickhead skull, Isidora called out, pointing at a shapeless mass floating lazily above them. — Your humor is always a pleasure, Lucifer answered without even looking up. They kept going, the atmosphere gradually growing denser, heavier, as if the air itself — if it could still be called that here — were slowly tightening around them. Then, in the distance, a strange silhouette began to take shape: a heap of furniture, dozens, maybe hundreds of pieces, piled on top of each other, floating a few meters above the liquid ground — chairs, tables, wardrobes, some familiar, others in a style Takeshi had never seen. — What's all this crap? asked Lucifer, slowing down. Isidora had stopped dead, her eyes fixed on the pile of furniture with a new, almost religious intensity. — It's here, she said simply. — How can you be so sure? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised. It's literally a pile of forgotten furniture. It could be anything. Isidora didn't answer right away, her eyes still riveted on the floating heap, something in her attitude having completely changed — no more sarcasm, no more nonchalance, just a quiet, inexplicable certainty. — I don't know how to explain it to you, Al, she said finally, her voice lower than usual. But I feel it. Like something pulling at the back of my skull. It's here. The chair is here. Takeshi, uncomfortable with this sudden change of tone in her, moved a little closer to the group. — And how do we find it in there? he asked, gesturing at the chaotic pile of suspended furniture. Isidora took a deep breath and stepped toward the floating heap, the water lapping gently around her feet. — We search, she answered simply. And we pray it isn't the wrong chair. They spread out among the heap, methodically searching through dozens of suspended pieces of furniture, pushing aside ordinary chairs, busted armchairs, wobbly tables — until Alastor, pulling on a half-collapsed chest of drawers, uncovered, nestled behind a stack of wardrobes, a chair decidedly different from all the others. Its wood seemed both ancient and intact, without a trace of wear or dust, and on top of its backrest sat a small crystal sphere, translucent, inside which a faint, almost hypnotic glow was dancing. — That's her, Isidora breathed, rushing forward. She took hold of it with a care unusual for her, carrying it at arm's length to a clearer patch of the liquid ground, where she set it down delicately, then stepped back a few paces, as if the object might shatter at the slightest sudden movement. A tense silence settled, every eye fixed on the empty chair, no one daring to make the first move. — Well, Lucifer said finally, who asks the first question? — Not me, Isidora answered immediately, stepping back even further. I already used my three questions centuries ago. I'm not allowed anymore. Every eye then turned to Alastor, who immediately raised his hands in refusal. — Oh no, count me out, he said. If I ask a lousy question and this thing blows up before we get the answer we want, I don't want it to be my fault. Lucifer sighed, glancing resignedly at the sphere. — And if I'm the one asking, and I make a mistake, he said, it's the king of Hell himself who burns a question. A bit more symbolic weight, isn't it? Every eye inevitably ended up converging on Takeshi, who felt his stomach knot all at once. — Wait, no, he said, backing away instinctively. Why me? — You've never asked anybody a question, Isidora answered with a shrug. You've still got your three chances intact. And incidentally, it's kind of your father and your Poppy problem that got us all the way here, so... — So what? Takeshi insisted, panic clearly showing in his voice. — So it's kind of logical that you're the one who asks, Alastor concluded with a smile that was anything but reassuring. Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, his eyes moving from the empty chair to the faces around him, all silent, all waiting. Then, with an almost painful slowness, he stepped toward the crystal sphere, his voice hesitant when he finally broke the silence. — And... and what do I ask first? Where 81 is, or where my father is? A voice suddenly rang out, calm, composed, coming from no visible mouth — seeming to emanate directly from the crystal sphere resting on the chair's backrest, vibrating in the air with a clarity strangely at odds with the heavy silence of the surrounding dimension. — Hello, visitors, said the voice. So, you managed to come here. Not everyone can. But I believe I recognize Isidora, who came here several centuries ago. Isidora stiffened slightly, a tense smile replacing her usual confidence. — Yeah, it's been a while, she answered, her voice losing a little of its customary composure. — But for the others, the voice went on, let me introduce myself. I am The Answer. A silence settled, everyone holding their breath before this invisible entity that nevertheless seemed to be watching them all, with a precision that gave them goosebumps. Takeshi, still motionless in front of the chair, felt his throat tighten even more. — Do you... do you know why we're here? he asked, his voice trembling. — I know everything there is to know, The Answer replied, in a perfectly neutral tone, neither warm nor cold. But I only answer questions asked directly. So, young Mystic — for that is indeed what you are, isn't it — ask your question. Just remember: three questions per soul, not one more. And two questions in particular will cause my immediate destruction if you ask them. Think carefully. Takeshi took a deep breath, his hands trembling slightly as he stared at the crystal sphere. — How do we free 81, oh great omniscient chair? — Could you please stop sucking up to it, Isidora called from the back, a sardonic smile on her lips despite the tension in the air. A silence followed, longer than the previous one, as if The Answer were taking the time to weigh each word before replying. — This crystal sphere resting on me is not something that belongs to me, it said finally, its voice as neutral as ever. It was placed there. And I do believe that a soul has been training for a long time, here, in this dimension. The group exchanged confused looks, Lucifer frowning first. — Wait, he said, are you telling us someone else is already here? For how long? — I do not have the answer to that precise question, The Answer replied. But the energy of this sphere does not come from me. It was placed deliberately, by a consciousness present in this dimension, capable of interacting with my structure without directly summoning me. Takeshi felt his heart race, a lightning-fast thought crossing his mind. — My father, he murmured. Could it be my father? — I can neither confirm nor deny that hypothesis unless you ask the question formally, The Answer replied. Remember: your first question — how to free 81 — remains pending. Do you wish me to answer it, or would you rather rephrase it to ask instead about the identity of this presence? Isidora stepped forward, a new urgency in her voice. — Wait, kid, think carefully, she said. You've only got three questions. If you change your mind now, it doesn't count as used, but if you phrase it badly, you might lose your chance for good. Takeshi clenched his fists, his decision made. — Yes, I want to know where 81 is, he said, his voice firm despite the trembling still in his hands. A silence settled, heavier than the previous ones, before The Answer spoke again, its voice as neutral as ever but charged with a new weight. — This crystal sphere, it said, is the God Killer's prison. A stunned silence fell over the entire group. Takeshi took a step back, his gaze settling with growing horror on the small translucent sphere that had been resting just above his head from the start, that faint glow dancing peacefully inside it. — Wait, said Lucifer, his voice strangled. Are you telling us that 81 — THE 81, the one who destroyed Heaven, who devoured a billion years of gods — is stashed away in this little thing the size of a golf ball? — The physical size of a container has no bearing on the power or the entity it holds, The Answer replied. A consciousness as vast as 81's was compressed, fragment by fragment, into this enclosed space, by the ten beings responsible for his sealing. It is not an ordinary prison. It is a prison on the scale of his soul. Isidora had frozen, her eyes riveted on the sphere with a new intensity, a mixture of fascination and pure terror crossing her usually so offhand features. — And that famous consciousness that's been "training" here for a while, she said slowly, you're telling me it might be the one that put this chair here. On purpose. Right next to 81's prison. — That is a possibility I can neither confirm nor deny without a direct question, The Answer repeated. Takeshi, still in shock, looked up at the sphere he had almost literally been holding in his hands a few moments earlier without knowing it, a chilling thought gradually forcing itself on him. — He said it had to be put somewhere else, he murmured, turning to Isidora. You moved that chair yourself, with that thing on it. We... we literally carried his prison without knowing it. Takeshi hesitated a split second before asking his second question, his voice more confident than before. — How can we free him? — To free 81, The Answer replied without the slightest delay, you just need to take this crystal sphere and break it, by throwing it on the ground, for example. But I advise you to do so on physical ground. A stunned silence greeted this answer of almost comical simplicity, in total contrast with the cosmic scale of the entity in question. — This is a joke, said Lucifer, his voice incredulous. Like, we've got ten super-powerful beings — including an Incarnation of Death and five Archdragons — who joined forces to seal away the most dangerous threat ever known... and all it takes is dropping it on the floor to screw everything up? — The complexity of a seal does not necessarily lie in the fragility of its breaking point, The Answer replied, but in the difficulty of reaching it. No one before you had located this dimension, let alone this specific sphere. The simplicity of the final act in no way diminishes the difficulty of the road traveled to get there. Isidora was already backing away instinctively, her hands raised as if to push Takeshi away from the sphere he was still holding between his fingers. — Wait, wait, wait, she said hastily. Put that fucking ball down right now, kid. Like, right now, right now. Takeshi looked down at the sphere he hadn't even noticed he had picked up again, a cold sweat instantly running down his spine. — Wait, he said, his voice going up a notch, you were telling me that while I was holding it in my hands?! — Technically, The Answer specified, as long as it is not broken on a surface dense enough to release the pressure contained inside, it remains stable. You were safe. Probably. — "Probably"?! Takeshi repeated, panic completely overwhelming him as he knelt with exaggerated slowness to set the sphere back down on the liquid ground with the delicacy of a bomb technician defusing a bomb. Takeshi, still shaken, slowly straightened up, taking a trembling breath before asking his last question. — Where is my father? — Your father is... IN THAILAND! Isidora yelled, cutting off the voice that was starting to answer. — I will start again, The Answer said in a perfectly even tone, as if the interruption had never even happened. — So your father is... AN ASSHOLE! Isidora shouted again, grinning from ear to ear. — I will start again, The Answer repeated, unruffled. — Your father... ABANDONED YOU! Isidora bellowed once more, punctuating every word with a theatrical sweep of her arm. — SHUT UP! I WANT TO TALK! The Answer finally shouted, its voice losing every trace of neutrality for the first time since their arrival. — SO I'M STARTING AGAAAAAIN! The Answer yelled over Isidora, visibly delighted by the chaos it was causing. YOUR FATHER IS LOCKED UP IN THE CULT OF... XAVIER DUPONT DE LIGONNÈS! — WILL YOU SHUT YOUR MOUTH!!! The Answer retorted, the crystal sphere vibrating violently under the sudden intensity of its voice, an irritated light pulsing inside it. A shocked silence abruptly fell again, Lucifer and Alastor doubled over, unable to hold back their laughter, while Takeshi stood open-mouthed, torn between hilarity and total dismay. — Your father, The Answer finally went on, its voice gradually regaining its usual calm, though still tinged with perceptible annoyance, is being held by the Cult of KJ. He is still alive. Takeshi froze, the words taking several seconds to truly sink into his mind, every trace of amusement evaporating instantly. — He... he's alive, he murmured, his voice trembling. Are you sure? — I am never wrong, The Answer replied. Your father is being held somewhere within the Cult of KJ, since the War of the Estrangement. That was your last question. You have now used your three questions. I can no longer answer any other, for this life. Isidora, a smile still hanging on her lips, crossed her arms with perfect nonchalance. — Then again, it's true he could've been in Thailand, getting his ass kneaded by some Thai girl, huh. We don't know. We don't judge. A brief silence preceded The Answer's reply, its voice returning to an icy calm, almost threatening in its recovered neutrality. — Isidora, it said, if I had arms, legs, charisma, strength, solidity — and not just someone else's prison to show off with — I would come and knead that bitch skull of yours. A stunned silence greeted this retort, before Lucifer burst out laughing once again, even louder than before, almost doubling over. — Now that, he said between hiccups, is the best thing I've heard in centuries. An ancient omniscient entity threatening to knead Isidora's skull. Isidora, for her part, stayed open-mouthed for a moment, before a delighted smile spread across her face, visibly more impressed than insulted. — Okay, she said, respect. I didn't think you had that in you, chair. — I am not a chair, The Answer replied curtly. I am an omniscient consciousness forced to reside in a piece of furniture for lack of options. There is a difference. — Yeah, yeah, said Isidora, waving a casual hand, the chair. Well, thanks for the info, anyway. Even if you nearly fried twice because of me. Takeshi, still shaken by the revelation about his father, stayed silent, his gaze lost in the dark immensity of the dimension, a new and fragile determination slowly beginning to form behind the persistent worry that filled him.

codex-t2-c1.title: Chapter 1 — Justice Came Out of My Ass
codex-t2-c1.html:
Isidora turned her phone back on without a word, resuming her live with disconcerting ease — a gesture no one around her even bothered to comment on, all of them visibly too used to the reflex to pay it the slightest attention.

— Okay, people, here we go again, she announced simply, positioning the camera to capture the imminent takeoff.

Agent 47, unfazed, spoke up again, his synthetic-sounding voice as neutral as ever despite the implicit gravity of the information being passed on.

— Reaper confirms: Justice Man has an estimated one percent chance of survival. Probability of victory against 81: zero.

81 let out a short, dry laugh, adjusting the swords on his back with growing nonchalance.

— One percent, he repeated. That's already better than Rex Stella had, at least.

— He may have a chance to escape, Reaper specified. His imprisonment ability could theoretically protect him temporarily, with no guarantee of long-term success.

Takeshi, climbing aboard the ship that had just gently landed on the white stone of the sanctuary, cast a worried glance at 81.

— Are you really planning to kill him too? he asked. Even though his power is precisely about not killing the people he captures?

81 settled heavily into the ship, his massive body making the structure creak under his weight.

— Doesn't change what he did to me, he answered, an icy coldness returning to his voice. He took part in sealing me. Never mind his fine values of justice. He'll pay like the others.

A heavy silence settled, Isidora herself momentarily pausing her live commentary, sensing the new tension that had just settled in the cabin.

Lucifer, climbing in in turn, laid a hand on Takeshi's shoulder, his tone more serious than usual.

— Drop it, kid, he murmured. You can't reason with a vengeance several millennia old. Just stay out of his way, and you'll be fine.

The ship took off, shooting through space toward Earth, while inside everyone stayed silent, aware that the next confrontation would be very different from the last.

The ship touched down discreetly in a dark alley not far from downtown Washington, its hull blending almost instantly into the surrounding darkness thanks to an optical camouflage Agent 47 had activated even before the landing was complete.

They got off one by one, Takeshi blinking in the glare of the streetlights and at the familiar noise of city traffic — a striking contrast after the cosmic landscapes he had just crossed.

— Welcome back to Earth, kid, Lucifer remarked, adjusting his jacket, an amused smile on his lips. Feels weird, huh, seeing normal stuff again.

— You call that normal? Takeshi answered, nodding toward Isidora, who was already filming the facades of the surrounding buildings for her live, visibly delighted with the change of scenery.

They made their way through the streets, Agent 47 in the lead, his earpiece crackling regularly as Reaper analyzed police reports in real time, looking for the slightest sign of an unusual intervention.

— Activity detected, 47 finally announced, stopping dead at an intersection. Police report: several assaults stopped within ten minutes, within a three-block radius. No suspects apprehended on site. Victims report a swift intervention followed by the immediate disappearance of the attackers.

81 gave a satisfied smile, his eyes — well, his single eye — narrowing with growing anticipation.

— That's him, he said. Still saving little shopkeepers and random passersby. He never changed.

They followed the indicated direction, walking past several shop fronts, until they spotted, at the end of the street, a figure in a dark suit, standing motionless in front of a small grocery store, seeming to watch over the surroundings with an almost fatherly vigilance.

— There, Isidora murmured, finally lowering her phone, her usual excitement giving way to a new tension. That's him.

Justice Man, instantly sensing a presence approaching, slowly turned his head toward them, his gaze freezing as he recognized, among the little group, the massive and familiar figure of 81.

Justice Man slowly straightened up, his gaze moving from 81 to Isidora, an immediate tension hardening his features.

— You, he said, his voice heavy with calm gravity. I knew you'd get out. But it's a little premature.

— You can say that again, he's probably premature about so many things, Isidora called out with a mocking smile, her phone already raised toward the scene.

— You, shut up, Justice Man shot back without even looking at her, don't start busting my balls.

Isidora raised her hands in innocence, a smile still on her lips, but didn't turn off her live for all that, continuing to film with obvious pleasure.

— Okay, okay, I'll shut up, she said. But I'm still filming, just so you know.

81 took a step forward, his two swords still sheathed, a fierce smile slowly stretching across his scarred face.

— Premature, you say, he repeated. I've been waiting for this for millennia, Justice Man. Premature isn't really the word I'd use.

Justice Man didn't back down, his posture firming up, a golden glow slowly beginning to emanate from his hands, the energy of his power already gathering.

— I always knew this day would come, he said. But know one thing, 81: even if I know I can't beat you, I won't surrender without a fight.

— I expected nothing less from you, 81 answered, slowly drawing one of his two swords, his smile widening as the excitement of the imminent fight rose in him.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47 and Lucifer, felt a lump form in his throat, a dull worry growing at what was about to unfold right in the middle of a Washington street, under the potential eyes of dozens of passersby still unaware of the danger looming over them.

— Shouldn't we, like, evacuate the civilians before it starts? he asked, his voice hesitant.

— Too late for that, Agent 47 answered simply, glancing at the few passersby who were already starting to stop, intrigued by the palpable tension of the scene.

With a sweeping gesture, Justice Man summoned a massive hammer, its metal handle engraved with glowing symbols, the head of the weapon as wide as a human torso, and took up a defensive stance, legs slightly bent, ready to absorb the first assault.

81, for his part, simply kept his sword in hand, his single eye never leaving his opponent, an almost amused patience crossing his scarred face.

That was when a police officer, alerted by the passersby who had gathered at a distance, stepped toward them, one hand resting on his service weapon, his tone resolutely professional despite the rather unusual scene unfolding before him.

— Excuse me, gentlemen, he said, but those weapons are prohibited. Surrender and come with me to the station.

— STAND BACK! Justice Man shouted, without taking his eyes off 81. This man is dangerous, you need to evacuate the city at the very least!

The officer, visibly unimpressed by the warning, frowned, his hand tightening on his weapon.

— Sir, he retorted curtly, stop resisting, or you'll be considered noncompliant with the law.

Isidora, still filming the scene with undisguised pleasure, couldn't help bursting out laughing.

— People, I swear, this is the best moment of my evening, she commented. The poor cop trying to arrest a god killer and the Incarnation of Justice for illegal possession of weapons.

81, also amused by the intervention, turned his head slightly toward the officer, a predatory smile stretching across his face.

— He's right, you know, he said to the officer, a hint of irony in his voice. You really should evacuate the city. It's good advice.

The officer, suddenly hesitant before the icy self-assurance of that answer, took a step back, his hand trembling slightly on the grip of his weapon, while around them the first passersby were finally beginning to understand that something far more serious than a simple altercation was about to happen.

The officer, panic definitively taking over, drew his weapon and fired without waiting any longer — the bullet hit 81 square in the chest, ricocheting off his skin without leaving the slightest mark, dropping to the ground with a pathetic clink.

81 looked down at the point of impact, a barely annoyed smile stretching across his face, before turning to the officer with chilling murderous intent.

— Mistake, he said simply, lunging toward the man with lightning speed.

But Justice Man reacted instantly, his hammer striking the ground with such force that a shockwave hurled the officer out of reach, sending him crashing against the wall of a nearby building, dazed but alive.

— RUN! Justice Man roared at the man, without even turning toward him, his whole body tensed facing 81. Evacuate the city, the state if you have to, but get out!

The officer, still shaken, got up as best he could and immediately bolted, shouting confused orders into his radio, his trembling voice betraying pure terror.

Around them, the crowd that had gathered was already starting to panic, screams rising from all sides as the first witnesses finally grasped the scale of the danger, a general stampede beginning in the adjacent streets.

In the distance, police sirens wailed, approaching fast, their shrill sound adding to the growing chaos.

Justice Man, while keeping his guard up against 81, cast a quick glance at the panicking crowd, a visible dilemma crossing his features — protect the civilians still pouring into the area, or focus entirely on the fight that seemed inevitable.

— See your problem, Justice Man? said 81, visibly savoring this hesitation. You've always been too busy saving everyone to focus on what really matters.

— Saving people matters, Justice Man retorted, his hammer tightening in his hand as he made a quick gesture toward the surrounding streets, a golden glow briefly sweeping the area, forming an invisible barrier that gently pushed the crowd back. Even if it costs me dearly in this fight.

Isidora, still live, zoomed in on the scene with growing excitement.

— People, it's officially total chaos, she commented. I hope you've got popcorn, because this is going to be one hell of a show.

The fight exploded without warning, 81 and Justice Man lunging at each other in an outburst of raw power — their first blows colliding with such violence that the resulting shockwave literally swept away several surrounding blocks, entire facades collapsing with a deafening roar, glass and rubble raining down on the already deserted streets.

Justice Man absorbed each impact with impressive resilience, his hammer rising every time to block or deflect 81's assaults, but the difference in power remained glaring, visible without even trying to analyze it — each exchange left Justice Man pushed back a little further, a little more out of breath, while 81 seemed to barely bother putting in any effort.

But it was neither of them who broke the tense silence that followed each titanic clash.

— Could you move over to fight, please? Isidora called from the side, her phone perfectly steady despite the surrounding chaos. The lighting's better on the right.

The two fighters froze for a fraction of a second, a stunned silence settling despite the surrounding destruction, before 81 turned his head slightly toward her, one eyebrow — well, the brow ridge above his single eye — raised.

— Are you serious right now? he said.

— Completely, Isidora confirmed with a radiant smile. The setting sun hits badly on this side, it makes crappy shadows on your faces. Whereas over there, she added, pointing to an intersection a little farther on, it'd be way more cinematic.

Justice Man, still panting, shot her an incredulous look, a hint of exasperation breaking through his concentration.

— We're in the middle of a fight for the survival of one of us, he said, and you're worried about the lighting?

— People have standards these days, Isidora answered with a shrug, not the least bit shaken by the remark. You don't want your epic fight to look like a bad found-footage movie, do you?

81, shaking his head with a mixture of amusement and exasperation, turned back to Justice Man, his sword still raised.

— She's not completely wrong, you know, he said. Okay, come on, let's keep going, but a little more to the right.

81 and Justice Man repositioned themselves a few meters farther on, in light that was indeed better...

Justice Man raised his hammer.

81 smiled.

— Let's resume.

The next clash shook the whole neighborhood. Justice Man took the hit, slid three meters across the cracked asphalt, his hammer raised just in time to parry a second blow.

— You feel the difference now...

— I've always felt it.

81 followed up, faster, heavier. Justice Man dodged the first blow, blocked the second, but the third hurled him against the facade of a building that half collapsed under the impact.

Isidora, phone still raised.

— Wow, the angle's perfect now, thanks for the decorating tips, guys.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47 and Lucifer, watched Justice Man painfully get back up, blood running down his temple.

— He's going to die.

Lucifer didn't answer right away.

— Yes.

Justice Man straightened up, his hammer back in position, his gaze still fixed on 81 despite his obvious exhaustion.

— I'll hold out as long as it takes for the civilians to get far away.

81 moved forward slowly, his sword dragging along the ground with a metallic screech.

— You've always been too noble for your own good, Justice Man.

Isidora, phone still aimed, not taking her eyes off the fight.

— Shut up and more action! The fans want a fight, not a date, so either you get a room or you fight!

81 turned his head slightly toward her.

— She's right.

Justice Man gripped his hammer.

— ...

81 lunged first, his blade tracing a perfect arc. Justice Man raised his weapon just in time, the impact sending out a wave that shattered the windows of the surrounding buildings for a hundred meters.

— YOUR PROBLEM, JUSTICE MAN, IS THAT YOU ALWAYS FIGHT FOR OTHER PEOPLE!

— AND YOURS IS THAT YOU ONLY FIGHT FOR YOURSELF!

81 struck again, faster, Justice Man backing up several meters, the asphalt cracking under his feet with every forced step.

Isidora, in the background.

— YES! FINALLY SOME PUNCH! KEEP IT UP!

Takeshi, motionless, watched Justice Man's hammer begin to crack under the repeated impacts.

— He's going to lose his weapon...

Agent 47, unfazed.

— Confirmed. Structural failure estimated within the next few seconds.

Justice Man raised his hammer one last time to block a blow. The handle snapped clean, the head of the weapon flying off with a metallic crash.

81 stopped, his sword hovering a few centimeters from the face of Justice Man, out of breath, disarmed, on his knees on the split asphalt.

— ...

81 smiled.

— So, Justice Man. Any last words?

A voice rang out from the sky, calm, charged with an ancient power.

— You're the one who should be saying your last words, 81.

A bright point appeared above them, a star hanging behind Justice Man, a beam of light slowly descending and settling on the cracked asphalt with almost theatrical gentleness.

A figure materialized out of the light.

81 looked up, his smile freezing into a grimace mixing amusement and old grudge.

— Aravos. Still here to piss me off, then.

Isidora, phone still in hand, tilted her head to the side.

— Ooh, smells like a throuple.

— SHUT UP! 81, Justice Man and Aravos shouted in a single voice.

Isidora raised her hands in surrender, a smile still on her lips, but obviously didn't cut her live.

Aravos stepped forward, his footsteps making no sound on the ground, his gaze fixed squarely on 81 with an ancient coldness.

— It's been a long time.

— Not long enough, 81 answered, his sword still raised above Justice Man, but his attention now entirely turned toward the newcomer. I was hoping to kill you last. You ruined the surprise.

— Likewise.

Justice Man, taking advantage of 81's momentary inattention, tried to back away, crawling a few meters before collapsing, exhausted, his gaze moving between the two figures now facing each other.

Takeshi, standing back, leaned toward Agent 47.

— Who's he?

— Aravos. The Star of Decline. One of the ten who sealed 81.

81 rolled his shoulder, his sword rising again, his fierce smile returning to his face.

— Right. Since you came all the way here for your daughter, might as well settle this now.

Aravos didn't answer right away.

— ...

Then his gaze hardened.

— Exactly.

A crackle in Agent 47's earpiece.

— According to my estimates, combined chance of survival for Aravos and Justice Man: one point twenty-five percent. Chance of definitive victory: zero.

Then screams. From the other side of the city.

Buildings were collapsing one after another in a continuous roar, cries of panic rising from everywhere at once. In the distance, an army was taking shape on the horizon, advancing in formation, and on the ruins of a gutted building stood an immense figure.

Two and a half meters tall. A mass of bulging muscles under skin stretched to the limit, two tattoos inked into each forearm.

DIE. Left arm.

MEMORIES OF DEFEAT. Right arm.

Aravos froze, his gaze instantly hardening.

— Kang.

Isidora, phone turned toward the horizon.

— OH FUCK, we've got a second surprise guest!

81, still motionless facing Aravos, a nasty smile slowly stretching across his face.

— Kang? The King of Kings? The one who never managed to meet me?

Aravos didn't answer, his eyes still fixed on the massive figure advancing through the rubble, every step making the ground shake under his titanic weight.

Justice Man, still on his knees, raised his head, blood still running from his temple.

— ...

— Another problem, he murmured.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed, took a step back.

— Are there many cosmic threats left that are going to show up today?

Lucifer, arms crossed, watched the scene with an almost weary calm.

— Given the day we're having... I wouldn't even dare bet on it.

Kang landed in the middle of the battlefield, his massive feet shattering the asphalt on impact, placing himself directly between 81 and the Aravos–Justice Man duo.

— Aravos. Finally, there you are. Now I can get my revenge.

Aravos raised a hand.

— Listen, Kang. You wanted to fight 81 today? There he is. Right in front of you. Help us, and we'll all have gotten what we wanted.

Kang stood motionless.

— ...

— I accept.

— TO ME! JOIN THE FIGHT!

— Reaper. Full recalculation needed.

— Calculating.

Agent 47, unfazed, spoke up again, his synthetic-sounding voice as neutral as ever despite the implicit gravity of the information being passed on. — Reaper confirms: Justice Man has an estimated one percent chance of survival. Probability of victory against 81: zero. 81 let out a short, dry laugh, adjusting the swords on his back with growing nonchalance. — One percent, he repeated. That's already better than Rex Stella had, at least. — He may have a chance to escape, Reaper specified. His imprisonment ability could theoretically protect him temporarily, with no guarantee of long-term success. Takeshi, climbing aboard the ship that had just gently landed on the white stone of the sanctuary, cast a worried glance at 81. — Are you really planning to kill him too? he asked. Even though his power is precisely about not killing the people he captures? 81 settled heavily into the ship, his massive body making the structure creak under his weight. — Doesn't change what he did to me, he answered, an icy coldness returning to his voice. He took part in sealing me. Never mind his fine values of justice. He'll pay like the others. A heavy silence settled, Isidora herself momentarily pausing her live commentary, sensing the new tension that had just settled in the cabin. Lucifer, climbing in in turn, laid a hand on Takeshi's shoulder, his tone more serious than usual. — Drop it, kid, he murmured. You can't reason with a vengeance several millennia old. Just stay out of his way, and you'll be fine. The ship took off, shooting through space toward Earth, while inside everyone stayed silent, aware that the next confrontation would be very different from the last. The ship touched down discreetly in a dark alley not far from downtown Washington, its hull blending almost instantly into the surrounding darkness thanks to an optical camouflage Agent 47 had activated even before the landing was complete. They got off one by one, Takeshi blinking in the glare of the streetlights and at the familiar noise of city traffic — a striking contrast after the cosmic landscapes he had just crossed. — Welcome back to Earth, kid, Lucifer remarked, adjusting his jacket, an amused smile on his lips. Feels weird, huh, seeing normal stuff again. — You call that normal? Takeshi answered, nodding toward Isidora, who was already filming the facades of the surrounding buildings for her live, visibly delighted with the change of scenery. They made their way through the streets, Agent 47 in the lead, his earpiece crackling regularly as Reaper analyzed police reports in real time, looking for the slightest sign of an unusual intervention. — Activity detected, 47 finally announced, stopping dead at an intersection. Isidora raised her hands in innocence, a smile still on her lips, but didn't turn off her live for all that, continuing to film with obvious pleasure. — Okay, okay, I'll shut up, she said. The setting sun hits badly on this side, it makes crappy shadows on your faces. Whereas over there, she added, pointing to an intersection a little farther on, it'd be way more cinematic. Justice Man, still panting, shot her an incredulous look, a hint of exasperation breaking through his concentration. — We're in the middle of a fight for the survival of one of us, he said, and you're worried about the lighting? — People have standards these days, Isidora answered with a shrug, not the least bit shaken by the remark. codex-t2-c2.title: Chapter 2 — A Star, a Judge, a Sore Loser, an Army, and Also a Bitch Filming
codex-t2-c2.html:
81 lunged first.

Kang's entire army poured into the street at the same instant, hundreds of overtrained soldiers converging on a single point.

He didn't back down.

His blade cut through the first three ranks in a single movement, bodies flying off to either side like straw. Kang leapt over his own men, his fist crashing into 81's shoulder — an impact that shook the whole block, but 81 took it without flinching, pivoting to drive his sword into Kang's side.

— DID YOU REALLY THINK YOU HAD A CHANCE?

Aravos, taking advantage of the opening, unleashed a rain of miniature stars on 81, each one exploding on impact with the force of a small bomb. 81 turned, one blade rising to deflect the first ones, the rest smashing against his skin without the slightest effect.

Justice Man, still on his knees, picked up the broken head of his hammer, clutching it in his fist like an improvised weapon.

— ...

He got back up.

The army kept charging, wave after wave, every soldier crashing against 81 without ever really managing to slow him down — but their numbers, their persistence, were nevertheless starting to create pressure, an accumulation of blows that, one by one, were nothing, but together forced 81 to move, to parry, to shift position relentlessly.

Isidora, standing back, was still filming, her smile widening with every explosion.

— NOW THAT'S A SHOW!

Kang straightened up, pulling out the sword stuck in his side, his black blood flowing onto the asphalt.

— Let's continue.

81 smiled, turning his sword in his hand.

— I was hoping you'd say that.

Isidora set her phone on a little pole that she planted right into the asphalt, perfectly framing the scene, then stretched, cracking her neck to one side and then the other.

— Right, that's all well and good, but I want to have some fun too. So I'm gonna kill the army, and you, 81, you can take care of your exes, you little rascal.

She threw herself forward.

Her hands transformed instantly, long black claws shooting out of her fingers, a material that seemed to absorb all the surrounding light. She went through the army's first ranks as if the soldiers were nothing but butter, every swipe of her claws cleanly slicing through armor and bodies without the slightest resistance, limbs and pieces of equipment flying in every direction.

— ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR...

She counted out loud, almost laughing, chaining her movements with an almost dancing fluidity, leaving behind her a trail of mangled bodies.

Kang, distracted for a moment by the massacre going on behind him, turned his head.

— She...

81 took immediate advantage, his sword sinking deep into Kang's shoulder.

— Stay focused on me.

Aravos, seeing his army being methodically decimated, clenched his fists, his gaze swinging between 81 and the carnage Isidora was causing.

— She's going to kill them all before we're even done.

Justice Man, still standing despite his exhaustion, watched the scene with an unreadable expression.

— ...

— She's almost worse than 81, he finally murmured.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47 and Lucifer, watched Isidora literally dance through the entire army, a mixture of horror and total fascination on his face.

— She really enjoys doing that.

Lucifer nodded, a resigned smile on his lips.

— Always.

Aravos turned away from the duel against 81, leaving Justice Man and Kang to take the assaults alone, and advanced toward Isidora, his figure crossing the space in a flash of starlight.

He found her bent over a dismembered body, biting into it with undisguised pleasure.

— You're almost worse than 81.

Isidora raised her head, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand, a few traces of blood still clinging to her lips.

— Don't worry, sweetie, we're all gonna have fun together. Preferably let's still skip the orgy, an army and all that, it's a lot, you understand.

Aravos took up his stance, a stellar aura slowly crackling around him.

— ...

Isidora stretched, cracking her joints one by one, a delighted smile spreading across her still blood-smeared face.

— So, shall we?

— I won't go easy on you.

— I should hope not, otherwise it's no fun.

She lunged first, her black claws slicing through the air toward Aravos's face, who dodged by a hair, a trail of stellar energy dispersing at the exact spot where his head had been a fraction of a second earlier.

— Fast, she remarked, almost admiring.

— You have no idea.

Aravos struck back, a blast of cosmic energy bursting from his hands and hitting Isidora head-on — she took it, sliding back several meters, but her smile didn't waver for a second.

— Okay, that stings a little.

— This is only the beginning.

In the distance, the din of the fight between 81, Kang and Justice Man kept shaking the whole city, while the last screams of the decimated army gradually died away in the restored silence of the devastated streets.

Aravos attacked first, a burst of stellar shards shooting from his hands at lightning speed.

Isidora dodged every shot without the slightest effort, moving with an almost insulting nonchalance, no parry, no counterattack, just a step to the side, a tilt of the head, a light pirouette.

— ...

Aravos clenched his jaw, intensifying his assaults, multiplying the angles, the speeds, the trajectories — nothing worked, Isidora kept dodging as if she were dancing rather than fighting.

— Are you ever going to defend yourself?

— I don't need to.

She spun around, avoiding three simultaneous shards in a single fluid motion, a mocking smile on her lips.

— At least 81 bothers to really attack me.

Aravos exploded, a blast of stellar energy sweeping the entire street around him.

— YOU WANT ME TO REALLY ATTACK YOU?!

— Well, yeah.

He threw himself forward, his speed multiplied tenfold, his fist wrapped in cosmic light hurtling straight at her. Isidora, for the first time, didn't move, letting the blow come at her.

— ...

Then she caught it. In midair. With one hand.

— Ah, there we go. Finally a bit of seriousness.

Aravos stood frozen, his fist stopped dead in Isidora's palm, a mixture of astonishment and pure rage crossing his face.

— How...

— I told you, sweetie. You just had to ask nicely.

Aravos leapt back, his hands rising toward the sky, a blinding light beginning to concentrate between his palms — an entire star being compressed, its heat already melting the asphalt for several meters around.

Isidora, not the least bit impressed, pulled out a third phone from who knows where and calmly started scrolling.

— Let me know when you're done charging and you launch the attack, okay? Because right now, I'm kind of bored.

— ...

Aravos, his concentration almost broken by irritation, shot her a dark look.

— You're scrolling. While I prepare an attack capable of leveling an entire neighborhood.

— Well, yeah, she answered without even looking up from her screen. Gotta keep busy, you look like you'll be a while.

He gritted his teeth, the light between his hands growing even more intense, the heat now visible as ripples in the air.

— There, it's ready.

— Ah, finally, said Isidora, putting her phone away with a nonchalant gesture. I was starting to think you were going to propose to me instead of attacking me.

Aravos hurled the molten star straight at her, a torrent of heat and light ravaging everything in its path, the impact kicking up a cloud of dust and incandescent debris.

When the light faded, Isidora was still standing exactly where she had been, a simple bubble of dark void surrounding her, the stellar energy having completely dissipated inside it without leaving the slightest mark on her.

— There, she said, dismissing the bubble with a wave of her hand. That was nice. A bit long to set up, but nice.

Aravos, his astonishment giving way to a cold rage, raised both hands to the sky — a point of light appeared in the distance, growing at a dizzying speed, an entire star torn from its orbit, hurtling straight toward Earth.

— If you won't fight seriously, then we'll all die together.

Isidora looked up at the approaching star, not the least bit worried, even taking out her phone to snap a picture of it.

— Oh, nice framing, that.

She put the phone away, raised one hand, and struck.

A single blow, almost lazy.

The entire star crashed to the ground in a muffled explosion, its mass absorbed and neutralized by the mere impact of Isidora's fist, leaving behind only a smoking crater and a few incandescent fragments.

— All things considered, she said, wiping her hand on her cape, a marriage proposal would've been more interesting.

Aravos stood frozen, his arms slowly dropping to his sides, an expression close to despair crossing his usually impassive face.

— ...

— How... you just stopped a star. With your bare hands.

— Yeah, said Isidora with a shrug. Okay, seriously, are you planning to keep this up much longer? Because I'm really starting to get bored, and when I get bored, I do stupid things.

Isidora pulled out a jar of pickles from who knows where — once again — and fished one out directly with her fingers, biting into it with undisguised pleasure.

— Want one? To get your strength back?

She held out the jar to Aravos, a calm smile on her lips, as if she were offering a simple snack between two card games rather than in the middle of a devastated battlefield.

Aravos stood there, arms dangling, his gaze moving from the jar of pickles to Isidora, unable to come up with any coherent answer.

— ...

— No? she said with a shrug, closing the jar. Your loss.

He finally shook his head, a deep weariness gradually replacing his initial rage.

— I don't even understand what's happening anymore.

— It's simple, though, Isidora answered, putting the jar away. You wanted revenge for centuries. I just want to eat pickles and watch 81 have a little fun over there. We're just not on the same wavelength, sweetie.

In the distance, the din of the fight between 81, Kang and Justice Man kept shaking the entire city, a new explosion briefly lighting up the sky.

Aravos looked down at his own hands, still trembling with unused energy, a bitter reality finally sinking in.

— I never had the slightest chance, did I.

— No, Isidora confirmed with disarming naturalness. But hey, you still managed to make me break out my emergency pickles, so it's not a complete failure.

Isidora raised her jar of pickles to face height, took a perfectly framed shot, then started typing frantically on her phone.

— There, posted.

#Pickles #FightBreak #StillHungry #EvenInTheMiddleOfTheApocalypse

Meanwhile, a little farther on, Kang and Justice Man were still going all out against 81 — their blows chained together, crossed, tried every possible opening, but nothing got through. 81 dodged, blocked, deflected every assault with almost insulting ease, his sword barely necessary since the two opponents could hardly even graze him.

— DON'T YOU GET EVEN A LITTLE TIRED?! Kang roared, his fist smashing into the empty space where 81 had been a fraction of a second earlier.

— Not really, no.

Justice Man tried a low attack, aiming for the legs, but 81 simply jumped over it, landing behind him with an almost mocking nonchalance.

— You're both talented, he said. But talented isn't enough against me.

Aravos, still standing in front of Isidora and her jar of pickles, cast a desperate glance at the main fight.

— They won't manage it either.

— Nope, Isidora confirmed with disconcerting naturalness, crunching a new pickle. Nobody will. That's kind of the whole point of the scene, you see.

Kang leapt at 81 with all his strength, fist forward, his whole cosmic weight thrown into the assault.

81 stepped aside, almost nonchalantly.

Kang crashed onto the asphalt, rolling twenty meters before slamming into a wall that collapsed entirely on top of him in a cloud of rubble.

Isidora, still next to Aravos, burst out laughing, her jar of pickles nearly slipping from her hands.

— HOW HARD DID HE EAT IT, FUCK! Did you see that, live chat? I'm gonna make a story!

She tapped frantically at her phone.

#FloorEater #LosesTo81 #LuluCouldveDoneTheSame

Kang emerged from the rubble, furious, shaking off the debris clinging to his shoulders, a vein visibly throbbing on his forehead.

— THAT WASN'T FUNNY.

— Oh, it kind of was, said Isidora, without even looking up from her screen, already adding the next hashtags.

81, still standing where Kang had tried to reach him, shook his head, an amused smile on his lips.

— Honestly, you should've warned me before charging like that. Even Justice Man aims better than you.

— THANKS, Justice Man muttered from a little farther away, without much conviction.

Kang, humiliated for the second time that day — the first having already been burned into his memory by Aravos himself — straightened up with growing rage, his fists tightening.

— I'M GOING TO KILL YOU.

— You've tried that several times now, 81 answered with a shrug. Still not convinced it's gonna work this time.

The fight dragged on for hours.

The entire city was nothing but a field of ruins, every structure razed below six meters, the skyscrapers themselves reduced to smoking concrete stumps. Blood covered what was left of the ground and walls, a dark, thick paint spreading over kilometers.

Kang and Justice Man kept on fighting, still.

Aravos had pulled away from his absurd duel against Isidora — after calling her, in a bitter breath, "the biggest bitch in existence" — and was now watching the main fight, a growing weariness replacing his initial anger.

— ...

Kang charged again. 81 countered with a simple backhand.

Justice Man tried a new approach, a different angle, a studied feint. 81 saw it coming before it even started.

Aravos clenched his fists.

— They don't have any chance left.

Isidora, coming up behind him, still crunching from her jar of pickles, nodded with disarming naturalness.

— They never did, sweetie. But hey, gotta admit they're hanging in there.

Kang took another hit, collapsing onto one knee, out of breath. Justice Man, beside him, was only standing by sheer willpower, every muscle in his body trembling with accumulated exhaustion.

81 didn't even seem to be sweating.

— Well, he said, twirling his sword between his fingers. Are we going to keep this up much longer, or would you rather we finish it now?

Aravos, his eyes fixed on the scene, felt a bitter truth settle definitively inside him.

— We never had the slightest chance. Not today. Not millennia ago.

A faint crackle sounded in the earpiece of Agent 47, who had stayed back since the start of the fight, his synthetic-sounding voice falling like a blade.

— Analysis complete, he announced. Reaper confirms: even if 81 were currently fighting at zero point zero zero zero... — and several billion more zeros — one percent of his real power, the outcome of the fight would not have changed. Certain victory, in every scenario calculated.

A heavy silence fell over the smoking ruins of the city.

Takeshi, sitting on a cracked concrete block, slowly turned his head toward 47.

— Are you telling me we just watched a massacre that lasted several hours... for nothing?

— Correction, 47 answered without the slightest emotion. Not for nothing. For entertainment.

Isidora, standing back with her now-empty jar of pickles, nodded with an enthusiasm that hadn't faded one bit since the start.

— That, at least, is objectively true.

Aravos, sitting right on the ground, his head in his hands, let out a bitter, almost broken laugh.

— A billion zeros. We fought for hours against a being who didn't even need a hundredth of a percent of his strength.

Kang, still on his knees, his body covered in wounds, looked up at 81, an empty expression gradually replacing his rage.

— ...

— It's over, Justice Man murmured beside him, in the same state.

— Right, he said. Who wants to die first?

A nuclear explosion tore through the sky above them, a blinding red light sweeping the entire horizon in a fraction of a second — 81 himself, despite all his power, felt the shockwave push him back several meters, a rare enough event to draw his immediate attention.

A figure emerged from the explosion.

Two meters tall. An angular face, a hard jaw, narrow eyes with piercing golden-yellow irises, thick eyebrows accentuating an implacable gaze. Dark, spiky hair streaked with reddish glints. Pale skin striped with red and black patterns running across his whole body — the neck, the massive shoulders, the dense and perfectly defined torso, a pronounced V-shaped silhouette, every muscle visible even at rest.

He swept the scene with his gaze, his expression betraying no emotion — only a cold, absolute authority.

— You are fighting on our Lord's territory. And I, the Assimilated, am going to make sure you never want to disturb him twice.

A stunned silence followed.

Takeshi, completely lost, turned to Agent 47.

— Who's this one now?

Lucifer, on the other hand, had frozen, his whole body stiffening instantly, a sudden pallor crossing his usually so relaxed face.

— ...

— A Higher Incarnation. Of KJ.

81, motionless, his sword still in hand, slowly turned his head toward the newcomer, a glint of cold calculation crossing his single eye — for the first time since his release, real caution appearing in his posture.

Isidora, her empty jar of pickles still in one hand, froze as well, her usual smile vanishing instantly.

— ...

— Okay. Now it's getting serious.

Justice Man and Kang stayed perfectly still, incapable of the slightest gesture, the Assimilated's presence literally crushing any impulse to move.

81, for his part, felt something different — a new pressure, a power that, for the first time since his release, truly deserved his attention. His grip tightened slightly on his sword.

— ...

Lucifer, inside his head, was already screaming dozens of catastrophic scenarios — but his body stubbornly refused to respond, frozen by an ancient, instinctive terror, the kind every Higher Incarnation of KJ inspired.

Isidora, alone in the midst of all this petrifying tension, had already raised her phone, filming the scene with the same unshakable enthusiasm she had shown since the start of the day.

— People, looks like the final boss just showed up.

The Assimilated slowly turned his head toward her, a silent contempt crossing his golden gaze.

— ...

— You. You find this funny?

— A little, yeah, Isidora answered without the slightest ounce of worry, adjusting her camera angle. Gotta admit you've got a hell of a sense of staging, with your nuclear explosion and all.

The Assimilated didn't answer right away, his gaze settling in turn on each of the fighters present — 81, Kang, Justice Man, Aravos, then Lucifer, whose silent terror visibly didn't escape him.

— You are lucky. Our Lord does not deal personally with minor nuisances.

81 let out a deep laugh, gradually regaining his composure despite the palpable tension.

— Minor nuisance. I like that.

— You shouldn't, the Assimilated answered, a chaotic energy slowly beginning to crackle around his fists. Because I am going to make sure it's the last time you use that word to describe yourself.

codex-t2-c3.title: Chapter 3 — #WhoDiesFirst? (Part 1)
codex-t2-c3.html:
Lucifer, finally regaining some semblance of control over his own voice, murmured to 81, without taking his eyes off the massive figure of the Assimilated.

— Don't believe what you're about to see. He's the Incarnation of Chaos. Nothing he does will be logical.

81 nodded slightly, his gaze never leaving his opponent.

— ...

The Assimilated readied his fists, a dark and unstable energy crackling all around him, flashes of impossible colors streaking the air, reality itself seeming to waver a few centimeters from his skin.

81 took up his stance in turn, both swords now raised, his body taut with a concentration he hadn't shown at any point until then.

For the first time since his release, he felt, deep inside, something he had almost forgotten after millennia of being sealed away.

Genuine doubt.

Isidora, still filming, tilted her head to one side, not the least bit impressed.

— Okay, this one went a little overboard on style with the tattoos, but hey, let's see what he's made of.

— People, she added to her live, we're finally going to find out if the red stripes are just tuning or if they actually do something.

The Assimilated lunged first, without warning, his speed defying all physical logic — one instant he was ten meters away, the next his fist was already crashing against 81's guard, the resulting shockwave instantly pulverizing everything left of the surrounding buildings within a radius of several hundred meters.

81 took it, his feet sinking deep into the asphalt under the violence of the impact, a growl of pain escaping him for the first time that day.

— ...

He looked up at the Assimilated, a fierce smile tinged with a new excitement stretching across his scarred face.

— Finally. A real fight.

Isidora, in the background, clapped limply with one hand, the other still holding her phone.

— Ooh, nice dull thud, that. Ten out of ten for sound design.

A crackle ran through Agent 47's earpiece — he had stayed motionless since the Assimilated arrived — his synthetic-sounding voice falling with a new gravity.

— Recalculation complete. For the first time since the start of this confrontation, the probabilities are balanced. Fifty percent for the Assimilated. Fifty percent for 81. The fight is even.

A stunned silence greeted this announcement, even Isidora momentarily pausing her commentary.

— ...

— Wait, she said finally, lowering her phone slightly. Say that again.

— Fifty percent each, 47 repeated without the slightest variation in tone. No available data makes it possible to determine a clear favorite.

Takeshi, still sitting on his concrete block, felt an icy shiver run down his spine.

— It's the first time anything's had a real chance against him.

Lucifer, still petrified, slowly nodded, unable to tear his eyes away from the fight.

— And that's exactly what should worry all of us.

81, hearing Reaper's announcement despite the distance, let out a deep, almost euphoric laugh, his smile widening further as he faced the Assimilated.

— Did you hear that? Fifty-fifty. It's been ages since anyone gave me a real chance of losing.

The Assimilated, unfazed, tightened his fists, a chaotic aura intensifying all around him.

— Numbers don't matter. Only the result counts.

— That, said 81, launching himself back into the attack, his two swords whirling, is the first sensible thing you've said since you got here.

Isidora, finally coming back to her senses, raised her phone with redoubled enthusiasm.

— PEOPLE, WE FINALLY HAVE A POSSIBLE DRAW! STAY TUNED, THIS IS GONNA BE HUGE!

The Assimilated raised a fist to the sky, a chaotic energy crackling all around him.

— I am the incarnation...

— OF DUMBASSES! Isidora yelled from her corner, phone still raised.

— No, I am the incarnation...

— OF ASSHOLES! she shouted again, a delighted smile on her lips.

— I AM THE INCARNATION...

— OF PEOPLE WHO STILL ARGUE ABOUT PAIN AU CHOCOLAT VERSUS CHOCOLATINE!

— SHUT UP! the Assimilated roared, reality itself wavering under the intensity of his voice, several dimensional cracks briefly opening in the air around him before closing again at once.

— I AM CHAOS. AND THE WORLD WILL UNDERSTAND IT.

A silence followed, broken only by Isidora's satisfied little laugh as she calmly tucked her phone against her hip.

— Okay, that one, I admit, wasn't bad.

81, already in position, a fierce smile on his lips, shook his head with an amused look.

— You see, he told the Assimilated, she does that to everyone. Nobody escapes it.

— I don't care who she is, the Assimilated answered, his golden gaze locking onto 81 again with redoubled intensity. You. Focus on me.

— Already am, said 81, his two swords rising.

This time he lunged first, without waiting — the two forces colliding with a crash that literally tore the sky open above them, the shockwave instantly sweeping away everything that was left of the city within a radius of several kilometers.

Isidora resumed her live, perfectly framing the two fighters now clashing at a speed impossible to follow with the naked eye, every exchange creating a shockwave strong enough to raze what was left of the city's foundations.

— PEOPLE, HOLD ON TIGHT, STUFF'S ABOUT TO BREAK!

The Assimilated struck, a fist charged with chaotic energy crashing against 81's crossed guard — the impact reversed gravity over several hundred meters, debris starting to float, rising toward a now unstable sky before slamming back down a few seconds later.

81 took it, staggered back three steps, then immediately counterattacked, his two blades tracing a parallel arc. The Assimilated almost dematerialized, his body briefly distorting into a shapeless mass before re-forming farther away, dodging the attack without the slightest apparent effort.

— You cannot predict my movements, he said, his voice echoing from several places at once. Chaos obeys no logic.

— Never needed logic, 81 retorted, spinning around to parry an attack coming out of nowhere, matter and energy merging around the Assimilated's fist.

The blows came one after another, faster and faster, more and more violent — the ground cracked, heaving up in places, the air itself sometimes seemed to invert, the light of the setting sun freezing in midsky before resuming its course in jerks.

Isidora, still filming, had to scramble back when a gust of inverted reality nearly carried her away.

— OKAY, THIS ONE'S CHEATING A LITTLE WITH THE LAWS OF PHYSICS!

81 suddenly drove his sword into the ground, using the leverage to launch himself at the Assimilated at multiplied speed, his fist finally smashing into his opponent's jaw — the first blow truly landed since the start of the confrontation.

The Assimilated staggered, a trickle of dark blood escaping his split lip, an expression of genuine surprise briefly crossing his impassive face.

— ...

— So, said 81, his fierce smile widening. Still as confident?

The two opponents straightened up almost simultaneously, each wiping his own wound with a brief gesture — 81 his split lip, the Assimilated a deep gash across his forearm where a blade had finally found its way.

— ...

— Finally something interesting, said 81, spinning his swords in his hands.

The Assimilated didn't answer right away, his golden gaze narrowing, an even denser chaotic energy building around his fists, filaments of warped reality crackling across his skin.

— You made me bleed. That hadn't happened in a long time.

— Happy to contribute, 81 answered with a predatory smile.

They threw themselves at each other at the same instant, the next clash literally tearing the ground apart for several hundred meters, a zigzagging crevasse opening across the ruins of the city. The Assimilated unleashed a series of blows at an ever more erratic speed, changing direction mid-movement, his body sometimes splitting in two for a fraction of a second to attack from two angles at once.

81 parried the first double, dodged the second by a hair, a gash opening on his shoulder where he hadn't fully managed to avoid the impact.

— ...

— You see, said the Assimilated, a cold satisfaction in his voice. Chaos always wins, in the end.

— We'll see about that, 81 answered, ignoring the pain, his sword rising for a new assault.

Isidora, standing back, kept filming with growing enthusiasm, her phone barely steady against the successive shockwaves.

— PEOPLE, THEY'RE REALLY HURTING EACH OTHER NOW, THIS IS OFFICIALLY THE BEST FIGHT OF MY LIFE!

The fight picked up again with renewed fury, every exchange more violent than the last, the entire city continuing to crumble under the combined pressure of two powers that, for the first time in millennia, seemed truly matched.

81, stopping for a moment facing the Assimilated, raised his sword to the sky, a new intensity crossing his scarred face.

— I am the one who...

— HAS NO FUTURE! Isidora yelled from her corner, phone still raised.

— I am...

— A SUB-SHIT! she shouted again, delighted.

— No, I AM...

— THE GROUP'S SHITHEAD, WELL, WHEN LULU'S HIDING HIS FACE!

— WILL YOU SHUT YOUR BIG MOUTH! 81 roared, his voice echoing through the entire ruins of the city. I AM THE ONE WHO TODAY WILL KILL CHAOS ITSELF AND BRING YOUR HEAD BACK TO KJ!

A brief silence followed, the echo of his declaration slowly fading through the ruins, before Isidora raised a thumb at the camera.

— Okay, he did save that one pretty well.

The Assimilated, unfazed by the interruption, wiped away the blood still running from his split lip.

— You can threaten all you want. KJ fears nothing from you.

— We'll see, 81 answered, his fierce smile returning to his face, his two swords tightening in his hands. Because I really, really want to check that in person.

He lunged again, even faster than in the previous exchanges, a new determination driving each of his movements — no longer just vengeance against those who had sealed him, but now a far vaster, far more dangerous ambition slowly taking shape behind every blow he landed.

The Assimilated froze, 81's words ringing like outright desecration in his ears, a chaotic aura instantly exploding around him, warping the surrounding space in successive waves.

— HOW DARE YOU THINK YOURSELF SUPERIOR TO KJ, YOU FILTHY INSIGNIFICANT BEING?!

Isidora, unfazed, raised an eyebrow.

— Did you mix up 81 and Lucifer, by any chance?

The Assimilated didn't even seem to hear her, his golden gaze entirely fixed on 81, a cold and absolute rage hardening every one of his features.

81 smiled, visibly savoring the reaction he had provoked.

— I'm sure I'll beat KJ someday. And you won't be around to see it.

— That's it, enough, the Assimilated retorted, his voice losing every trace of humanity, now resonating like several voices layered on top of one another.

— Domain Expansion... Infinite Chaos.

The air tore apart all around them, reality itself beginning to bend, to twist, fragments of sky breaking off like pieces of shattered glass, gravity intermittently reversing, daylight giving way to impossible hues — violet, acid green, a black deeper than any natural shadow.

Takeshi, still standing back with Lucifer and Agent 47, felt the ground itself become unstable beneath his feet, seized by immediate nausea at this total distortion of space.

— What is this madness...

Lucifer, his voice trembling, took a step back despite his forced paralysis.

— His domain. He just deployed his domain.

Isidora, for her part, looked around with sincere interest, not the least bit disturbed by the surrounding chaos.

— Oh, nice decor.

81, alone at the center of this dislocated reality, immediately felt the change — nothing obeyed the laws he knew anymore, every movement, every attack now subject to total and uncontrollable chance.

— ...

A fierce smile stretched across his scarred face nonetheless.

— Perfect. Now we're really going to see what you're made of.

Inside the distorted domain, every one of the Assimilated's blows gained power unpredictably — sometimes doubled, sometimes multiplied tenfold with no apparent logic, the chaotic reality amplifying his assaults at the whim of total chance.

81 took a first blow of new violence, hurled across several dozen meters before righting himself in midair, landing on his feet with a dull rumble.

— ...

He got back up at once, adapting, learning to read not movements anymore but intentions, anticipating the unpredictable with a new concentration. His sword found an opening, cutting deep into the Assimilated's side — a wound larger than the previous one, dark blood flowing abundantly.

The Assimilated struck back without waiting, his fist sinking into 81's ribs with a force that made something distinctly crack, a groan of pain escaping him for the first time.

The exchanges multiplied, closer and closer together, bloodier and bloodier — every blow now leaving its mark, another gash, a spreading bruise, blood flowing from both sides in increasingly visible quantities.

81 drove a blade deep into the Assimilated's shoulder. The Assimilated answered with a knee strike that broke several more ribs.

— ...

— You're stronger than I thought, 81 admitted, spitting out a little blood, a fierce smile still hanging on his lips.

— So are you, the Assimilated answered, his voice gradually losing its multiple echo, becoming almost human again under the strain.

Isidora, watching the scene with new attention, seemed for the first time to hesitate before resuming her usual commentary.

— ...

— Okay, fine, this time it's really serious, she said finally, her tone nevertheless remaining surprisingly light.

The fight went on, the two opponents inflicting deeper and deeper wounds on each other, every second bringing a little closer the outcome of a confrontation whose result no one, not even Reaper, could predict anymore.

A faint crackle ran through Agent 47's earpiece, Reaper's voice as neutral as ever despite the cataclysmic scale of the fight.

— Recalculation complete. Result unchanged. Equal chances of victory for both parties.

47, out of pure habit, transmitted all the accumulated data and analyses to Grand Patron Luigi — less out of protocol than habit, a routine ingrained over years of service.

A short silence followed, before an answer came directly through his earpiece.

— ...

— Order received, 47 announced, adjusting his weapon without the slightest hesitation. Intervention authorized against the Assimilated. Assistance to 81.

Takeshi, still shaken by the surrounding chaos, turned his head sharply toward him.

— Wait, you're really going to step in? Against a Higher Incarnation?

— The Boss's orders, 47 answered simply, as if that were enough to justify any madness.

He stepped forward, his weapon unfolding into a firing mode that existed in no known military catalog, his eyes locking onto the Assimilated with cold, calculated precision.

Isidora, noticing the movement, raised an eyebrow, her usual smile finally reappearing.

— Ooh, this is getting interesting. Grand Patron Luigi's little doggy is coming to play too.

— I am not a dog, 47 answered without turning around, his finger settling on the trigger.

81, catching 47's movement out of the corner of his eye, shouted through the surrounding chaos, his voice charged with a mixture of surprise and growing respect.

— You really don't need to help me!

— This is not to help you, 47 answered, unfazed, carefully aiming at the Assimilated. It is to test my limits.

He fired.

The Assimilated, distracted for an instant by the rapid movement coming out of nowhere, dodged most of the shots — but two bullets found their way, sinking deep into his shoulder and thigh, a new pain crossing his face, different from what 81 had inflicted, sharper, almost surgical.

— ...

He turned his head toward the source of the shots, his golden gaze settling on Agent 47, immediate recognition crossing his scarred features.

— You.

47 didn't answer, reloading his weapon with mechanical precision, his face as expressionless as ever.

— The God of Death, the Assimilated murmured, a new caution replacing his initial rage. I've heard of you. A creature of Grand Patron Luigi. Capable, in theory, of wounding a Higher Incarnation.

— The theory has just been confirmed, 47 answered simply, taking aim again.

81, taking advantage of this unexpected diversion, lunged through the surrounding chaos, his sword sinking deep into the Assimilated's back while he was still distracted by 47's presence.

The Assimilated let out a cry of pain, spinning around abruptly, a chaotic aura exploding around him to push 81 back.

— So now the two of you are ganging up on me?

— You deployed an entire domain against me alone, 81 answered with a fierce smile. I don't see the problem.

Isidora, standing back, clapped softly, her phone still trained on the scene.

— Ah, now that's some beautiful teamwork, people! Even if technically, nobody really asked 47 for his opinion.

47, unfazed, kept advancing slowly, his weapon still aimed at the Assimilated, a calculating coldness in each of his movements.

— Reaper, recalculate probabilities with my intervention included.

A brief crackle preceded the answer.

— Calculating...

A faint crackle ran through 47's earpiece, Reaper's voice resuming with its usual precision.

— Calculation complete. With your intervention included: seventy-five percent chance of victory for 81 and 47 combined. Twenty-five percent for the Assimilated.

47 barely nodded, reloading his weapon with a fluid gesture.

— Acceptable.

81, hearing the announcement, let out a deep laugh despite the blood still flowing from his many wounds.

— Seventy-five percent. I already like that better.

The Assimilated, still enduring the two bullet wounds that kept burning him with a strange pain, took a step back, his golden gaze moving from 81 to 47 with visible calculation.

— Two against one. That's not very honorable.

— Honor is a human concept, 81 answered with a shrug, his swords rising. Never really had that in me.

— Nor I, 47 added simply, his weapon steadying again.

Isidora, in the background, raised a hand as if to step in, a mischievous smile on her lips.

— Technically, I could join in too, but hey, I already broke my Aravos toy today, gotta leave some challenge for the others.

The Assimilated, sensing the gradual shift in the balance of power, intensified his chaotic aura, a new distortion of reality spreading all around him, more violent, even more unstable than the previous one.

— Very well. If you want to play two against one, I'll have to stop holding back.

81 smiled, his sword pointed straight at him.

— That's exactly what I was hoping to hear.

All three of them launched themselves at once, the fight entering an even more destructive phase, every exchange now threatening to raze what was left of the entire region.
