Isidora, standing back, was herself starting to show unusual signs of impatience, her phone still raised but her foot tapping nervously against the ground.

— Okay, people, this fight is starting to drag on. Even I think it's taking forever, and that says something.

Takeshi, exhausted by hours of tense watching, slumped a little further against his concrete block.

— How can you even measure... how much time is left, in something like this?

Lucifer, still pale, slowly shook his head.

— You can't. You watch, and you hope it ends well.

Isidora Néant pulled out her phone, typing quickly on the screen despite the surrounding chaos making the ground tremble under her feet.

— Fuck, this is long, we're bored.

She switched on the front camera, vaguely framed the fight in the background — an explosion of rubble right behind her that she dodged without even looking — and launched a poll in her story.

#WhoDiesFirst?
🟥 The Assimilated
🟦 81 (nah just kidding, he's not gonna die)

— Vote, guys, it adds a little suspense to this slog.

Takeshi Ashford, still hiding behind his concrete block, turned his head toward her, completely flabbergasted.

— ...

— What?

— You... you're doing a poll. Right now.

— Well, yeah. Let's not kid ourselves, it's dragging. Might as well keep the followers busy.

Lucifer Morningstar, still pale, looked at her with an almost mechanical slowness, as if his brain refused to process the information.

— Isidora, there's a Higher Incarnation of Chaos fifteen meters from us.

— I know, I can see him, he's in the shot right there, look.

She turned the screen toward him — sure enough, the Assimilated was taking a sword blow from 81 square in the chest, hurled through three buildings, perfectly visible in the background of the story.

— Makes a good background, right?

The votes were already starting to pour in, scrolling live on the screen. Isidora let out a satisfied little sound.

— Oh look, 81 is leading at 73%. People have faith.

A dull cry rang out in the distance — the Assimilated had just taken a shot from Agent 47 square in the shoulder, black blood spurting from the wound before being reabsorbed almost instantly, soaked up by the surrounding chaotic domain.

— Oh wait, no, actually, look at that, his wound is closing up, that's so OP.

She zoomed in on it, commenting live like a sports commentator.

— So, friends, for those just joining the live, it's officially been... — she quickly checked her phone's stopwatch — three hours and twelve minutes of them beating on each other without anyone gaining the upper hand. A classic.

— Isidora, Lucifer growled, couldn't you... I don't know... help?

— Help with what, watching them fight faster?

— Step in!

— But Lucifer, honey, if I step in, you know me, I'm gonna wreck everything in ten seconds and then we won't have any more content for the story.

Takeshi brought a hand to his face, completely overwhelmed.

— ...

In the distance, 81 had just driven a blade right into the Assimilated's throat — who, with a movement of inhuman speed, partially dematerialized to avoid the fatal blow, his body re-forming a few meters away in a cloud of black and red particles.

— Ohhh, that was slick, Isidora commented, still filming. Okay, polls close in two minutes, guys, hurry up.

A little farther off, Aravos, Kang and Justice Man watched the scene, motionless, each too badly hurt to make the slightest move. Aravos was holding his visibly dislocated arm against his chest, Kang was struggling to stay upright, leaning on what was left of his cracked armor, and Justice Man, his broken hammer lying at his feet, stared at the fight with an empty expression.

— ...

— Shouldn't we... try something? Kang breathed, his voice hoarse.

Justice Man slowly shook his head.

— You saw the same thing I did. We wouldn't last five seconds.

Aravos spat a little blood on the ground, his eyes riveted on the fight in the distance, where the Assimilated had just taken another sword blow from 81 without even staggering.

— ...

No one added anything. The silence between the three of them was answer enough.

Meanwhile, Lucifer Morningstar had moved closer to Isidora Néant, his face still marked by unusual tension.

— Fuck's sake, Isidora, step in, he said.

— Okay, Lulu, I'll do a poll. If people want me to step in, I'll step in. Happy now, asshole?

She turned her phone back toward herself, typing at full speed.

#ShouldIsidoraStepIn?
✅ YES GO FOR IT
❌ NO KEEP THE SUSPENSE

Lucifer brought a hand to his face.

— ...

— It's for democracy, Lulu. I can't just decide like that, I've gotta consult the people.

— There's a Higher Incarnation of Chaos destroying Washington.

— Exactly, that deserves an informed vote.

The results started scrolling on the screen, the percentage climbing quickly on the "YES" side.

— Oh well, look at that, 89% want me to step in. Okay.

She finally put her phone away in a pocket that hadn't really existed a second earlier, her black claws slowly beginning to form along her fingers.

— Well, since the people have spoken...

She turned her head toward Lucifer, a wide and perfectly carefree smile on her lips.

— You'll see, it's gonna be fun.

Isidora Néant leapt off, her phone still in hand, the front camera filming her own laughing face as she flew through the air toward the battlefield.

— Guys, this is the moment you've all been waiting for, the long-requested intervention!

She landed between 81 and Agent 47 in a cloud of black dust, her claws already formed, her smile as wide as ever.

— So, having fun without me?

81 barely turned his head, wiping the blood off his chin.

— Took you long enough.

— Had to consult the people, democracy's important.

Agent 47, unfazed, reloaded his weapon without a word, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Riper, new calculation.

A moment of silence, then Reaper's synthetic voice rang out directly inside his skull.

"Recalculating... probability of victory for the trio: 90%."

47 raised an eyebrow, the only visible sign of his surprise.

— 90%.

— Seriously? Isidora called out, visibly delighted. Well, we're gonna win then, cool.

But despite that number, despite Isidora entering the equation, the Assimilated kept holding on. His movements remained precise, his chaotic domain still active, warping reality around them intermittently — and yet, something was off.

The Assimilated himself seemed to notice it, his golden gaze narrowing slightly as he narrowly avoided a combined blow from 81 and Isidora.

— ...

— Riper, 47 insisted, why are the probabilities going up while nothing changes concretely?

"Analyzing... anomaly detected. An external force is limiting the expansion of the chaotic domain. Source unidentified."

— An external force? Isidora repeated, dodging a slab of reality that had just twisted a few meters from her. Who's that, us?

"Negative. The limitation existed before your intervention."

81 frowned, his sword still raised against the Assimilated, who was backing away slightly, his breath shorter than before.

— You hear that? You've got a brake somewhere?

The Assimilated didn't answer right away. His expression, usually cold and assured, cracked slightly — a hint of genuine confusion crossing his golden gaze.

— ...

— I don't... he began, his voice hesitating for the first time since the start of the fight.

— Ooh, he doesn't know, Isidora observed, almost amused. That's a new one.

The Assimilated clenched his fists, his chaotic domain wavering around him as if he were trying to force something that stubbornly refused to give way.

— My power... should be total. Something is holding it back.

He looked at his own hands, as if the answer lay there, before raising his eyes to his three opponents, a new glint — almost worried — crossing his face.

— It's not you.

— Well, that's clear at least, Isidora called out, shrugging before launching back into the attack. Okay, never mind, let's take advantage of it then!

An entire section of the chaotic domain cracked, then shattered like pulverized glass — revealing, in the middle of the fragments of reality hanging in the air, a motionless figure.

A doll.

Her skin, very pale, almost grayish, contrasted with her big rosy cheeks. Her oversized, round, blue-gray eyes stared straight ahead without blinking, framed by long black lashes. Her dark red, almost burgundy hair was gathered into two voluminous pigtails of messy curls, held by dark blue ribbons, a wide lock swept down over her forehead. Her midnight-blue dress, with geometric pleats and a large collar adorned with a blue bow, floated slightly despite the lack of wind, her arms spread out on either side as if suspended by invisible strings.

— ...

The entire fight seemed to pause. Even the Assimilated, motionless, stared at the apparition with an unreadable expression.

Isidora Néant, phone still raised, narrowed her eyes — then her face lit up all at once.

— Poppy! My favorite bitch, after me of course!

— ...

81 turned his head toward Isidora, his sword still dripping with black blood.

— You know her?

— Yeah, old acquaintance. She hunts people all over the place, very nice hobby, very harmless, zero danger.

Takeshi Ashford, still hiding behind his concrete block with Lucifer Morningstar, froze instantly upon hearing that name, his whole body going rigid.

— ...

— Takeshi? Lucifer asked worriedly, noticing the immediate change.

— It's her. It's... it's her who's been hunting me from the start.

The doll, still motionless in the middle of the fragments of the shattered chaotic domain, slowly turned her head — a mechanical movement, almost too fluid to be natural — her empty gaze settling directly on the Assimilated.

— ...

The Assimilated, for the first time since the start of the fight, seemed to back away slightly.

Reaper's synthetic voice crackled again in Agent 47's earpiece.

"Recalculating... new entity integrated into parameters. Probability of victory: 99%."

47 raised an eyebrow, glancing at the doll still motionless among the debris.

— 99%. With no combat data on her.

— Well, she doesn't need to fight to scare the crap out of you, Isidora commented, amused. Look at her face, it's already a visual assault.

The Assimilated, for his part, clearly felt the balance tipping. His chaotic domain, already hampered by that mysterious force he still didn't understand, kept cracking under the combined pressure of 81, Agent 47, Isidora, and now this additional presence he knew nothing about.

— ...

His golden gaze quickly swept the scene — 81, his 621 hearts pulsing with raw and growing energy, Agent 47 already reloading his weapon, Isidora whose black claws still hadn't stopped growing, and this motionless doll whose aura alone was enough to sow deep doubt.

He understood.

Too many forces. Too many unknowns. Even at full power, the odds were becoming untenable.

— ...

Without a word, the Assimilated partially dematerialized, his body breaking apart into black and red particles, beginning a lightning-fast vertical escape toward the sky.

— He's bailing! Isidora shouted, pointing.

81 reacted in a fraction of a second, leaping at lightning speed, his hand closing around the Assimilated's ankle before he had fully re-formed.

— Where do you think you're going?

The Assimilated, half materialized, twisted his body with brute violence and brought his free foot down square on 81's jaw, the force of the impact enough to make him let go.

81 was hurled backward, crashing into the rubble of a building, while the Assimilated took advantage of that second of respite to complete his dematerialization, disappearing for good into the sky in a trail of dark particles.

— ...

Silence abruptly fell over the devastated battlefield.

81 slowly got up, spitting out a little blood, his gaze fixed on the point in the sky where the Assimilated had just vanished.

— ...He ran off.

— Well, at least it was fun, Isidora remarked, finally putting her phone away. So, what do we do now?

Isidora Néant stood frozen for a second, staring at the point in the sky where the Assimilated had just disappeared — then her face suddenly contorted, going from total amusement to disproportionate fury.

— GODDAMN FUCKING SHIT!

Her fist flew without warning, smashing into the remains of an already half-destroyed building — the entire structure collapsed, bringing two neighboring buildings down with it in a monumental crash.

— NOBODY DIED, THERE'S NO CONTENT, DAMN IT, DAMN IT AND DAMN IT AGAIN, YOU LITTLE DICKS!

81, still half sprawled in the rubble, slowly turned his head toward her, one eyebrow raised.

— ...

— Fine, fine, I'm calming down, she grumbled, shaking her hand as if the punch had bothered her more than expected.

Agent 47, unfazed as ever, put his weapon back in its holster.

— The fight is over.

— Yeah, well, that's exactly the problem, Isidora grumbled, crossing her arms. Three hours of live, a boss who bails without dying, no memorable death, my followers are gonna curse me.

Takeshi Ashford, still hiding with Lucifer Morningstar, exchanged an incredulous look with him.

— ...

— She's really more worried about her views than about the Incarnation of Chaos who just escaped, Takeshi murmured.

— You're only just starting to understand who she is, Lucifer answered, slowly shaking his head.

Poppy, still motionless in the middle of the debris of the shattered domain, slowly turned her head toward Isidora — her expression, still perfectly neutral, not having changed once since her appearance.

— ...

Isidora noticed the look, turning toward her with a smile already taking shape again despite her earlier anger.

— What, you want your share of the content shitstorm too? We can do a duet if you want, I've still got battery.

codex-t2-c5.title: Chapter 4 — Let's Go Home, Damn It, I'm Hungry!
codex-t2-c5.html:
Poppy slowly turned her head toward Isidora, her movement as mechanical as ever, her face still perfectly neutral.

— It's been a while.

— Yeah, totally, Isidora answered, pointing her phone at her out of reflex before thinking better of it and putting it away. You've still got that creepy doll face, nice to see nothing changes.

— ...

— So 81 is free, Poppy went on, her gaze sliding toward the colossus still sprawled in the rubble. You could have warned me.

— Well, it happened fast, okay, Isidora pleaded, shrugging. One day you're chilling, minding your business, the next, bam, your nephew shows up with a demonic pact and the whole game changes.

81 straightened up with difficulty, wiping the blood off his chin, his one-eyed gaze settling on Poppy with new attention.

— Who's she?

— Poppy, Isidora introduced. Hunter of things and people, very good at what she does, a bit of a psychopath around the edges, but we love her anyway.

Takeshi Ashford, still frozen behind his concrete block, felt his heart speed up all at once at hearing the name spoken so openly.

— ...

— She's here for me, he murmured to Lucifer Morningstar, his voice tense.

— Sure looks that way, Lucifer answered, his gaze remaining fixed on the scene with new caution.

Poppy, as if she had heard despite the distance, slowly turned her head toward the concrete block — her empty, fixed gaze settling directly on the spot where Takeshi was hiding.

— ...

A heavy silence settled, broken only by the wind sweeping across the smoking rubble of the destroyed city.

Poppy stood motionless for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on Takeshi Ashford, before tilting her head slightly — a slow movement, almost too fluid to look natural.

— Haven't I seen you before?

— Yes, Takeshi answered, his voice trembling slightly despite himself. You tried to kill me in my apartment. Everyone has their own way of getting acquainted.

— ...

Poppy stared at him for a few more seconds, her expression still perfectly neutral, not a trace of emotion showing on her doll's face. Then she slowly looked away, as if the information had just been filed somewhere.

— Fine. Since 81 puts up with you, I'll do the same. Besides, Isidora knows you, so it'll be fine.

Takeshi blinked, the tension leaving his shoulders slightly without disappearing completely.

— ...Does that mean you're not going to try to kill me anymore?

— For now.

— That's... reassuring.

Isidora Néant burst out laughing, slapping Takeshi on the back hard enough to make him stumble.

— Ah, that's Poppy for you, warm as ever. You'll get used to it.

81, still standing in the middle of the rubble, crossed his arms, his one-eyed gaze moving from Poppy to Takeshi and then to Isidora.

— Can someone explain to me why everyone here seems to know each other except me?

— Long story, Lucifer Morningstar answered, finally stepping out of his hiding place with Takeshi. We'll fill you in later.

Agent 47, silent throughout the exchange, adjusted his weapon against his shoulder, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Riper reports that the Assimilated has completely disappeared from the radar. No trace of his current position.

— Cool cool cool, Isidora said, stretching. So what now? Do we go home? I'm hungry.

While Poppy, 81, Lucifer and Takeshi talked over what had just happened — Isidora was pacing in circles in the middle of the rubble, completely indifferent to the discussion.

— WHEN ARE WE GOING HOME, DAMN IT, I'M STARVING!

— ...

No one reacted. Lucifer was still explaining to 81 how Poppy had, without even realizing it at first, begun hampering the Assimilated's chaotic domain long before her visible appearance — a consequence of her own hunt, focused on Takeshi, which was eating away at the area of effect without her knowing it herself.

— Seriously, is anyone listening to me? I'M STARVING!

— We got it, Isidora, Lucifer sighed without even turning his head. Five minutes.

— You always say five minutes and then it's three hours. I know how this goes.

She walked over to the group, planting herself right between Lucifer and Poppy, cutting the conversation short.

— Anyway, so basically, 81 summed up, she's the one who was blocking his power from the start without meaning to.

Poppy stayed silent for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on the point in the sky where the Assimilated had disappeared.

— ...

— That explains the 99%, Lucifer added. Your hunt must already have been spreading across the area before you even appeared physically.

— I was only looking for him, she said, her gaze sliding toward Takeshi. Nothing more.

Takeshi felt an unpleasant shiver run down his spine.

— ...So basically, if I hadn't been hunted by you, the Assimilated might have won.

— Possibly, Poppy answered, without the slightest emotion in her voice.

— EXCUSE ME? Isidora exploded, completely ignoring the importance of the revelation. WHEN. ARE. WE. GOING.

81 let out a grunt that vaguely resembled a laugh.

— You really have no priorities, do you.

— MY PRIORITY IS MY STOMACH, THANK YOU.

Lucifer slowly massaged his temples, returning nonetheless to the original question.

— We're first going to finish figuring out why Poppy had such an impact on his domain, Isidora.

— Okay, but then we eat.

— Then we eat, he confirmed, resigned, before turning back to Poppy. That level of disruption... that's not normal for a simple hunt, is it?

Poppy looked at him, her expression still perfectly neutral.

— No. It's not normal.

— SHUT UP! Isidora shouted. WE'RE GOING TO EAT, DAMN IT, OR I'LL TAKE YOUR BIG FOREHEADS AND MAKE A TACO OUT OF THEM, SO LET'S GO!

She grabbed Lucifer's hand on one side, Poppy's on the other, without the slightest ounce of hesitation, as if she were dragging two unruly kids out of a toy store.

— ...

81 stood frozen on the spot, his one-eyed gaze moving from the scene to Takeshi, completely stunned, unable to come up with any reaction.

— ...

— You too, Isidora called out, half turning to point her chin at 81 without letting go of the two hands she was already holding. Move your butt.

— ...She just literally took our hands like we're five years old, 81 finally managed to say, addressing Takeshi as if seeking confirmation that the scene was really happening.

— Yeah. Welcome to the group, Takeshi answered with a crooked smile.

Lucifer, his hand still captive, let out a long resigned sigh, as if this kind of treatment were nothing unusual for him at all.

— Isidora, I am the King of Hell.

— So what? I'm the Witch of the Void, we're even on long-winded titles, come on, let's move.

Poppy, for her part, simply stared at her own captive hand with an expression still perfectly neutral, as if analyzing a new and incomprehensible phenomenon.

— ...

— Is she really going to drag us like this all the way to wherever we're eating? Takeshi asked, falling into step despite himself.

— With Isidora, anything is possible, Lucifer answered, letting himself be dragged along without resisting anymore.

Agent 47 followed the group at a distance, his measured stride contrasting with the general agitation, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Riper, analysis.

"Analyzing..."

— I want to be sure this is not some outside mental manipulation. Confirm that the observed scene corresponds to reality.

A short silence, then Reaper's synthetic voice rang out again.

"Full sweep complete. No psychic, illusory or dimensional manipulation signature detected in the area."

— ...

"Formal confirmation: Isidora is currently dragging Lucifer Morningstar, King of Hell, and Poppy, interdimensional hunting entity, by the hand, like children. This scene is reality."

47 stayed silent for a moment, his gaze fixed on the scene before him — Isidora still in the lead, pulling her two improvised hostages, Takeshi and 81 following as best they could, each with a different expression ranging from resignation to total astonishment.

— ...Understood.

"Would you like a supplementary psychological analysis on the subject Isidora?"

— No. That will not be necessary.

"Recommendation archived."

47 picked up his pace slightly to catch up with the group, his face as impassive as ever despite everything he had just confirmed.

— The situation has been verified, he announced simply as he drew level with them. No outside manipulation. It's real.

81 turned his head toward him, almost despairing.

— You really needed to ask your AI if this was real.

— As a precaution.

— It's Isidora, not a cosmic threat.

— That is precisely the precaution in question, 47 answered, unfazed.

Isidora, without even turning around, tightened her grip on Lucifer's and Poppy's hands.

— I CAN HEAR EVERYTHING YOU'RE SAYING, YOU TRAITORS, WE'RE GOING TO EAT NOW!

The same explosion suddenly tore through the air in front of them — a burst of black and red particles materializing the Assimilated once again, his body fully re-formed, his wounds erased, an aura much denser than before crackling all around him.

— ...

The whole group froze. 81 instinctively reached for his sword, Lucifer stiffened, Takeshi took a step back, Agent 47 was already raising his weapon.

— Did you really think I would flee forever? the Assimilated enunciated, his voice charged with new power. I have returned more—

Isidora didn't even let him finish his sentence.

She instantly let go of Lucifer's and Poppy's hands, shot forward in a flash, and brought her right fist down square in the Assimilated's face with such violence that the air itself split under the impact.

— GET LOST, I'M STARVING!

The Assimilated literally disappeared before the blow even really touched him — an instant, preventive disintegration, as if his own body had understood that taking that punch meant certain and irreversible death.

Silence fell again.

— ...

81 stood with his mouth half open, staring at the empty spot where the Assimilated had been standing a second earlier.

— ...He literally just vanished so he wouldn't take your punch.

— Yeah, well, he should've gotten lost faster, Isidora grumbled, shaking her hand as if the gesture had stung her a little too. I'm starving, I don't have time to waste on this kind of crap.

Poppy stared at the scene, her neutral expression slightly strained toward something that almost resembled surprise.

— ...

Agent 47 slowly lowered his weapon, his earpiece crackling.

— Riper, calculate the Assimilated's probability of survival against that blow if it had connected.

"Calculating... 0%. Total destruction, no regeneration possible."

— ...That was her weakest blow since the start of the scene, 47 added, almost to himself.

Takeshi, still in shock, slowly turned his head toward Isidora.

— You just... you literally just made a Higher Incarnation of Chaos run away because you were hungry.

— Exactly. So, CAN WE GO NOW?

Lucifer massaged his temples once again, taking back the hand Isidora had let go of in the meantime and holding it out to her again without even thinking.

— ...Fine, let's eat.

The Assimilated materialized in the heart of the Imperial Palace, his body still marked by the traces of the fight, yet his gait keeping a furious, almost humiliated stiffness.

He crossed the corridors without a word, without a glance at the guards who instinctively stepped aside as he passed, until he reached the great doors of a hall reserved for the Higher Incarnations.

He opened them with a simple gesture, the residual power of his still unstable domain enough to slam them against the walls.

— ...

Inside, several Incarnations turned toward him. Some silent, others already exchanging knowing looks — news of his defeat had visibly spread faster than he had.

Tempus, sitting off to the side, his piercing gaze fixed on the Assimilated since he came in, was the first to speak.

— So. The rumor is true.

— Shut up, Tempus.

— A God Killer set free, a Witch of the Void, a hunting entity, and you come back without even a single victim to your name. Impressive.

The Assimilated clenched his fists, his domain crackling faintly around him, still unstable after his hasty escape.

— Where is KJ. I want to speak to him.

A heavy silence crossed the hall. Several Incarnations looked away, uncomfortable.

Tempus slowly stood up, his expression as impassive as ever.

— KJ isn't here.

— ...What?

— He's been gone for several days. No one knows where. Even the Palace Demon doesn't know.

The Assimilated stood frozen for a moment, his golden gaze sweeping the hall, seeking confirmation in the other faces present.

— Impossible. KJ never leaves the Palace without informing his own.

— And yet, Tempus answered, crossing his arms. It's the first time in several millennia that it's happened.

A worried murmur ran through the hall, the other Incarnations exchanging increasingly tense looks.

— ...Then who is in charge, in his absence?

No one answered right away.

— No one, Tempus finally said, his voice suddenly graver. And that may be the real problem.

Another silence settled, broken a few moments later by the slow opening of the great doors.

Void walked in, his presence alone enough to silence the last murmurs in the hall, his domain of hallucinatory fog seeming to precede him by several meters.

— KJ let me know that I am the one taking command in his absence.

— ...

Tempus tilted his head slightly, with no apparent surprise.

— That explains the silence of the past few days.

Void swept the hall with his gaze, his cold, corrupted expression finally stopping on the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of the fight, his domain still unstable.

— ...

A slow, almost cruel smile formed on his face.

— Well, well. You. The great Incarnation who's been drilling it into us for millennia that you're superior to us. You just got beaten by a fucking streamer who was hungry.

— ...

The Assimilated clenched his jaw, his domain crackling dangerously around him.

— I was not beaten. I made a tactical choice.

— A tactical choice, Void repeated, visibly savoring every word. Is that what we call disappearing before the blow even touches you now?

A few muffled snickers ran through the hall. Tempus himself did nothing to hide them.

— You weren't there, the Assimilated spat. You know nothing of what I faced.

— What I know above all is that the God Killer is free, that he has an improvised army made up of a suicidal streamer, Grand Patron Luigi's right-hand man, and a hunting entity talented enough to wreck your domain without even meaning to. That, yes, I know.

Void walked forward slowly, settling onto what looked like a secondary throne at the back of the hall, his gaze never leaving the Assimilated.

— And now that I'm in charge, in KJ's absence, I'm going to have to decide what to do with this lovely mess you left behind.

— ...

— So the next time you open those doors in a fit of wounded pride, Void enunciated, his voice icy, at least make sure you have a victory to tell. Because right now, all you've brought back is your shame.

The doors opened once more, more slowly this time, an icy and absolute aura preceding the entrance of Akuma.

— ...

Silence fell instantly, even heavier than the one caused by Void's arrival.

— All of you are going to shut up now.

No one dared answer.

Akuma walked to the center of the hall, her gaze slowly passing over each Incarnation present before stopping on Void, still seated on his secondary throne.

— And you, Void. Stop saying KJ entrusts you with anything. Let alone the entire Palace.

— ...

— We, the Incarnations — it's logical, he ranked us. So if he isn't here, I'm the one who takes command.

Void clenched his jaw, his domain wavering slightly around him — a palpable tension, but no open challenge. Even he seemed to understand that he didn't carry enough weight against Akuma on this ground.

— ...

Akuma then turned her gaze to the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of his confrontation, his domain still unstable.

— And you, Assimilated. You're going back with Tempus to kill that little group and bring me their heads. And their dicks. But that's secondary.

— ...

Tempus slowly rose from his seat, his expression as impassive as ever despite the order.

— Directly? Without any further preparation?

— You control time individually, Akuma answered, her voice cold and final. Use that fucking ability for once instead of sitting there commenting on other people's failures.

Tempus added nothing, a slight bitter crease crossing his usually neutral face.

The Assimilated, for his part, slowly raised his head, a new — almost desperate — determination replacing the shame that had still marked his face a few moments earlier.

— This time, I will not return without a victory.

— I should hope so, Akuma answered, already turning away, as if the conversation no longer deserved her attention. Anyway. Go.

Tempus and the Assimilated exchanged one last look before heading together toward the exit of the hall, the doors slowly closing behind them in a heavy silence.

The group had finally ended up seated in a small taco restaurant, several states away from Washington — a forced move, not so much out of fear of being hunted by cosmic forces, but simply because the entire state had just been wiped off the map.

— ...

Takeshi stared at his plate without touching it, still visibly shaken by the events of the last few hours. Lucifer, sitting across from him, seemed just as disinclined to eat, his gaze lost in space. Poppy, motionless as always, hadn't even ordered anything. 81, despite his massive build, was just staring at his food with an unreadable expression. Agent 47 hadn't ordered anything at all, simply discreetly scanning the room.

Isidora, for her part, was already devouring her third taco.

— Seriously, nobody's eating? We just accidentally wrecked an entire country and you're picking at tacos?

— ...

No one answered. 81 finally set down his fork, unable to work up an appetite despite his natural hunger.

— I can't. Like, mentally, I can't.

— Well, I can, Isidora answered, moving straight on to a fourth taco. I missed three meals today, I can't afford to go "oh no, too much trauma to eat."

She swallowed the taco in two bites, then, her plate now empty, she stared at it for a moment before bringing it straight to her mouth.

— ...

— Isidora, Lucifer began, in a cautious tone.

CRUNCH.

She bit straight into the ceramic plate, chewing as naturally as if she were eating a simple cookie.

— Isidora, you're eating the plate, Takeshi managed to say, completely overwhelmed by the scene.

— Yeah, well, I'm still hungry and the waiter's taking forever, she answered, her mouth full of ceramic shards.

Poppy slowly turned her head toward her, her neutral expression slightly more frozen than usual.

— ...

Once the plate had been entirely swallowed, Isidora looked around, visibly searching for her next target. Her eyes landed on the table.

— ...Isidora, no, Lucifer tried.

— Isidora, yes, she answered, before sinking her teeth straight into the edge of the wooden table.

CRACK.

A whole chunk came away under the pressure of her jaw, which she chewed with the same casualness as everything else.

81 pushed his chair back slightly, staring at the scene with a mixture of horror and fascination.

— ...How does she not hurt herself eating that?

— Nobody knows, Lucifer answered, resigned. We stopped asking that question centuries ago.

The rest of the table kept being methodically devoured, piece by piece, until there was nothing left but a lone leg, somehow still balancing upright.

— ...And there we go, Isidora concluded, satisfied, before leaning toward the floor.

— NO, Takeshi and 81 exclaimed in unison.

Too late. She had already sunk her teeth into the tiles, ripping off an entire piece with a sharp, sinister crack, under the stunned gaze of the restaurant's other customers.

— It's actually crunchy, she remarked, calmly chewing. A bit bland, but crunchy.

Agent 47, still impassive, murmured discreetly into his earpiece.

— Riper. Note for future report: Isidora has just eaten a plate, a table, and a restaurant floor.

"Noted. No biological anomaly detected. Usual behavior confirmed."

Agent 47, still impassive despite the scene, spoke into his earpiece a second time, as if he needed additional confirmation.

— Riper. New analysis. Confirm that this is not a collective hallucination or an outside mental manipulation affecting my perception.

A silence slightly longer than usual preceded the answer.

"No. She's genuinely just a lunatic."

— ...

47 froze for a second, his usually impassive face showing, for the very first time, the tiniest shift — one eyebrow slightly raised.

— ...Riper, your answer contains an emotional inflection.

"Affirmative."

— You are an artificial intelligence.

"Affirmative. And yet."

47 slowly lowered his gaze to Isidora, who had just ripped off a second piece of tile with obvious pleasure, chewing noisily under the ever-despairing gaze of the rest of the group.

— ...Explain.

"I have analyzed primordial deities, Higher Incarnations, cosmic anomalies, and Grand Patron Luigi himself during his millennial meltdowns. None of these subjects has generated this level of..."

A pause, almost hesitant, as if even the AI were searching for its words.

"...calculated dismay."

81, who had followed the exchange from his chair, couldn't hold back a nervous burst of laughter.

— Even the AI is overwhelmed.

— Riper is never overwhelmed, 47 answered, almost defensively.

"Correction: I am never overwhelmed. I am, however, currently recalculating the theoretical limits of my own definition of 'normal.'"

Isidora, vaguely hearing the conversation despite her full mouth, turned toward 47 with a predatory smile, one last piece of tile still stuck between her teeth.

— Is your AI talking about me?

— It is simply confirming your condition, 47 answered soberly.

— Cool. Tell it thanks from me.

"...I do not accept thanks from subjects classified as 'non-hostile but exhausting behavioral anomaly.'"

Takeshi nearly choked on the water he had finally brought himself to drink.

— It just literally roasted you, Isidora.

— Oh, did it? she answered, not the least bit affected, before turning to the waiter approaching, visibly terrified. EXCUSE ME, YOU WOULDN'T HAVE A SPARE CHAIR? THAT ONE LOOKS GOOD TOO.

The waiter approached cautiously, carrying on his tray the 261st taco of the minute, his hands trembling slightly under the combined weight of exhaustion and pure terror.

Isidora slowly turned her head toward him.

— ...

Her gaze slid from the taco... to the waiter himself. A slow, far too interested smile formed on her face, her eyes looking him over with an appetite that suddenly had very little to do with the food set in front of her.

— ...

81 was the first to react, his chair scraping loudly across the floor, he stood up so fast.

— NO!

— NO! Takeshi chimed in, nearly knocking over his glass of water.

— Negative, Lucifer added, one hand already raised in formal prohibition.

47 stood up as well, his hand settling firmly on the waiter's shoulder to pull him back, out of reach.

— No.

"Confirmation: NO," even Reaper added directly in 47's earpiece, with a brand-new urgency in its synthesized voice.

Isidora blinked, slowly coming out of her trance, a disappointed pout twisting her face.

— What, I was just looking.

— You were looking like you were gonna eat him, literally, 81 retorted, still half standing, ready to step in physically if necessary.

— I'm hungry, can't I just visually appreciate my options?

— NOT WHEN YOUR OPTIONS INCLUDE A LIVING HUMAN BEING, Takeshi shouted, completely panicked.

The waiter, ashen, took another step back, the tray trembling dangerously in his hands.

— Can I... can I just put the taco down and leave?

— YES, 81, Takeshi, Lucifer and 47 answered in unison.

Poppy, the only one who had remained perfectly still throughout the scene, finally turned her head toward Isidora, her expression as neutral as ever.

— Would you really have eaten him?

— Well, I dunno, I've never tried, Isidora answered with a perfectly sincere shrug.

— ...

— SOMEBODY WATCHES HER AT ALL TIMES FROM NOW ON, 81 decreed, slowly sitting back down but keeping a wary eye on her.

The waiter set down the taco at record speed before hurrying back toward the kitchen, visibly traumatized for life.

— Well, Isidora sighed, picking her taco back up as if nothing had happened. He wasn't bad, the little guy, too bad.

— ISIDORA.

— WHAT? I'M TALKING ABOUT THE TACO, NOT THE WAITER, WELL, I THINK.

The group finally left the restaurant, leaving behind a traumatized waiter and a bill Isidora had categorically refused to pay "because technically I ate the table, that counts as compensation."

Isidora, on her way out the door, stopped for a second in front of the restaurant's glass pane.

— ...

— Isidora, no, Takeshi immediately tried, already recognizing the look.

— Isidora, yes.

CRUNCH.

She bit straight into the glass door, tearing off an entire piece with a sinister crack, chewing the glass with the same casualness as everything else.

81, holding the door half open to let the group through, stared at the scene with an almost resigned weariness.

— It's not really a surprise at this point.

Nearby, a customer seated on the terrace, completely petrified since the start of the meal, instinctively tightened his arms around his own tray of food, as if to make sure she wasn't targeting that too.

Isidora turned her head toward him, one eyebrow raised, her mouth still full of glass shards.

— Relax, I only want the door.

The customer nodded frantically, not daring to answer.

Lucifer, bringing up the rear, cast one last apologetic glance at the devastated restaurant behind them — door half devoured, table in pieces, floor full of holes, plates gone.

— We should probably leave a monumental tip next time.

— Or just avoid restaurants, Takeshi suggested.

— Where's the fun in that, Isidora retorted, swallowing the last piece of glass with a satisfied click of her tongue.
