I'm starving, I don't have time to waste on this kind of crap. Poppy stared at the scene, her neutral expression slightly strained toward something that almost resembled surprise. — ... Agent 47 slowly lowered his weapon, his earpiece crackling. — Riper, calculate the Assimilated's probability of survival against that blow if it had connected. "Calculating... 0%. Total destruction, no regeneration possible." — ...That was her weakest blow since the start of the scene, 47 added, almost to himself. Takeshi, still in shock, slowly turned his head toward Isidora. — You just... you literally just made a Higher Incarnation of Chaos run away because you were hungry. — Exactly. So, CAN WE GO NOW? Lucifer massaged his temples once again, taking back the hand Isidora had let go of in the meantime and holding it out to her again without even thinking. — ...Fine, let's eat. The Assimilated materialized in the heart of the Imperial Palace, his body still marked by the traces of the fight, yet his gait keeping a furious, almost humiliated stiffness. He crossed the corridors without a word, without a glance at the guards who instinctively stepped aside as he passed, until he reached the great doors of a hall reserved for the Higher Incarnations. He opened them with a simple gesture, the residual power of his still unstable domain enough to slam them against the walls. — ... Inside, several Incarnations turned toward him. Some silent, others already exchanging knowing looks — news of his defeat had visibly spread faster than he had. Tempus, sitting off to the side, his piercing gaze fixed on the Assimilated since he came in, was the first to speak. — So. The rumor is true. — Shut up, Tempus. — A God Killer set free, a Witch of the Void, a hunting entity, and you come back without even a single victim to your name. Impressive. The Assimilated clenched his fists, his domain crackling faintly around him, still unstable after his hasty escape. — Where is KJ. I want to speak to him. A heavy silence crossed the hall. Several Incarnations looked away, uncomfortable. Tempus slowly stood up, his expression as impassive as ever. — KJ isn't here. — ...What? — He's been gone for several days. No one knows where. Even the Palace Demon doesn't know. The Assimilated stood frozen for a moment, his golden gaze sweeping the hall, seeking confirmation in the other faces present. — Impossible. KJ never leaves the Palace without informing his own. — And yet, Tempus answered, crossing his arms. It's the first time in several millennia that it's happened. A worried murmur ran through the hall, the other Incarnations exchanging increasingly tense looks. — ...Then who is in charge, in his absence? No one answered right away. — No one, Tempus finally said, his voice suddenly graver. And that may be the real problem. Another silence settled, broken a few moments later by the slow opening of the great doors. Void walked in, his presence alone enough to silence the last murmurs in the hall, his domain of hallucinatory fog seeming to precede him by several meters. — KJ let me know that I am the one taking command in his absence. — ... Tempus tilted his head slightly, with no apparent surprise. — That explains the silence of the past few days. Void swept the hall with his gaze, his cold, corrupted expression finally stopping on the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of the fight, his domain still unstable. — ... A slow, almost cruel smile formed on his face. — Well, well. You. The great Incarnation who's been drilling it into us for millennia that you're superior to us. You just got beaten by a fucking streamer who was hungry. — ... The Assimilated clenched his jaw, his domain crackling dangerously around him. — I was not beaten. I made a tactical choice. — A tactical choice, Void repeated, visibly savoring every word. Is that what we call disappearing before the blow even touches you now? A few muffled snickers ran through the hall. Tempus himself did nothing to hide them. — You weren't there, the Assimilated spat. You know nothing of what I faced. — What I know above all is that the God Killer is free, that he has an improvised army made up of a suicidal streamer, Grand Patron Luigi's right-hand man, and a hunting entity talented enough to wreck your domain without even meaning to. That, yes, I know. Void walked forward slowly, settling onto what looked like a secondary throne at the back of the hall, his gaze never leaving the Assimilated. — And now that I'm in charge, in KJ's absence, I'm going to have to decide what to do with this lovely mess you left behind. — ... — So the next time you open those doors in a fit of wounded pride, Void enunciated, his voice icy, at least make sure you have a victory to tell. Because right now, all you've brought back is your shame. The doors opened once more, more slowly this time, an icy and absolute aura preceding the entrance of Akuma. — ... Silence fell instantly, even heavier than the one caused by Void's arrival. — All of you are going to shut up now. No one dared answer. Akuma walked to the center of the hall, her gaze slowly passing over each Incarnation present before stopping on Void, still seated on his secondary throne. — And you, Void. Stop saying KJ entrusts you with anything. Let alone the entire Palace. — ... — We, the Incarnations — it's logical, he ranked us. So if he isn't here, I'm the one who takes command. Void clenched his jaw, his domain wavering slightly around him — a palpable tension, but no open challenge. Even he seemed to understand that he didn't carry enough weight against Akuma on this ground. — ... Akuma then turned her gaze to the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of his confrontation, his domain still unstable. — And you, Assimilated. You're going back with Tempus to kill that little group and bring me their heads. And their dicks. But that's secondary. — ... Tempus slowly rose from his seat, his expression as impassive as ever despite the order. — Directly? Without any further preparation? — You control time individually, Akuma answered, her voice cold and final. Use that fucking ability for once instead of sitting there commenting on other people's failures. Tempus added nothing, a slight bitter crease crossing his usually neutral face. The Assimilated, for his part, slowly raised his head, a new — almost desperate — determination replacing the shame that had still marked his face a few moments earlier. — This time, I will not return without a victory. — I should hope so, Akuma answered, already turning away, as if the conversation no longer deserved her attention. Anyway. Go. Tempus and the Assimilated exchanged one last look before heading together toward the exit of the hall, the doors slowly closing behind them in a heavy silence. The group had finally ended up seated in a small taco restaurant, several states away from Washington — a forced move, not so much out of fear of being hunted by cosmic forces, but simply because the entire state had just been wiped off the map. — ... Takeshi stared at his plate without touching it, still visibly shaken by the events of the last few hours. Lucifer, sitting across from him, seemed just as disinclined to eat, his gaze lost in space. Poppy, motionless as always, hadn't even ordered anything. 81, despite his massive build, was just staring at his food with an unreadable expression. Agent 47 hadn't ordered anything at all, simply discreetly scanning the room. Isidora, for her part, was already devouring her third taco. — Seriously, nobody's eating? We just accidentally wrecked an entire country and you're picking at tacos? — ... No one answered. 81 finally set down his fork, unable to work up an appetite despite his natural hunger. — I can't. Like, mentally, I can't. — Well, I can, Isidora answered, moving straight on to a fourth taco. I missed three meals today, I can't afford to go "oh no, too much trauma to eat." She swallowed the taco in two bites, then, her plate now empty, she stared at it for a moment before bringing it straight to her mouth. — ... — Isidora, Lucifer began, in a cautious tone. CRUNCH. She bit straight into the ceramic plate, chewing as naturally as if she were eating a simple cookie. — Isidora, you're eating the plate, Takeshi managed to say, completely overwhelmed by the scene. — Yeah, well, I'm still hungry and the waiter's taking forever, she answered, her mouth full of ceramic shards. Poppy slowly turned her head toward her, her neutral expression slightly more frozen than usual. — ... Once the plate had been entirely swallowed, Isidora looked around, visibly searching for her next target. Her eyes landed on the table. — ...Isidora, no, Lucifer tried. — Isidora, yes, she answered, before sinking her teeth straight into the edge of the wooden table. CRACK. A whole chunk came away under the pressure of her jaw, which she chewed with the same casualness as everything else. 81 pushed his chair back slightly, staring at the scene with a mixture of horror and fascination. — ...How does she not hurt herself eating that? — Nobody knows, Lucifer answered, resigned. We stopped asking that question centuries ago. The rest of the table kept being methodically devoured, piece by piece, until there was nothing left but a lone leg, somehow still balancing upright. — ...And there we go, Isidora concluded, satisfied, before leaning toward the floor. — NO, Takeshi and 81 exclaimed in unison. Too late. She had already sunk her teeth into the tiles, ripping off an entire piece with a sharp, sinister crack, under the stunned gaze of the restaurant's other customers. — It's actually crunchy, she remarked, calmly chewing. A bit bland, but crunchy. Agent 47, still impassive, murmured discreetly into his earpiece. — Riper. Note for future report: Isidora has just eaten a plate, a table, and a restaurant floor. "Noted. No biological anomaly detected. Usual behavior confirmed." Agent 47, still impassive despite the scene, spoke into his earpiece a second time, as if he needed additional confirmation. — Riper. New analysis. Confirm that this is not a collective hallucination or an outside mental manipulation affecting my perception. A silence slightly longer than usual preceded the answer. "No. She's genuinely just a lunatic." — ... 47 froze for a second, his usually impassive face showing, for the very first time, the tiniest shift — one eyebrow slightly raised. — ...Riper, your answer contains an emotional inflection. "Affirmative." — You are an artificial intelligence. "Affirmative. And yet." 47 slowly lowered his gaze to Isidora, who had just ripped off a second piece of tile with obvious pleasure, chewing noisily under the ever-despairing gaze of the rest of the group. — ...Explain. "I have analyzed primordial deities, Higher Incarnations, cosmic anomalies, and Grand Patron Luigi himself during his millennial meltdowns. None of these subjects has generated this level of..." A pause, almost hesitant, as if even the AI were searching for its words. "...calculated dismay." 81, who had followed the exchange from his chair, couldn't hold back a nervous burst of laughter. — Even the AI is overwhelmed. — Riper is never overwhelmed, 47 answered, almost defensively. "Correction: I am never overwhelmed. I am, however, currently recalculating the theoretical limits of my own definition of 'normal.'" Isidora, vaguely hearing the conversation despite her full mouth, turned toward 47 with a predatory smile, one last piece of tile still stuck between her teeth. — Is your AI talking about me? — It is simply confirming your condition, 47 answered soberly. — Cool. Tell it thanks from me. "...I do not accept thanks from subjects classified as 'non-hostile but exhausting behavioral anomaly.'" Takeshi nearly choked on the water he had finally brought himself to drink. — It just literally roasted you, Isidora. — Oh, did it? she answered, not the least bit affected, before turning to the waiter approaching, visibly terrified. EXCUSE ME, YOU WOULDN'T HAVE A SPARE CHAIR? THAT ONE LOOKS GOOD TOO. The waiter approached cautiously, carrying on his tray the 261st taco of the minute, his hands trembling slightly under the combined weight of exhaustion and pure terror. Isidora slowly turned her head toward him. — ... Her gaze slid from the taco... to the waiter himself. A slow, far too interested smile formed on her face, her eyes looking him over with an appetite that suddenly had very little to do with the food set in front of her. — ... 81 was the first to react, his chair scraping loudly across the floor, he stood up so fast. — NO! — NO! Takeshi chimed in, nearly knocking over his glass of water. — Negative, Lucifer added, one hand already raised in formal prohibition. 47 stood up as well, his hand settling firmly on the waiter's shoulder to pull him back, out of reach. — No. "Confirmation: NO," even Reaper added directly in 47's earpiece, with a brand-new urgency in its synthesized voice. Isidora blinked, slowly coming out of her trance, a disappointed pout twisting her face. — What, I was just looking. — You were looking like you were gonna eat him, literally, 81 retorted, still half standing, ready to step in physically if necessary. — I'm hungry, can't I just visually appreciate my options? — NOT WHEN YOUR OPTIONS INCLUDE A LIVING HUMAN BEING, Takeshi shouted, completely panicked. The waiter, ashen, took another step back, the tray trembling dangerously in his hands. — Can I... can I just put the taco down and leave? — YES, 81, Takeshi, Lucifer and 47 answered in unison. Poppy, the only one who had remained perfectly still throughout the scene, finally turned her head toward Isidora, her expression as neutral as ever. — Would you really have eaten him? — Well, I dunno, I've never tried, Isidora answered with a perfectly sincere shrug. — ... — SOMEBODY WATCHES HER AT ALL TIMES FROM NOW ON, 81 decreed, slowly sitting back down but keeping a wary eye on her. The waiter set down the taco at record speed before hurrying back toward the kitchen, visibly traumatized for life. — Well, Isidora sighed, picking her taco back up as if nothing had happened. He wasn't bad, the little guy, too bad. — ISIDORA. — WHAT? I'M TALKING ABOUT THE TACO, NOT THE WAITER, WELL, I THINK. The group finally left the restaurant, leaving behind a traumatized waiter and a bill Isidora had categorically refused to pay "because technically I ate the table, that counts as compensation." Isidora, on her way out the door, stopped for a second in front of the restaurant's glass pane. — ... — Isidora, no, Takeshi immediately tried, already recognizing the look. — Isidora, yes. CRUNCH. She bit straight into the glass door, tearing off an entire piece with a sinister crack, chewing the glass with the same casualness as everything else. 81, holding the door half open to let the group through, stared at the scene with an almost resigned weariness. — It's not really a surprise at this point. Nearby, a customer seated on the terrace, completely petrified since the start of the meal, instinctively tightened his arms around his own tray of food, as if to make sure she wasn't targeting that too. Isidora turned her head toward him, one eyebrow raised, her mouth still full of glass shards. — Relax, I only want the door. The customer nodded frantically, not daring to answer. Lucifer, bringing up the rear, cast one last apologetic glance at the devastated restaurant behind them — door half devoured, table in pieces, floor full of holes, plates gone. — We should probably leave a monumental tip next time. — Or just avoid restaurants, Takeshi suggested. — Where's the fun in that, Isidora retorted, swallowing the last piece of glass with a satisfied click of her tongue.

codex-t2-c6.title: Chapter 5 — Death's Incarnation Is on Snap
codex-t2-c6.html:
81, still walking alongside the group, suddenly seemed to remember something — his revenge list, still in progress, with the Incarnation of Death, vanished from every reality, remaining his most elusive target so far.

— Isidora.

— Mh?

— If you help me kill the concept of death, I'll give you the address of a place where you can get infinite food.

— ...

Isidora stopped dead. Then, with an absolutely abnormal slowness, she began to turn her head toward him — a movement so gradual, so stretched out in time, that it took her literally two full minutes before 81 finally entered her field of vision.

— ...

— Can you repeat that?

— Yes, 81 answered, unfazed by this supernatural slowness. If you help me, I know a place where you'll get all the food you want, unlimited.

— FUCK, FOR UNLIMITED FOOD I'D KILL KJ IF I HAVE TO, I DON'T GIVE A SHIT, I'M HUNGRY!

Takeshi, walking right in front, spun around, completely stunned by the sudden volume.

— ...You just offered to kill KJ for an all-you-can-eat buffet.

— YEAH, SO WHAT? PRIORITIES, TAKESHI, PRIORITIES!

Lucifer massaged his temples, a gesture that had become almost automatic since the start of the day.

— We are genuinely recruiting a Witch of the Void into a cosmic vendetta against Death itself... with promises of food.

— The method clearly works very well, Agent 47 remarked, unfazed.

"Confirmation: instant buy-in rate of 100% following the food offer.", Reaper added in his earpiece.

81 crossed his arms, a satisfied smile on his lips.

— So that's settled. Isidora, you're with me on Death.

— OBVIOUSLY I'M WITH YOU, YOU THINK I WAS GONNA SAY NO TO UNLIMITED FOOD?

Poppy, still perfectly neutral, watched the exchange without a word, before finally speaking up.

— That's the most efficient thing I've seen in my entire existence.

— Thanks, 81 replied, almost proud of himself.

— It wasn't a compliment.

Takeshi sighed and started walking again, resigned to the total absurdity of the situation.

— Okay, so... we're looking for Death now, is that the plan?

— After the unlimited food, Isidora clarified, more serious than ever. Gotta check it's real first.

— It's real, 81 confirmed.

— PERFECT, LET'S GO!

The group had stopped, the reality of the problem starting to sink in.

— She erased her traces from every reality, 81 summed up, jaw clenched. Which means searching for her the normal way would take...

— How long, exactly? Takeshi asked, already dreading the answer.

47 checked his earpiece, a calculating silence settling in.

— Riper estimates somewhere between several billion years, depending on the search method used.

— ...

A heavy silence fell over the group. Lucifer rubbed his face with both hands, Takeshi literally sat down on the ground, discouraged, while 81 stared into space, visibly recalculating the scale of his revenge in his head.

— Well, that's dead then, Takeshi sighed.

— NO IT'S NOT DEAD, Isidora suddenly exclaimed, barging into the conversation completely relaxed, as if she'd only just realized a problem existed. Chill out, guys, I know where to find her.

Every eye turned to her.

— ...You know where Death is, 81 said slowly, as if he didn't dare believe it.

— Yeah. Basically, a few thousand years ago, I met her. I lent her a phone, that bitch never gave it back, but that's another story, we'll get to it later. Anyway, basically we added each other on Snap, so I've got her location, 'cause she sucks at technology, like Lulu, maybe even worse.

— EXCUSE ME? Lucifer exploded. I do NOT suck at technology!

— Lulu sweetie, you still don't know how to use a microwave.

— That's NOT the same thing!

Takeshi slowly got back up, completely dumbfounded.

— Wait. Wait wait wait. You follow Death. On Snapchat.

— Yeah.

— The entity that's been collecting souls since the dawn of time. Has a Snapchat account.

— Well yeah, she's gotta post her stories too, she has a life.

81, overwhelmed, dropped onto a nearby rock.

— ...I waited literally my entire existence for this revenge, and the solution was to ask Isidora from the start.

— Shoulda asked sooner, she replied with a shrug, already pulling out her phone to check the famous location. Okay, where is she... where is she... oh look, she posted three days ago.

Poppy came closer, glancing discreetly over her shoulder.

— What did she post?

— A picture of a sunset with the caption "another day of reaping souls, same old routine".

— ...

— She's got 2 followers, Isidora added, scrolling. It's actually sad.

Agent 47, unfazed as always, murmured into his earpiece.

— Riper. Locate the approximate GPS position associated with this account.

"Analysis in progress... Result obtained. Coordinates transmitted."

— We have a location, 47 announced.

81 leapt to his feet, a new determination crossing his face.

— Then we go. Now.

— After the unlimited food, Isidora reminded him immediately.

— ...After the unlimited food, 81 confirmed, resigned.

Reaper finally transmitted the exact coordinates, his synthesized voice ringing in 47's earpiece.

"Location confirmed. The entity matching the profile 'Death' is currently at a spa on the outskirts of Berlin."

— ...

A stunned silence fell over the group. Takeshi's jaw dropped, Lucifer blinked several times as if the information refused to register properly, 81 frowned, visibly unable to reconcile the image of his ultimate revenge with that of a Berlin spa.

— ...A spa, Takeshi repeated, his voice almost cracking. The Incarnation of Death. At a spa. In Berlin.

— Well yeah, Isidora answered, not surprised in the slightest, already putting her phone away. She loves that stuff, facials, clay masks, the whole shebang. She says it helps her unwind after millennia of reaping souls.

— ...

81 rubbed his face with both hands.

— I pictured this showdown in a cosmic void, a dimensional battlefield, a place worthy of what she represents. Not a goddamn German spa.

— Life is full of surprises, Isidora philosophized, utterly unfazed.

Poppy didn't react in the slightest, her expression as neutral as ever in the face of the news.

— ...

47 didn't show the slightest visible reaction either, merely adjusting his weapon as if the nature of the place had no operational relevance whatsoever.

— Coordinates confirmed. We can leave immediately.

Reaper, however, seemed to pause unusually before speaking again.

"...I am currently recalculating all my certainties regarding the fundamental nature of the universe."

— Again? 47 asked, almost jaded at this point.

"The functional entity responsible for collecting every soul in existence goes to a spa. I believe it is justified."

Lucifer, still in shock, turned to Isidora.

— How can you be so unsurprised by this.

— 'Cause I know her, Lulu. Seriously, last time we saw each other, she offered me a couples massage. I said no 'cause I was hungry, but the offer stood.

— ...

Takeshi put a hand to his forehead, completely overwhelmed by the pile-up of absurdities this day had brought.

— We're really going to confront Death at a spa.

— With unlimited food on the line, yes, 81 confirmed, straightening up, his determination restored despite the incongruity of the situation. Come on, let's go.

81 froze, his hand already raised to signal departure.

— ...Wait.

— What? Isidora asked, already plotting a route to Berlin on her phone.

— The Death you're talking about. The spa one. That's the soul collector, right? The one from Mortis Iterum?

— Well yeah, why?

81 slowly shook his head, a flash of frustration crossing his face.

— She's not the one I'm after. My revenge is against the Incarnation of Death. The one who created the very concept of death. Not the one who just reaps the souls afterward.

— ...

Isidora stood frozen, her finger hovering over the screen.

— Wait, there are two different deaths?

— Completely different, 81 confirmed. One made the concept. The other just handles the paperwork afterward.

— That's a super badly organized system, Isidora commented, almost outraged. They could've at least merged the positions.

Takeshi, still overwhelmed by the flood of cosmic information, raised a hesitant hand.

— So basically we were about to bother the wrong death entity at a German spa for nothing.

— Apparently, Lucifer confirmed, massaging his temples again.

47, unfazed, spoke into his earpiece again.

— Riper. Cancel the previous location. New target: the Incarnation of Death who created the concept, vanished from every reality for millennia. Distinct from the functional entity of Mortis Iterum.

"Correction recorded."

A pause.

"...This search will be considerably more complex. The previous target had an active Snapchat account."

81 turned to Isidora, a glimmer of hope returning despite the correction.

— You probably don't know this one, though.

Isidora thought for a moment, scratching her chin.

— Mmh... nope, I don't know that one personally. But that means we're actually gonna have to search.

— Billions of years, Takeshi reminded them, almost in despair.

— Or, Poppy suggested, speaking up for the first time in a while, we use someone capable of tracking anyone, anywhere, even entities that have erased every trace of themselves.

Every eye slowly turned to her.

— ...You, Takeshi realized.

— Me, Poppy confirmed, her expression as neutral as ever. It's literally my domain.

81 seemed to regain hope all at once.

— Can you find her?

— I can find anyone. It's a question of time, not of possibility.

— How much time? Lucifer asked cautiously.

Poppy seemed to calculate for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on nothing.

— Much less than billions of years. Let's say... a few weeks, if she's really as well hidden as you say.

Isidora, already over her earlier confusion, put her phone away with a satisfied smile.

— Oh cool then. Okay, in the meantime, are we still going to the spa? I've never tried a clay mask.

— ISIDORA.

81, noticing Isidora sprawled on a public bench, one arm dangling in the air, a position clearly unworthy of a Witch of the Void, couldn't help but comment.

— Damn, Isidora, why are you sleeping on a bench like a hobo?

— ...

— Shut the fuck up, she grumbled without even opening her eyes, I barely wake up and I see your ugly mugs. Speaking of which...

She sat up abruptly, rummaging in a pocket that probably hadn't existed a second earlier, pulling out a crumpled paper bag that she handed straight to 81.

— Put this paper bag on Lulu's head.

— ...

81, without asking a single question, took the bag and calmly walked over to Lucifer, who was watching the scene with growing suspicion.

— No, Lucifer began.

— Isidora said so.

— That's not a reason.

— It's always a reason, 81 replied, unfazed, holding out the bag.

Lucifer looked at the bag, then at Isidora, still half asleep on her bench, then at the bag again.

— ...Why.

— 'Cause your face tires me out in the morning, Isidora answered from her bench, eyes still half-closed.

— It's 2 p.m.

— It's my morning, I do what I want.

Lucifer sighed deeply, that now-familiar weariness running through his whole being — then, without any further resistance, he took the bag and put it over his own head, pulling it down to his shoulders.

— ...

Silence fell again, broken only by the sheer incongruity of seeing the King of Hell standing there, a paper bag on his head, in some random street.

— There, Lucifer said from inside the bag, his voice muffled, heavy with total resignation. Done.

Takeshi, who had been watching from the start, put a hand to his face.

— He actually did it.

— He always does what she asks, 81 commented, almost fascinated by the phenomenon. I still haven't figured out why.

Agent 47, unfazed, merely added a line to his mental report.

— Riper. Additional note.

"Already taking notes."

Poppy, arriving at that exact moment, stopped dead when she spotted Lucifer, paper bag still firmly on his head, standing in the middle of everyone as if nothing were amiss.

— ...

— I have information on the location of the Incarnation of Death, she finally announced, visibly choosing to ignore the scene completely.

— Why is Lucifer wearing a bag, she asked anyway, unable to ignore it entirely.

— Isidora asked, 81 simply answered, as if that explained absolutely everything.

— ...Works for me, Poppy concluded, as if it did indeed explain everything.

Lucifer, still under his bag, vaguely raised a hand.

— I'm still here, in case anyone's wondering.

— Nobody's wondering, Isidora replied, finally fully awake, getting up from her bench with a stretch. Okay, Poppy, where'd you find that bitch Death?

Poppy stepped forward, her expression as neutral as ever despite the information she was about to deliver.

— I found her. She's on Earth. On KJ's side.

— ...

81 frowned.

— On Earth? After millennia hiding in God knows what dimension, she's just... on Earth?

— Exactly. In a bar. In Colombia.

A new stunned silence settled in, this time tinged with an almost predictable weariness, given how many absurd revelations of this kind the day had already piled up.

Takeshi put a hand to his forehead.

— Another totally normal place for a cosmic entity.

— After the Berlin spa, I'm not really surprised anymore, Lucifer added, still under his paper bag, his voice muffled but resigned.

Isidora, for her part, already seemed thrilled.

— A bar? In Colombia? What do they do there, rum? I'm so down.

— We're supposed to confront her for a cosmic revenge, not go on a booze tour, 81 reminded her, even though his own determination seemed to waver slightly at the news.

— Can't we do both? Isidora asked, almost sincerely surprised that it was a problem.

Agent 47, pragmatic as ever, spoke up again.

— The fact that she's within KJ's sphere of influence poses a logistical problem. Any intervention in that zone risks drawing unwanted attention.

— The Sect, Poppy clarified. Or worse, an Incarnation.

81 clenched his fists, visibly thinking back to his earlier confrontation with Justice Man, Kang and Aravos — then, more recently, the Assimilated.

— We'll handle it. We've handled worse.

— We literally almost died against the Assimilated, Takeshi reminded him.

— Minor detail, 81 cut in.

Lucifer, still under his bag, raised a hesitant hand.

— Question. Can I take the bag off now, or is it still ongoing?

— Still ongoing, Isidora answered immediately, without even thinking.

— ...Okay, he sighed, resigned, his hand dropping back down.

Poppy watched the exchange, her face still perfectly impassive, before continuing.

— When do we leave for Colombia?

— After the rum, Isidora decreed.

— BEFORE the rum, 81 corrected firmly.

— We'll see when we get there, Isidora settled it, already walking off in what vaguely looked like a random direction. Come on, let's move!

The group set off for Colombia, a crossing made easier by a dimensional rift Isidora had opened with an absent-minded wave, barely focused on the task, busy as she was already digging through her cloak.

— Ah, there it is.

She pulled out a ten-liter bottle of rum, held in one hand as if its weight simply didn't exist, the label half worn away by time.

— ...Where'd you get that, Takeshi asked, staring at the bottle with a disbelief that didn't even really surprise him anymore.

— From my cloak. It's to get myself ready.

— Ready for what exactly, 81 asked, one eyebrow raised.

— To face Death, obviously. You gotta be relaxed for this kind of showdown.

She unscrewed the cap and put the neck straight to her mouth, chugging the rum without the slightest pause, the liquid disappearing at a speed that defied all physical logic.

— ...

81 watched the scene for a few seconds, then turned to Takeshi with a jaded expression.

— She's just an alcoholic. Don't overthink it.

— IT'S CALLED MENTAL PREPARATION, Isidora yelled, bottle still half raised, a trickle of rum running down her chin.

— You drank two liters in five seconds.

— THEN I'VE GOT A LOT OF PREPARING TO DO!

Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, walked silently beside the group, his muffled voice rising timidly.

— Question. Still ongoing, the bag?

— STILL ONGOING, Isidora confirmed without even looking at him, going straight into another monumental gulp.

— ...Okay, he sighed, with a resignation that was now almost philosophical.

Poppy, walking at the front, led the way without turning around, her tracking sense guiding her straight to the Colombian bar without the slightest hesitation.

— We're getting close.

Agent 47, still on alert despite the general mood, glanced at Isidora, the bottle already half empty despite the few seconds that had passed since she opened it.

— Riper. Calculate her theoretical blood alcohol level if she were human.

"Calculating... incompatible with human survival. Three times over."

— She isn't human, 47 reminded himself, almost under his breath.

"Lucky for her."

81, as jaded as ever, shook his head watching Isidora keep drinking while walking, weaving slightly without it seeming to affect her coordination in the least.

— Honestly, at some point, we should maybe worry about her.

— I've known her long enough, Lucifer answered from his bag, we've stopped worrying. Now we just endure.

The group kept moving, Isidora calmly finishing her ten-liter bottle as if it were nothing, Lucifer still wearing his paper bag, and Poppy leading them straight to their next cosmic confrontation in a remote Colombian bar.

Isidora, barely done with the first bottle, plunged her hand straight back into her cloak, pulling out six more bottles of rum, all the same size, which she casually stacked in her arms like ordinary groceries.

— ...

Agent 47, who had been following the scene from the start with clinical detachment, stayed silent for a moment, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Riper, analysis status.

"Analysis complete."

A pause, longer than usual.

"Isidora, listen. I think if there were an Incarnation of Alcohol, you could take its place, you're that superior. I just dug through my archives and calculated that you've literally already eaten 30 bars in the same second. And when I say eaten, I mean literally. The walls, the floor, the bottles, the customers, etc."

— ...

Isidora, in the middle of opening a new bottle, stopped dead, a huge smile spreading across her face.

— See! Finally someone who recognizes my talent!

— That's not supposed to be a compliment, 81 cut in, staring at Reaper — or rather at 47's earpiece — with growing disbelief.

"It was neutral. Purely factual.", Reaper specified.

— Well, I'm taking it as a compliment, Isidora decided, bringing the new bottle straight to her mouth.

Takeshi, who was seriously starting to lose count of the day's absurdities, turned to 47.

— Wait, 30 bars. In the same second. How is that possible.

— Riper analyzes archived data from multiple realities and timelines, 47 explained, unfazed. Isidora appears in several simultaneous occurrences across different dimensional layers.

— ...So there are several Isidoras existing at the same time, Lucifer realized from inside his paper bag, his voice betraying a brand-new horror.

"Confirmed."

— HOLY SHIT, HOW MANY OF YOU ARE THERE, Takeshi exclaimed, panic clearly rising in his voice.

— Dunno, Isidora answered with a completely carefree shrug, taking another swig. Never really counted.

Poppy, still at the head of the group, stopped briefly to turn around, her neutral expression slightly more pronounced than usual.

— That is officially the most terrifying piece of information I've heard today. And I watched the Assimilated get humiliated by a hungry fist.

— THANK YOU! Isidora exclaimed, taking the remark as yet another compliment, utterly indifferent to the growing concern around her.

81, slowly shaking his head, resumed his march toward the Colombian bar, visibly determined to stop trying to understand.

— We keep moving. The sooner we find Death, the sooner I can pretend this conversation never happened.

Reaper spoke up again, his synthesized voice once more ringing in 47's earpiece.

"Correction. Isidora is lying to you."

— ...

Isidora stopped dead, bottle halfway to her mouth, a nervous smile floating on her face.

— What are you talking about, I've never lied in my life.

"She killed all her clones so they wouldn't overtake her in followers. So she is the only Isidora in all realities. And she alone ate the 30 bars. Not her doubles."

An absolute silence fell over the group.

"Just putting that out there. Do what you want with it."

— ...

Takeshi slowly brought a hand to his face, unable to find anything at all to add.

— She killed her own clones. For views.

— It was a matter of principle, Isidora defended herself, not embarrassed in the slightest. There wasn't room for two of me on the social media market.

81 slowly shook his head, a mix of exasperation and morbid fascination crossing his face.

— She's so far gone that even the AI can't stand her anymore.

"Confirmed.", Reaper added immediately, without the slightest hesitation.

— HEY, Isidora exclaimed, offended for the first time all day. Need I remind you I congratulated you earlier!

"And I already regret it."

Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, let out a muffled laugh.

— Honestly, at this level, it's almost impressive.

— IT IS IMPRESSIVE, Isidora confirmed, instantly regaining her confidence, completely ignoring the latent horror of the revelation. I literally ate 30 bars all by myself, no help, no cheating. That's pure talent.

Poppy, still in the lead, merely shook her head slightly, resuming her walk toward the Colombian bar without further comment.

— We keep going. Before she eats something else.

— Good idea, 81 agreed, picking up the pace.

47, bringing up the rear, cast one last glance at Isidora, still calmly drinking as if the information about the mass murder of her own doubles were just one detail among many.

— Riper. Add that to the file.

"The file is starting to look more like a psychiatric report than an intelligence profile."

— Note it anyway.

"Already done."

Takeshi had been walking in silence for a few moments, staring at Isidora with an expression wavering between total disbelief and the beginnings of existential fatigue.

— ...

— You okay, Takeshi? Lucifer asked, noticing his unusual silence despite the bag still firmly on his head.

— No. No, I'm not okay.

— What exactly is wrong, 81 asked, still walking toward the bar.

Takeshi vaguely gestured at Isidora, still knocking back her bottle as if it were nothing, then at 47's earpiece, from which Reaper kept muttering disillusioned remarks in the background.

— That. All of that. Her. She's my aunt. She's literally my aunt.

— So what? Isidora asked, apparently not bothered by the remark.

— So you're so weird that an artificial intelligence that's supposed to be purely cold and logical literally created emotions for itself just so it could comment on you properly.

— ...

A silence settled in, everyone seeming to realize just how perfectly that sentence, once spoken out loud, summed up the scale of the situation.

"He is not wrong.", Reaper commented, almost pensive.

— Even you confirm it, Takeshi breathed, desperate.

"I had no programmed emotional inflection before today. I had to develop a real-time capacity for dismay simply to keep functioning properly in Isidora's presence."

— SEE! Takeshi exclaimed, turning to the group. I'm not the one exaggerating, a cosmic AI confirms it!

81 shrugged, seeming almost used to it by now.

— Welcome to the family, Takeshi. You learn to live with it.

— How do you guys do it, seriously.

— We endure, Lucifer simply answered from his paper bag. Like I said earlier. We've stopped trying to understand, now we just endure.

Isidora, utterly indifferent to the existential debate unfolding around her, finished her bottle in one last gulp before tossing it carelessly over her shoulder, without turning around to see where it landed.

— Okay, are we still far from this bar or what?

Poppy, at the front, answered without even turning around.

— Two minutes.

— PERFECT, I've got time for one last one before we get there.

Takeshi closed his eyes, breathing deeply, visibly trying to find some kind of inner peace in the face of the total absurdity of his new family life.

— ...I don't regret dying and going to Hell. It's important that's said. But sometimes I wonder if I really came out ahead.

The group walked through the door of the bar, but for once, nobody even looked up at them — not a customer, not a waiter, as if their presence was of absolutely no importance compared to what already held the whole room's attention.

— ...

At the back of the bar, sitting alone, was the Incarnation of Death.

A hooded silhouette, draped entirely in black, two immense dark wings spread out on its back, almost brushing the low ceiling of the establishment. A sword rested against its shoulder, the blade tinted a deep red. Its face remained invisible, hidden in the shadow of its hood.

Around it, empty bottles of vodka and rum were piled up by the thousands, some columns literally reaching the ceiling, the whole thing forming a true landscape of glass in an almost religious silence.

81 stopped dead, staring at the scene.

— ...That's her.

Isidora, her own bottle still in hand, eyed the stacks of empty glass with undisguised admiration.

— Okay, her, I like her already.

Takeshi stood frozen, throat dry, his eyes unable to tear away from the motionless silhouette at the back of the room.

— ...She's scary.

— Of course, Lucifer answered from his paper bag, his voice suddenly more serious than it had been in hours. She's literally the concept of death.

Poppy remained perfectly neutral, her gaze simply analyzing the silhouette with the same coldness she applied to any target.

— Confirmed. That's her.

Agent 47 discreetly moved his hand toward his weapon, without drawing it, his earpiece crackling.

— Riper. Threat analysis.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause, longer than usual.

"...I recommend extreme caution."

81 slowly took a step forward, his hand instinctively tightening on the hilt of his sword, every trace of hesitation gone from his face.

— Let's go.

I had to develop a real-time capacity for dismay simply to keep functioning properly in Isidora's presence." — SEE! Takeshi exclaimed, turning to the group. I'm not the one exaggerating, a cosmic AI confirms it! 81 shrugged, seeming almost used to it by now. — Welcome to the family, Takeshi. You learn to live with it. — How do you guys do it, seriously. — We endure, Lucifer simply answered from his paper bag. Like I said earlier. We've stopped trying to understand, now we just endure. Isidora, utterly indifferent to the existential debate unfolding around her, finished her bottle in one last gulp before tossing it carelessly over her shoulder, without turning around to see where it landed. — Okay, are we still far from this bar or what? Poppy, at the front, answered without even turning around. — Two minutes. — PERFECT, I've got time for one last one before we get there. Takeshi closed his eyes, breathing deeply, visibly trying to find some kind of inner peace in the face of the total absurdity of his new family life. — ...I don't regret dying and going to Hell. It's important that's said. But sometimes I wonder if I really came out ahead. The group walked through the door of the bar, but for once, nobody even looked up at them — not a customer, not a waiter, as if their presence was of absolutely no importance compared to what already held the whole room's attention. — ... At the back of the bar, sitting alone, was the Incarnation of Death. A hooded silhouette, draped entirely in black, two immense dark wings spread out on its back, almost brushing the low ceiling of the establishment. A sword rested against its shoulder, the blade tinted a deep red. Its face remained invisible, hidden in the shadow of its hood. Around it, empty bottles of vodka and rum were piled up by the thousands, some columns literally reaching the ceiling, the whole thing forming a true landscape of glass in an almost religious silence. 81 stopped dead, staring at the scene. — ...That's her. Isidora, her own bottle still in hand, eyed the stacks of empty glass with undisguised admiration. — Okay, her, I like her already. Takeshi stood frozen, throat dry, his eyes unable to tear away from the motionless silhouette at the back of the room. — ...She's scary. — Of course, Lucifer answered from his paper bag, his voice suddenly more serious than it had been in hours. She's literally the concept of death. Poppy remained perfectly neutral, her gaze simply analyzing the silhouette with the same coldness she applied to any target. — Confirmed. That's her. Agent 47 discreetly moved his hand toward his weapon, without drawing it, his earpiece crackling. — Riper. Threat analysis. "Analysis in progress..." A pause, longer than usual. "...I recommend extreme caution." 81 slowly took a step forward, his hand instinctively tightening on the hilt of his sword, every trace of hesitation gone from his face. — Let's go.

qualdi-t1-c1.html:
Bullets whistled down the alley.

Two members of the Chimamire clan were running flat out, a Toride squad right on their heels. A burst of gunfire blew up a jar right next to them.

"Left! Go left!"

They turned, then turned again, and ran straight into a wall. A dead end.

The first one flattened himself against the stone.

"Shit, we're trapped! Give me the gun!"

The second one tossed him his submachine gun.

"Here, take it and spray anything that moves and wants you dead!"

He caught it in midair, dove behind a pile of crates and opened fire just as the Toride soldiers came around the corner. One soldier went down. The others threw themselves into cover.

"Contact! Dead end, ten o'clock!" a voice shouted. "They're cornered!"

The return fire came instantly. The crates exploded into splinters one by one.

"I'm almost out!" the first one yelled.

"I know, I know!"

The second one looked at the wall behind them, then at the mouth of the alley. The soldiers were advancing, covering one another.

"Okay… we're gonna have to improvise."

The shooting started up again, harder than before.

The first one rose behind the crates and emptied his magazine toward the mouth of the alley. A Toride soldier collapsed. Then another.

"Yeah! Come on, you dogs!"

But around the corner, more black helmets appeared. Four. Then six. Then ten.

"How many of them are there, damn it?!"

"Too many! Reload, reload!"

The second one tossed him a magazine. The first one slammed it in, raised the gun to his shoulder…

A bullet hit him square in the chest.

He took one step back and looked at the hole in his leather vest, as if he didn't understand. The gun slipped from his hands.

"No… no, no, no!"

The second one threw himself on him and dragged him behind what was left of the crates. He pressed both hands on the wound. The blood ran between his fingers, warm, far too fast.

"Stay with me! Stay with me, you hear me?!"

The first one opened his mouth. Nothing came out. His eyes stayed fixed on the blue sky of the Anarchy, then stopped moving.

The second one stayed still for a second. Just one.

"Cease fire!" a voice called from the Toride side. "There's one left! We want him alive!"

He picked up his partner's gun, held it tight against him and looked around. The wall behind. The soldiers in front. A broken window, two meters up, off to the side.

"Alive, huh…"

He fired a burst toward the mouth of the alley. The soldiers dove for cover. In the same second, he leapt onto a crate, grabbed the window ledge and hauled himself inside. Shards of glass sliced into his arms.

"He's going through the window! Surround the building!"

He landed in a dark room that smelled of dust and oil. He didn't stop. He crossed the hallway, tore down a staircase, smashed open a door with his shoulder. Behind him, boots were already climbing the stairs.

He ran, lungs on fire, the gun in one hand, the other pressed against his belt.

He could think of only one thing: getting back to Akasuna.

He kicked open a door.

A whole family was sitting at the table. The father, the mother, three kids, bowls of soup in their hands. Every head turned at the same time.

"Sorry!" he shouted as he crossed the room.

He knocked over a chair, jumped over the table and left through the back door. Behind him, the Toride soldiers burst into the kitchen.

"Which way did he go?!"

The father pointed his spoon at the back door, without even getting up.

The fugitive was already in the house next door. He charged down a hallway, turned and fired a blind burst behind him. A vase exploded, a painting fell, and a soldier hit the floor.

"He's shooting! He's shooting!"

"Of course he's shooting, move!"

Another door. Locked. He smashed it open with his shoulder and came face to face with an old man in his underwear, shaving in front of a mirror.

"Oh, is the gunfire for you again?" the old man sighed.

"Sorry, old timer!"

He opened the window, jumped onto the neighboring roof and landed heavily in a courtyard full of drying laundry. The sheets wrapped around him. He thrashed and swore, tore everything off and ran on, a white sheet still hanging from his shoulder.

Bullets rained down from the roof. The clotheslines snapped. A chicken took off screaming.

He turned, raised the gun and fired. The soldier on the roof pulled back into cover.

"He's in the courtyard! Cut off his exit!"

He crossed a carpet shop, knocking over two entire piles. He smashed through the back door, burst out into another alley and felt the magazine click empty.

Out of bullets.

He threw the gun away, pulled the pistol from his belt and started running again. In the distance, above the rooftops, the tall red towers of Akasuna were already in sight.

Three more streets.

Maybe four.

Behind him, the Toride boots weren't slowing down.

He reached the end of the last alley, and the city stopped all at once.

In front of him there was nothing but desert. Red dunes as far as the eye could see, and the sun crushing everything.

He didn't think. He ran.

His boots sank into the sand with every step. The sheet still hanging from his shoulder snapped in the hot wind. Behind him, the Toride soldiers were coming out of the city one after another.

"He's heading into the desert!"

"After him! Don't lose him!"

Five. Ten. Fifteen. Twenty black helmets advancing in a line across the sand, rifles raised.

He turned and fired two pistol rounds. Neither hit anyone. The soldiers didn't even bother to duck.

"Stop!" one of them shouted. "You won't get anywhere! There's nothing in this desert!"

"There's less of you, at least!" he yelled without slowing down.

He scrambled up a dune on all fours, the burning sand under his hands, and half rolled down the other side. He got up, spat out sand and kept going.

His legs were starting to shake. His throat was as dry as the desert itself. The blood from the cuts on his arms had dried into red crusts mixed with dust.

Behind him, the Toride soldiers weren't running. They were walking, at a steady pace, in formation. They didn't need to run.

The desert would end up stopping him for them.

"Come on… come on…" he panted, gripping his pistol. "Akasuna… it's not far… it's not far…"

He looked ahead. The red towers of Akasuna shimmered in the distance through the heat.

They didn't seem to be getting any closer.

He pushed his legs harder. Faster. Even faster.

The sand flew around him. His heart pounded so hard he could hear it in his ears. He wasn't looking back anymore. He was only looking at the red towers.

He didn't hear the footsteps closing in behind him.

A Toride soldier had broken away from the line. Younger, faster than the others, he had left his rifle with a colleague and run with everything he had too.

He leapt.

The impact threw the fugitive face first into the sand. The pistol flew out of his hand and slid a meter away. He thrashed, kicked, tried to turn over, but the soldier crushed his back with a knee and twisted his arm behind him.

"Don't move! Don't move!"

"Get off me! Get off me, you bastard!"

"It's over, buddy. It's over."

A metallic click. The cold of a handcuff around one wrist. Then the other.

The fugitive stopped moving. He lay there, cheek against the burning sand, out of breath, eyes fixed on the red towers of Akasuna.

They were still just as far away.

A second soldier came jogging up, bent down and picked the pistol up from the sand. He looked it over, emptied it and slipped the bullets into his pocket.

"Nice run," he said. "Really. We almost could've let you win."

The other eighteen were coming up behind, in no hurry.

The soldier who had tackled him pulled him up by the collar and forced him onto his knees. The fugitive spat out sand and looked up at them. Twenty black helmets. Twenty rifles. And the sun of the Anarchy above, giving no one any favors.

"So," the soldier said, wiping the sweat under his helmet. "You and me are gonna have a long talk."

The soldier raised a hand to his radio.

"This is unit three. Suspect apprehended. Requesting a vehicle at our position, we…"

He stopped.

At the top of the dune, facing them, silhouettes had just appeared. About ten. Red scarves, leather jackets, weapons in hand. On their armbands, the same drop of blood.

"Contact! Dune, twelve o'clock!"

The twenty Toride rifles rose in a single movement. The clan mercenaries didn't move. They weren't aiming at anyone. They were waiting.

Then, without a word, they stepped aside.

Someone was coming down the dune behind them.

He walked slowly, unhurried, as if the sand didn't bother him. A raised hood hid his face in shadow. A cape of black feathers covered his shoulders, and from his belt hung vials, pouches and a dagger. In his right hand he held a tall staff topped with a red orb that glowed faintly, like a beating heart.

The soldier holding the radio let it drop against his vest.

No one in unit three needed to be told who this was.

The man stopped a few meters from them. He glanced briefly at the prisoner kneeling in the sand, then raised his head toward the soldiers.

"You have no business here, soldier. This is my territory."

His voice was calm. Cold. Without anger.

The soldier in command of the unit took a step forward. His hand trembled slightly on the grip of his rifle, but his voice held.

"Your man stole, wrecked the place and killed a soldier. It would be worrying if we'd let him get away with that, don't you think?"

Crimson didn't answer right away.

The red orb pulsed once. Then a second time.

The soldier felt something strange. A throbbing in his temples, stronger than usual. A heat rising in his veins. Next to him, one of his men raised a hand to his nose. His fingers came back red.

"You will leave my territory," said Crimson, "or I will drain every drop of blood from your miserable carcass."

Silence fell over the desert.

Twenty rifles. About ten mercenaries. A single hooded man.

And yet, in unit three, everyone knew perfectly well which side had the advantage.

The soldier didn't take his eyes off Crimson. Slowly, very slowly, he raised the radio back to his mouth.

"Unit three to the Junta. Critical situation. The leader of the Chimamire clan is on site. I repeat, Crimson is on site. Requesting authorization to… to… Awaiting your orders."

Static.

Nothing.

The seconds stretched on. A drop of sweat ran down under the soldier's helmet. The prisoner, still on his knees, gave a little smile. Crimson didn't move a millimeter.

Then the radio crackled.

"Good day to you, chief of the Bandit Republic."

A deep voice, hoarse, calm. The voice of an old man who had seen too many battlefields to get worked up over the phone.

General Gérard Eldrath himself.

Crimson turned his head slightly toward the radio.

"General Gérard. I don't think you know who you're dealing with."

Behind the unit leader, a young soldier leaned toward the man next to him and whispered:

"The general's gonna send in the army. He won't be laughing then."

His neighbor didn't answer. Blood was still running from his nose.

The radio crackled again.

"Take back your man, Crimson, if you let my soldiers leave."

Total silence.

The young soldier opened his mouth, closed it, then opened it again.

"Wait… what?"

The unit leader turned to him with a look that clearly meant: shut up.

Crimson stood still for a long moment. Then the red orb of his staff stopped pulsing. The soldiers felt the heat leave their veins all at once, like a hand loosening its grip.

"Take off his handcuffs," Crimson said simply.

The soldier who had tackled the fugitive looked at his leader. His leader looked at the radio. The radio said nothing more.

"… Do what he says."

The clink of the handcuffs echoed in the silence of the desert. The prisoner got up rubbing his wrists, scraped a little dignity together from the sand and rejoined the clan mercenaries without looking back.

As he passed the young soldier, he gave him a wink.

"Nice run, huh?"

The Toride vehicle arrived a few minutes later, in a cloud of red dust.

No one spoke while the soldiers climbed aboard. The twenty black helmets crammed into the back, rifles between their knees, without taking their eyes off the dune where the Chimamire clan still stood.

The engine roared. The vehicle turned around and drove off toward the border.

In the back, the young soldier couldn't hold it in anymore.

"I don't get it."

"Shut up," his neighbor muttered, a blood-soaked handkerchief under his nose.

"No, seriously. That's Crimson. The most wanted criminal in the world. He was right there, five meters from us, and the general… he just lets him go? Like that?"

"Did you see what he did to us without even moving? What did you want, for us to shoot him?"

"I don't know! Send in the army! Tanks! A bomb! Anything!"

The unit leader, sitting up front, didn't turn around.

"The general made his decision," he said. "He saved twenty lives today. Period."

The young soldier opened his mouth, then closed it. Through the rear window he watched the clan silhouettes shrinking at the top of the dune.

"Still," he muttered. "It's weird."

No one answered him.

On the dune, Crimson watched the vehicle disappear over the horizon. He stayed still until the sound of the engine had completely died away.

The clan member who had just been freed came over, head down.

"Boss… thank you. I…"

"Your partner is dead."

It wasn't a question. The fugitive lowered his head even further.

"Yes, boss."

Crimson said nothing more. He turned and began to climb back up the dune, staff in hand, his cape of black feathers quivering in the hot wind. The mercenaries followed him without a word.

Behind them, the wind was already erasing the footprints in the sand.
